Glasco-144.remote_wikitext:
== Biography ==

'''Thomas Glascoe''' married [[Duffy-?|Margaret Duffy]], daughter of [[Duffy-?|Patrick Duffy]] and his wife Anne.

An undated handwritten pedigree of the Duffy family identifies Margaret as:

: “Margt, wife of Thomas Glascoe”

Margaret’s father, Patrick Duffy, was associated with Back Lane, Dublin. The pedigree states that Patrick made his will on 9 April 1774 and that it was proved in June 1775.

The pedigree also names Margaret’s siblings as John Duffy, Peter Duffy, Judith Duffy, Mary Duffy, and possibly Teresa Duffy. Judith married Cornelius Blewitt.

No children of Thomas and Margaret are shown on the pedigree. This does not prove that they had no children.

== Research Notes ==

* Thomas’s birth and death dates are unknown.
* His birthplace and residence are not stated.
* His occupation and parentage have not been identified.
* No marriage date or place has yet been found.
* The surname is written as '''Glascoe''' in the pedigree. Searches should also consider variants such as Glasco, Glascow and Glasgow.
* Thomas should not be assigned a Dublin birthplace solely because his father-in-law lived at Back Lane, Dublin.
* Patrick Duffy’s probate record may contain further information about Thomas and Margaret.

Glasgow-1024.summary: Father James-1025, specifically the James/Margaret Rutherford family-account role: James-1024 18%→78%, Samuel-1492 23%→76%, Robert-2425 18%→77%, William-2426 46%→84%, all now probable. The American Robert-12/Arthur-649/Joseph-1543 father grades remain35%, John-4027 remains30%, Mary-4030 remains22%; James-1025’s own William-1026 father remains32%. The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris on p.9 explicitly gives James Glasgow, husband of Margaret Rutherford, four sons: William, Robert, James who settled near Moneymore, and Samuel who went to America, plus daughter Ellen. The letter-defined father is the family role represented by James-1025. These are specific named relationships, substantially stronger than the contributed-tree and locality summaries used by the earlier percentages. The same full-letter tradition was already read on 20 October; actual Faris pages now confirm its full structure. Its reproduction by Albert Rutherford and Faris’s pedigree are dependent presentations, not independent witnesses. James-1024 is reviewed as the letter-defined son who settled near Moneymore. The father James and son James occupy explicitly distinct generations in that account; the earlier possibility that these two family roles were one duplicated adult no longer deserves the same weight. The 78% assessment does not identify the son with the Corvanaghan householder or make him father of the American emigrant Robert. These are probable, not confident, relationships reconstructed from an anonymous retrospective family recollection, with no newly inspected parent register. The original letter remains uninspected. Faris calls the anonymous recollection file5 within PRONI T1959, while Rutherford’s reproduced copy cites T1959/3; retain this reference discrepancy pending archive checking. The 1759 probate index says Drumcarn and names no kin; neither that testator nor the inherited life dates are identified by this reassessment. The letter calls William eldest although the imported sibling birth estimates put him later; those estimates remain unverified. Faris also flags Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in1824 against the supposed early paternal death. Those tensions require testing, not automatic exclusion. Preserve all existing people, vital fields, maternal grades and alternatives. No Scottish migration, identity merge, live edit or new father attachment is claimed.

=== Earlier public research, superseded only as specified above ===

=== Current family assessment, 23 October 2026 ===

The actual Faris book has now been inspected, rather than only its catalogue abstract. Printed p.11 uses a dotted possible connection from James of Moneymore to the American brothers; p.12 explicitly reports that evidence for Robert and his brothers’ parentage had not been found. James was the author’s identifiable County Londonderry candidate, not an evidenced father. The retrospective Irish pedigree on pp.8–9 and Samuel’s 1824 Pennsylvania will discussed on p.12 identify an Irish sibling group, including William, James and Robert remaining in Ireland, without joining it to the emigrant brothers. County setting, a compatible generation and the existing family tradition keep James a plausible candidate, but cannot sustain the earlier probable father assessment. Existing father-profile propositions only: [[Glasgow-12|Robert]] 85% → 35%; [[Glasgow-649|Arthur]] and [[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] each 82% → 35%; [[Glasgow-4027|John]] 76% → 30%; [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] 64% → 22%. All five were probable; the first four are now possible and Mary uncertain. [[Glasgow-1024|James]] remains the selected named candidate; no attachment is removed. [[Glasgow-1024|James]]’s own older father stays 18%, and [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]]’s father stays 23%. Mary’s case additionally depends on identifying the 1779 will witness Mary Arter as the emigrant sister. Faris p.13 transmits an unnamed sister styled Mrs Arthur; p.15 identifies Mary Arter with that sister through the tax/probate cluster, rather than an explicit sibling or birth statement. The association remains positive but does not establish her father. Robert, Arthur and Joseph’s established brotherhood remains separately supported by the maintained 1806 letter transcription and Joseph’s 1831 will. John of Peters Township remains a probable brother at 83%; Faris p.15 also reconstructs the four brothers from the 1779–1780 tax/probate cluster. These sibling arguments do not identify their father. The 1824 Samuel will has been read only through Faris’s excerpt, not its manuscript. The Irish Robert in that will/pedigree is not identified as the emigrant Robert born in 1749. All mothers, upstream ancestry, life dates and current attachments are preserved; no live WikiTree save or identity merge follows. Exact percentages are subjective pair-specific judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied probabilities.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990), printed pp.8–15; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FN-6 pp.10–11], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9FV-S pp.14–15]; FamilySearch film 2055438 Item 5, DGS 007834162, images 1564–1567, visually inspected 23 October 2026. Published genealogy, not newly inspected original wills or letters.</ref>

=== Earlier public research, superseded only for the father grades above ===

=== Peters Township family review,20 October 2026 ===

Extend James of Moneymore’s probable fatherhood to the preferred fourth-brother account John of Peters Township, at 76%; the other three sons remain 85% and James’s own older father remains 18%.

Fendrick’s checked 1944 abstract of the 1779 Peters Township will identifies John Glasgow’s wife Ann, daughters Lates and Agnes, and son Joseph. [[Glasgow-4028|Lates Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-4029|Joseph Glasgow]] are the existing record-defined daughter and son accounts, not speculative later adult identifications. Assess John as their father at 98% each, strongly supported by the explicit abstracted relationship and matching will context. The manuscript has not been inspected, so this does not certify the spelling or completeness of the abstract. Joseph the son is distinct from the adult Joseph who witnessed the will.

Assess James of Moneymore, [[Glasgow-1024|James Glasgow II]], as John of Peters Township’s probable father at 76%. The 2024 Adams County family account specifically identifies the John who died in 1779 as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph. Fendrick’s abstract independently supplies a contemporary Joseph Glasgow witness in John’s Peters Township will; James Neely’s presence also fits the later Neely-associated emigrant family. Faris’s catalogue description identifies Robert’s father as James of Moneymore and reports four emigrant brothers. Together these identify a specific compatible family, rather than only another local James. Extend that probable father across the preferred fourth-brother identification, while rating John lower than the three established brothers because his place in that group depends partly on the later account and witness identification. Assess the John-to-each-established-brother relationship as probable at 83%.

The original will and probate packet remain uninspected. The checked abstract gives 1779, not the execution/probate days; existing 14 March and 3 September date limits are preserved from the earlier cited profile account, not newly verified. The will index verifies John’s locator, Cumberland Will Book C, p.161, but supplies no relatives. Ann is named as wife, not expressly mother of the children; her existing maternal attachments remain unassessed. Nancy (Glascoe) Wright is only a possible identification of Agnes: an approximately 1778 birth fits a child alive in 1779 and Agnes/Nancy can be compatible name forms, but the later Maryland/Indiana household has no inspected parent, guardianship or estate bridge to Peters Township. Her existing John father is therefore possible at 37%, not confident. The witness Joseph is not proved to be Joseph of Wythe County. The family-history article may depend on Faris and is not independent corroboration of his genealogy. The older James-1025 father of James-1024 remains 18%; no Scottish migration, Mary Harkness maternity, new mother, identity merge or live edit follows. Exact percentages express individual subjective judgments, not measured frequencies or multiplied independent probabilities.<ref>[https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdclccn/57/05/15/50/57051550/57051550.pdf#page=88 Virginia Shannon Fendrick, American Revolutionary Soldiers of Franklin County, Pennsylvania (1944), printed p.88, PDF p.88, Joseph Glassgo entry; page visually checked 20 October 2026]; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm Cumberland will-book index: John Glasgow, C161; checked 20 October 2026]; [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ Joyce Wilson, Our Ancestors of Adams County,29March2024; secondary account checked 20 October 2026]. The 1944 abstract, not the original will, was inspected.</ref>

=== Possible James Glasco of Omagh ===
The 1786 marriage column names James Glasco, Omagh publican aged 61, and Jane Murray of the same place aged 16.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050075355/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1786-09-05, p.3].</ref>

Three 1793 Hope advertisements name James Glasco, Omagh, as a freight/passage contact; the 25 May issue adds a sailing delay.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021067/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-11, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021086/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-18, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021100/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-25, p.1].</ref>

The marriage was reported by 5 September 1786; the exact ceremony day is not given. James’s reported age suggests birth about 1724–1725. The same uncommon name and Omagh business context support, without proving, continuity with the 1793 contact. The notices do not name his parents or establish a previous marriage.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1024]]. Estimated birth c.1722 and Moneymore context are compatible; neither identifies the Omagh publican.

=== Possible James Glascow, Fogs Manor postal addressee ===
James Glascow, Fogs Manor, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39395391/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1757-04-07, p.1].</ref>

Fogs Manor is the printed address qualifier. A neighbouring "Phil. Co." in a separate alphabetic column is not this man’s address. The list states no occupation, so it does not identify him as the later Greenwich Packet master.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1024]]. Estimated c.1722 birth is chronologically plausible; death date absent. Irish location is not a concrete contradiction. The postal record states no occupation.

=== Possible James Glascow, master of Greenwich Packet ===
Greenwich Packet: James Glascow, master; James Young, owner; from Philadelphia to Winyew, Carolina; with rum, bread, flour and porter.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/34421452/ The Public Advertiser, 1777-05-14, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/396765804/ The Ipswich Journal, 1777-05-17, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971522063/ The Gloucester Journal, 1777-05-19, p.1].</ref>

James Young is the separate vessel owner, not another form of the master’s name. Three issues repeat one voyage report. Neither the route nor the cargo establishes the master’s family or identifies him with the 1757 Fogs Manor addressee.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1024]]. Estimated c.1722 birth is chronologically plausible; death date absent. Irish location is not a concrete contradiction.

=== Possible James Glasgow, Edinburgh game certificate, 1789 ===
James Glasgow, Esq., Edinburgh, appears in the Mid-Lothian game-duty list of certificates issued since 8 September 1789.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601822968/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1789-12-11, p.8].</ref>

The list gives an Edinburgh designation but no age or relatives; it is not evidence of a military or maritime career.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1024]]. Birth c.1722, estimated, County Londonderry; death date not recorded. Chronologically possible, but no Edinburgh/certificate connection is documented.

The American [[Glasgow-12|Robert]]/[[Glasgow-649|Arthur]]/[[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] father grades remain35%, [[Glasgow-4027|John]] remains30%, [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] remains22%; [[Glasgow-1025|James]]’s own [[Glasgow-1026|William]] father remains32%. The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris on p.9 explicitly gives James Glasgow, husband of Margaret Rutherford, four sons: William, Robert, James who settled near Moneymore, and Samuel who went to America, plus daughter Ellen. The letter-defined father is the family role represented by [[Glasgow-1025|James]]. These are specific named relationships, substantially stronger than the contributed-tree and locality summaries used by the earlier percentages. The same full-letter tradition was already read on 20 October; actual Faris pages now confirm its full structure. Its reproduction by Albert Rutherford and Faris’s pedigree are dependent presentations, not independent witnesses. The source links the named family roles; it does not identify this [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel]] with the testator or replace his existing John father. These are probable, not confident, relationships reconstructed from an anonymous retrospective family recollection, with no newly inspected parent register. The original letter remains uninspected. Faris calls the anonymous recollection file5 within PRONI T1959, while Rutherford’s reproduced copy cites T1959/3; retain this reference discrepancy pending archive checking. The 1759 probate index says Drumcarn and names no kin; neither that testator nor the inherited life dates are identified by this reassessment. The letter calls William eldest although the imported sibling birth estimates put him later; those estimates remain unverified. Faris also flags Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in1824 against the supposed early paternal death. Those tensions require testing, not automatic exclusion. Preserve all existing people, vital fields, maternal grades and alternatives. No Scottish migration, identity merge, live edit or new father attachment is claimed.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio(1990), printed pp.8–12; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-J pp.8–9], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], DGS007834162, images1564–1566. === Earlier public research, superseded only as specified above ===

=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. Glasgow-1027.remote_wikitext:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}} == Biography == === Parentage and early life === '''Robert Glasgow''' was born probably in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland. His current estimated birth year of about 1583 is uncertain. He was the son of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]]. His parentage is supported by two independent testamentary records: * Jonet Meik’s 1607 testament identifies Robert as her son. * Ninian Glasgow’s 1613 testament independently identifies Robert as his son.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/5, testament of Jonet Meik, 1607, identifying Robert as her son; and CC9/7/9, testament of Ninian Glasgow, 1613, independently identifying Robert as his son. Transcriptions are recorded on the associated WikiTree profiles. Robert was an adult by 1613, when he was named as executor in his father’s testament. No baptismal record for Robert has yet been identified, so neither the current estimate of about 1583 nor the earlier estimate of about 1575 should be treated as exact. === Cordiner, burgess and guild brother === The 1613 Glasgow burgess roll records a '''Robert Glasgow, cordiner''', who was admitted as a burgess and guild brother as heir of a burgess.James R. Anderson, editor, ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (Glasgow, 1925), entry for Robert Glasgow, cordiner, in the 1613 roll. A cordiner worked in leather, commonly as a shoemaker. The timing, name and civic status make this man a strong match for Ninian Glasgow’s testament-proved son Robert. The burgess entry itself does not name the previous burgess from whom Robert inherited his entitlement, so the identification should be described as '''highly probable''' rather than independently proved by that record. His admission establishes that the matching Robert held recognised status within the Glasgow burgh community. === Marriage === Robert was associated with '''Jonet Conynghame''', whose surname also appears as '''Cunningham'''. Glasgow parish records name Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame or Cunningham as parents of several children baptised between 1614 and 1627. The Scotland's People marriage index records Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame at Glasgow on 6 April 1613.Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 230/10, Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame, 6 April 1613. This was sixteen days before the 22 April 1613 burgess admission of Robert Glasgow, cordiner, and further supports—but does not by itself prove—the identification of the husband with that cordiner. === Children === Glasgow Old Parish Register entries attribute the following children to Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame: * [[Glasgow-1079|Ninian Glasgow]], recorded 6 January 1614 * [[Glasgow-1080|Jonat Glasgow]], daughter, recorded 18 May 1615 * [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabethe Glasgow]], recorded 15 December 1616 * [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised 17 November 1618 * [[Glasgow-1092|Bessie Glasgow]], recorded 24 January 1623 * [[Glasgow-1517|Elizabeth Glasgow]], recorded 24 August 1625 * [[Glasgow-1490|Catherine Glasgow]], recorded 2 October 1627 The 1618 entry records:
Robert lawful sone to Robert Glasgow & Jonet Conynghame - Godf: John & George Glasgowis.
This directly supports [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] as their son.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow High Kirk Old Parish Register 644/1, reported reference 10/272, baptism of Robert Glasgow, 17 November 1618; transcription: "Robert lawful sone to Robert Glasgow & Jonet Conynghame - Godf: John & George Glasgowis." The later Elizabeth may have been named after the older Elizabethe if the first child had died, but that interpretation has not been confirmed by a burial record or another contemporary source. === George and John Glasgow === John Glasgow and George Glasgow appear as witnesses or sponsors in the 1618 baptism of Robert’s son. [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]] also appears in records associated with other members of the family. The repeated association suggests that he was a close relative of Robert, possibly a brother or cousin. No cited record presently states their exact relationship. George should therefore not be attached or described as Robert’s certain brother without further evidence. === Later life === No precise death date or place has been established for Robert. His documented association with Glasgow as a cordiner, burgess, guild brother and parent places him there during the early seventeenth century. Later same-name records must be assessed individually rather than assumed to concern this Robert. == Research Notes == === Birth year === Robert’s birth date is not known. Two estimates have been proposed: * about 1575, based on the assumption that he was already a mature adult when acting as executor in 1613 * about 1583, the estimate currently used on the profile The testament establishes only that Robert was old enough to act as executor in 1613. It does not supply his age or birth year. The birth date should remain uncertain. === Parentage === Robert’s parentage is directly supported by testamentary evidence. Jonet Meik’s 1607 testament calls Robert her son. Ninian Glasgow’s 1613 testament independently calls him his son. The relationships to [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]] may therefore be marked certain. === Identification with the 1613 cordiner === The 1613 burgess roll identifies a Robert Glasgow as a cordiner who was admitted burgess and guild brother as heir of a burgess. This is probably Ninian Glasgow’s son because: * the name and location agree * the entry occurs in the year of Ninian’s testament * Robert was already an adult and executor * admission as heir of a burgess is compatible with succession within an established Glasgow family The roll does not explicitly name Ninian as the preceding burgess. The cordiner identification is therefore highly probable, while the testamentary parentage remains the direct proof. === The November 1645 James === The original Glasgow parish register records [[Glasgow-3971|James Glasgow]] on 25 November 1645 as the son of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunynghame, with James Cunynghame and Johne Muir named as godfathers.Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/56, James Glasgow, male, 25 November 1645, parents indexed as “Rot. Glasgow/Jonet Cunnyngham”. Original register image inspected 31 August 2026; it names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers but gives no occupation, residence, age, birthplace or parentage for Robert. See also [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK FamilySearch record VQHK-VMK], a derivative index. That entry falls about thirty-one years after the first children attributed to this couple and about twenty-seven years after their son Robert’s baptism. One couple having children across this entire period is biologically possible, but the same names in different generations, a transcription problem or a child placed one generation too high are at least as plausible. The best current reconstruction places [[Glasgow-3971|the Scottish James]] as the recorded son of a Robert Glasgow and the younger [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]]. [[Glasgow-1078|Robert baptised in 1618]] is a possible father, not a proved identification. Under that model, the older Robert and Jonet on this profile were James’s possible grandparents. The Scottish child must also remain separate from [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]], whose identity with him is unproved. James should therefore remain outside this older couple’s biographical child list. The original 1645 image has now been examined: its two godfathers create a useful Cunynghame–Muir research cluster, but it supplies no detail identifying the father as either this older Robert or his son baptised in 1618. === Duplicate given names === The records presently attributed to this family include Elizabethe in 1616 and Elizabeth in 1625. Repeated use of the same name often indicates that the older child had died, but it can also result from mistranscription, duplicate indexing or two different couples. The original entries should be reviewed before drawing a firm conclusion. === Later descendants === Claims connecting Robert to [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow]], Alexander Glasgow or Sir Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan require documented parent-to-child evidence through every intervening generation. Surname recurrence, naming patterns and unsourced online trees are not sufficient proof of descent. === Further research === Useful next records include: * The original 1613 burgess-roll entry and related admission records * Original baptism entries for each proposed child * Records identifying the 1645 godfathers James Cunynghame and Johne Muir and their relationship, if any, to this household * Burgh court, guild, trade-incorporation and burgess records concerning Robert the cordiner * Records identifying John and George Glasgow’s relationships to Robert * Probate, property or burial records distinguishing different men named Robert Glasgow == Sources == * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/5, testament of Jonet Meik, 1607. * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, testament of Ninian Glasgow, 1613. * James R. Anderson, editor, ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (1925), 1613 roll. * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow High Kirk Old Parish Register 644/1, reported reference 10/272, baptism of Robert Glasgow, 17 November 1618. * Glasgow Old Parish Register entries attributed to children of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame or Cunningham.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' is recorded as born or baptised on 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder, Midlothian, with James Glasgow and Agnes Adamson attached as his parents. The older profile cited only “Old Parish Records” for this event; the original entry and the precise birth/baptism distinction remain to be checked. The supplied NRS index names James Glasgow as father (Mid Calder OPR 694/10/28), supporting a confident father relationship for this record-defined child; the later adult-identity comparisons remain provisional.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Mid Calder, John Glasgow, 18 February 1616, father James Glasgow, parish 694, reference 10/28; supplied Scotland’s People index, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ repository].</ref>

A John Glasgow and [[Patoune-11|Helen Patoune]] were named as parents of [[Glasgow-3014|John Glasgow]], recorded on 11 January 1638 at Duddingston, Midlothian.<ref>Duddingston Old Parish Register, parish 684, reference FR38, “JOHNE GLASGOW/HELENE PATOUNE,” entry for Johne, 11 January 1638; citation carried from the former Glasgow-3015 profile. The original page has not been compared with this index wording.</ref>

Later entries name a John Glasgow with [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] as parents of [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell Glasgow]], recorded on 4 April 1643 in Edinburgh parish,<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD entry for Issobell Glasgow, 1643], naming John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; cited on the child's profile.</ref> and [[Glasgow-1439|Anne Glasgow]], recorded on 20 June 1652 at Kirknewton and East Calder. The latter child's profile cites a [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 FamilySearch tree] rather than an inspected register entry, so its details remain to be verified.

[[Glasgow-3107|James Glasgow]] is also attached as a son. His own profile documents a 1663 marriage at Polwarth but says his parentage remains unconfirmed; that attachment must not be read as an established child of this John.

== Research Notes ==

The former Glasgow-3015 profile and this profile were combined as the leading identification. The 1638 Duddingston father and the father of the 1643 and 1652 children share a name, generation and neighbouring Midlothian parishes; there is no recorded overlap in the two maternal child sequences. No death of Helen Patoune, marriage to Issobell Porteous or continuous identifier has yet been found, so identifying both fathers as one man and inferring a second union remain provisional. The earlier profile's approximate 1618 birth was an adult-status estimate, not a separate birth record.

== Biography ==
'''Robert Glasgow''' was a farmer and Presbyterian church elder at Kilwaughter, County Antrim. A derivative chronology reports his November 1729 marriage to Rachel Wilson and the births of James, Ann and Rachel.<ref name="KilwaughterChronology">Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html “Chronology of the Glasgow Family”], archived 24 November 2010, derived from PRONI MIC/1B/6.</ref> Registry memorial 74015 independently identifies Rachel, formerly Wilson, as Robert's wife in 1738.<ref name="Mem74015">[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=74015 Registry of Deeds memorial 74015], vol. 105, p. 301, 13 February 1738, derivative memorial transcription.</ref> An 1817 equity complaint says Rachel died in 1742 leaving James and Ann, and Robert's grandson later called Rachel his paternal grandmother and Ann his father's sister.<ref name="EquityComplaint">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124220018id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_Complaint.html 1817 equity complaint transcription].</ref><ref name="EquityReply">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://www.lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Paper_Reply.html Robert Glasgow's sworn answer transcription].</ref> These sources strongly support Robert's nuclear family. No inspected record identifies his father.

=== Original lease names his son, 1764 ===

On 20 December 1764 Robert Glasgow of Ballykeel, parish of Kilwaughter, gentleman, leased to [[Shannon-4518|Hugh Shannon]] of the same parish half the lower Ballykeel farm, estimated at 31½ acres. The measuring lives explicitly include Robert the grantor and “Jas Glasgow son of the sd Robt”. This is direct contemporary evidence for a son James, identified with [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]] by the combined Ballykeel, church and Wilson-estate evidence. The third life, Elinor Jones otherwise Agnew, is called William Agnew’s daughter; she is not a member of Robert’s household.<ref name="Ballykeel1764">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159661, lease dated 20 December 1764, registered 18 April 1766, pp. 415–416; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-33Q6-L FamilySearch image 542] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-33QZ-Y image 543], original manuscript images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The lease does not name Robert’s father or call Hugh Shannon his son-in-law. It independently strengthens the Robert–James connection without proving the older attached ancestry. James Shutter’s affidavit of execution was sworn at Carrickfergus on 29 March 1766.

=== Timeline of Relevant Events (Kilwaughter/Larne Context) ===

* '''c. 1710:''' Approximate, uncertain birth year. The attached [[Glasgow-1502|older Robert Glasgow]], and the proposed siblings [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh]] and [[Glasgow-1504|James]], remain unproved relationships.
* '''1722:''' A James Glasgow (possibly [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow (abt.1650-1726)]] or [[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow (abt.1707-)]]?) served as one of six Commissioners to the Presbytery.
* '''1724:''' Patrick Agnew of Kilwaughter Castle died.
* '''1726:''' Death recorded for James Glasgow (likely the elder [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow (abt.1650-1726)]]).
* '''1727:''' Will of James Glasgow of Kilwater (likely [[Glasgow-1081]]) proved.
* '''1727 (Aug 5):''' A James Glasgow (possibly [[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow (abt.1707-)]]?) married Sara Muray [[Muray-101|Sara Muray?]] in the Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church. Their known children included:
** Jean (b. 1728)
** William ("Will") (b. 1730)
** Hellen (b. 1732)
** Christian (b. 1740)
* '''1729:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' married Rachel Willson [[Willson-888|Rachel Willson?]] in the Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church.
* '''1731:''' Baptism of '''[[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]]''', son of [[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]] and Rachel Willson, Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church.
* '''1731:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' became a Church Elder in Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church.
* '''1731:''' Baptism of Jean Glasgow, daughter of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], recorded in New Town (Larne).
* '''1733:''' Baptism of '''[[Glasgow-1500|Ann Taggard Glasgow]]''', daughter of [[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]] and Rachel Wilson, Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church.
* '''1735:''' Baptism of Rose Glasgow, daughter of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], of New Town, Larne.
* '''1736:''' Baptism of Mary Glasgow, daughter of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], of New Town, Larne.
* '''1737:''' Birth of James Glasgow, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], New Town, Larne. (Likely [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow (1737–1802)]], wife Janet Shutter, per St. Cedma's tombstone).
* '''1738:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' leased land from William Agnew in Kilwaughter Parish.
* '''1738:''' Baptism of '''[[Glasgow-1501|Rachel Glasgow]]''', daughter of [[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]] and Rachel Wilson, Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church.
* '''1739:''' A John Glasgow ("John2" distinct from John b.c1650) captained the Ship Abigail of Belfast. (Port-News article in Belfast News Letter).
* '''1740:''' Year of the "Great Frost" causing famine and emigration.
* '''1741:''' [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] made elder of the Larne/Kilwaughter Presbyterian Church.
* '''1741:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' witnessed a deed registered in Dublin (Vol 109, p 476, No 76724) involving land in Larne parish leased by Rev Josias Clugston from William Agnew. Robert is described as a farmer of Kilwaughter.
* '''1742:''' Death of Rachel Willson [[Willson-888|Rachel Willson?]], wife of '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]'''. Possible causes include childbirth or widespread sickness following the Great Frost.
* '''1743:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''', as senior elder, attended meeting of the Presbytery in Belfast and several similar meetings.
* '''1744:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' became church treasurer of Larne/Kilwaughter Presbyterian Church.
* '''1745:''' Birth of Hugh Glasgow ("Hugh3"), son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]. Died age 11 (1745–1756).
* '''1747:''' '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' was brought before the church session for the sin of fornication. Refusing public confession, he was turned out of the Kilwaughter/Larne Presbyterian Church. The session account names no woman or child and does not establish the parentage of [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]].
* '''1772 (1 April):''' An archived source note for PRONI T808/15082 places Robert Glasgow, James Glasgow and Hugh Shannon consecutively under Kilwaughter Parish. John Glasgow appears separately under Larne Parish. The grouping supports association among the Kilwaughter men but the petition itself states no kinship; it does not identify [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] as Robert's son. The 7 April date belongs to newspaper publication, not the petition.<ref name="Petition1772">Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184109/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/sources.html archived source notes], citing PRONI T808/15082 and the ''Belfast News-Letter'', 7 April 1772.</ref>
* '''1772 (Late) / 1773:''' '''[[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]]''' (son of [[Glasgow-1143|Robert]] and Rachel Willson), and his wife Mary (speculated Crozier), immigrated to Craven County, South Carolina. Earliest documented date for James in SC is Nov 16, 1774.

=== 1772 petition: evidential limit ===

The Kilwaughter grouping supports the identification of Robert and his proved or strongly supported family associates [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]] and Hugh Shannon. Because John Glasgow was listed under Larne and the petition supplies no relationships, it cannot prove that [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] was Robert's son.<ref name="Petition1772" />

=== Original deed checks, 1738–1743 ===
The original continuation of memorial 74015, a lease dated 13 February 1738, names Robert Glasgow, [[Glasgow-1144|Jas Glasgow junior]] and [[Willson-888|Rachel Glasgow otherwise Wilson]], explicitly described as Robert's wife. The association of James with the linked profile draws on the combined church and later deed evidence, including the explicit 1764 son clause; this 1738 instrument alone does not establish that parentage. The holding comprised 63 acres of Lower Ballykeel and 15 acres of Upper Ballykeel. Patrick Taylor proved execution at Carrickfergus on 12 April 1742. This confirms the wife clause previously known through an abstract; "junior" is not an explicit son clause, and the renewal wording abbreviates "person and persons", not sons. Robert's father is not named.<ref>Registry of Deeds, memorial 74015, pp. 301–302; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-B9MS opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-B99B continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

Memorial 76724 records William Agnew's lease to Rev. Josias Clugston of 45 acres of Ballyboly in Larne parish, dated 17 June 1741. Pat Crawford of Ballysavage and Robert Glasgow of Kilwaughter, farmer, witnessed it; Robert proved execution at Belfast on 21 April 1743, and registration followed on 13 June 1743. The manuscript year is 1743, not the automated transcription's 1748. Identification of this farmer with this Robert is plausible, but name and place alone do not expressly exclude [[Glasgow-1502|the older Robert Glasgow]]. No kinship is stated.<ref>Registry of Deeds, memorial 76724, pp. 476–477, image 577; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S4ML original image], inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was born before 16 June 1641, probably in Scotland. His precise date and place of birth have not been identified.

He became a weaver and burgess of Edinburgh.

=== Apprenticeship and burgess status ===

On 16 June 1641 James, explicitly described as a son of '''Robert Glasgow, servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston''', was apprenticed to William Sclaitter, weaver.<ref name="Apprentice1641">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666'' (Scottish Record Society, 1906), printed p. 71, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up scan]: “Glasgow, James, son to Robert G., servitor to William Crichtoun, in Wester Duddingston, with William Sclaitter, weaver 16 June 1641.”</ref>

James was admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh on 20 June 1649. The entry identifies him as a weaver, states that he had been apprenticed to the deceased William Sklatter, and repeats the apprenticeship date of 16 June 1641.<ref name="Burgess1649">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208: “Glasgow, James, B., weiver, as p. to umq. Wm. Sklaitter, weiver, B. (16 June 1641) 20 June 1649.”</ref>

The matching master and exact apprenticeship date establish that the 1641 apprentice was the later Edinburgh weaver and burgess.

=== Marriages ===

James married first '''[[Whyte-2772|Bessie Whyte]]''' at Edinburgh on 6 July 1649.<ref name="EdinburghMarriages">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 267: “Glasgow, James, weaver; Bessie Whyte 6 July 1649” and “James, weaver; Agnes Duncan 11 Nov. 1653.”</ref>

He married second '''[[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]]''' at Edinburgh on 11 November 1653.<ref name="EdinburghMarriages" />

The matching name, occupation and parish, together with the sequential dates, identify the bridegroom in both entries as the same James Glasgow.

=== Children ===

James's known children were:

* '''[[Glasgow-3097|Helen Glasgow]]''', daughter of Bessie Whyte;
* '''[[Glasgow-3099|Jonet Glasgow]]''', daughter of Bessie Whyte;
* '''[[Glasgow-1374|Robert Glasgow]]''', son of Agnes Duncan;<ref name="RobertBaptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRSV-T1T Robert Glasgow, baptised 5 May 1655, Edinburgh], son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>
* '''[[Glasgow-3143|Marion Glasgow]]''', daughter of Agnes Duncan;
* '''[[Glasgow-1373|Bethia Glasgow]]''', daughter of Agnes Duncan; and
* '''[[Glasgow-1057|John Glasgow]]''', son of Agnes Duncan.

The individual baptismal records should be consulted for the evidence identifying each child's mother.

Marion Glasgow married William Calder at Edinburgh on 29 June 1686.<ref name="MarionMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Marion; William Calder 29 June 1686.”</ref>

On the following day William Calder was admitted as a burgess through his wife Marion, who was explicitly described as a daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess.<ref name="CalderBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 91: “Calder, Wm., B., weaver, be r. of w. Marion, dr. to James Glasgow, weaver, B. 30 June 1686.”</ref>

This directly establishes Marion as James's daughter.

James's date and place of death have not been identified.

== Research Notes ==

=== Birth ===

The former birth date of 19 March 1626 and birthplace of Inveresk do not belong to this James.

The only presently supported birth statement is that James was born before 16 June 1641, when he entered his apprenticeship.<ref name="Apprentice1641" />

His birthplace remains unknown.

=== Parentage ===

The apprenticeship record directly identifies James's father as '''Robert Glasgow, servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston'''.<ref name="Apprentice1641" />

'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' is a plausible existing-profile match for this father because of the Wester Duddingston association and chronology. The record does not, however, contain enough information to prove that the named father and the existing profile represent the same man. That relationship should therefore remain uncertain.

The record does not name James's mother.

'''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' is not identified as his mother in any inspected record. Any attachment should remain uncertain and be treated as a working hypothesis rather than an established relationship.

=== Distinct from the Inveresk James ===

This James was not '''[[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]]''', who was baptised at Inveresk and Musselburgh on 19 March 1626 as a son of [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-296|Jannet Clerk]].<ref name="InvereskBaptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', James Glasgow, baptised 19 March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh, son of Alexander Glasgow, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW record VQ4V-GQW] (accessed 2025).</ref>

The 1641 apprenticeship names Robert Glasgow, not Alexander Glasgow, as the father of the Edinburgh weaver. The two men should remain on separate profiles.

=== Incorrect child profile ===

'''[[Glasgow-1376|James Glasgow]]''' is not a supported child of this family and should not be attached as a son born on 29 January 1657.

The cited record for that date is the baptism of Marion Glasgow and names James Glasgow as her father. It is not a birth or baptism record for a son named James.

=== Identity caution ===

This James should not be confused with '''[[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow]]''', who married [[Clerk-460|Helen Clerk]] and was associated with [[Glasgow-3093|John Glasgow]].

The Edinburgh weaver is identified by:

* the 1641 apprenticeship naming him as a son of Robert Glasgow;
* his apprenticeship to William Sclaitter;
* his 1649 admission as an Edinburgh burgess;
* his occupation as a weaver;
* his marriages to Bessie Whyte and Agnes Duncan; and
* the 1686 burgess record identifying Marion Glasgow as his daughter.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original apprenticeship papers or incorporation records;
* records establishing whether [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]] was the father named in the apprenticeship;
* records identifying James's mother;
* original baptism entries for each child;
* any further records establishing the children's mothers;
* a burial or testament for James;
* records identifying James's birthplace; and
* further records concerning William Calder and Marion Glasgow.

== Biography ==
James Glasgow (recorded often with spelling variations like Glasow, Glasgoue, Glasgou) was christened on '''11 May 1712''' in Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. His parents were recorded as Patrick Glasow and Helen Fairbarn<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-GMN : 16 September 2021), James Glasow, 1712. Parents: Patrick Glasow, Helen Fairbarn. Christening Date: 11 May 1712, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.</ref>. (A birth date of 5 May 1712 is given with this christening).

He married Elizabath Tait (also spelled Elizabeth) on '''25 January 1740''' in Stitchel, Roxburghshire<ref>"Scotland Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQ1-SPB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow marriage to Elizabath Tait, 25 Jan 1740, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.</ref>.

Based on available christening records, James and Elizabath had the following children primarily in Stitchel, with a later record in Swinton:
* [[Glasgow-1225|Patrick Glasgow (bef.1742-)]] (Glasgoue), christened 20 June 1742 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-5XM : 16 September 2021), James Glasgoue in entry for Patrick Glasgow, 1742. Christening Date: 20 Jun 1742, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgoue, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgow-1218|David Glasgow (bef.1744-)]], christened 6 June 1744 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMQ-472 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Daved Glasgou, 1744. Christening Date: 06 Jun 1744, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabeth Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgoue-1|James Glasgoue (abt.1746-)]], christened 27 July 1746 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-R58 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgoue in entry for James Glasgoue, 1746. Christening Date: 27 Jul 1746, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgoue, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.
* [[Glasgou-2|Elspeth Glasgou (abt.1748-)]], christened 27 March 1748 in Stitchel<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMM-R73 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgou in entry for Elspeth Glasgou, 1748. Christening Date: 02 Apr 1750, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabath Tait.</ref>.

Christening Date: 04 Aug 1765, Swinton, Berwickshire, Scotland. Parents: James Glasgow, Elizabeth Tait.</ref>. (Note the location change and time gap).

'''Important Note on Son John:''' [[Glasgow-1606|John Glasgow]] (born circa 1738, husband of Mary Robertson) has previously been identified as a son of this James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait. However, a christening record for John naming these parents has not yet been located or cited in this profile alongside his siblings listed above. Confirmation of this parental link is required (See Research Notes).

No death information for James is currently cited.

== Research Notes ==
* '''Confirming Son John:''' The primary research goal is to confirm if [[Glasgow-1606|John Glasgow]] (b. c1738) is indeed the son of this James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait. A birth/christening record for John, ideally dated around 1738-1741 (before Patrick) in Stitchel or nearby, naming James and Elizabath/Elizabeth as parents, is needed. Alternatively, other documents like wills or land records might establish the connection. Without this, the link between John (b.c1738) and this James (b.1712) remains unproven.
* '''Spelling Variations:''' Note the variations in spelling for the surname (Glasgow, Glasow, Glasgoue, Glasgou) and Elizabeth's first name (Elizabath) in the records. Consistent searching across variations is recommended.
* '''Birth Date:''' The exact birth date of May 5, 1712 needs verification, as the cited record confirms the May 11, 1712 christening. Checking the original parish register image may clarify if the birth date was recorded.
* '''Gap in Children & Relocation:''' There is a 15-year gap between the christening of Heling (1750 in Stitchel) and William (1765 in Swinton, Berwickshire). This suggests other children might be missing, or the family relocated during this period. The reason for the move from Roxburghshire to Berwickshire is unknown. Research in Swinton records around 1765 might provide further clues.
* '''Death Records:''' Death or burial records for James Glasgow and Elizabath Tait are needed. They might be found in Stitchel, Swinton, or potentially elsewhere depending on later movements.

== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}
Alexander Glasgow was christened on 9 March 1741 in the parish of Kirknewton, Midlothian, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-3052|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-313|Janet Clerk]].<ref name="Birth1741">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-P56 : 12 February 2020), Alexander Glasgow, 1741.</ref>

He married '''[[Munro-4088|Mary Munro]]''' (recorded as Munrow) in July/August 1757. Their marriage was recorded in both Edinburgh, Midlothian, and Barony, Lanarkshire, a common practice when the bride and groom resided in different parishes.<ref name="Marriage1757">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMW-HXK), Alexander Glasgow and Mary Monro, 31 Jul 1757, Edinburgh, Midlothian; AND "Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWC-Q5G), Alexander Glasgow and Mary Munrow, 4.co.uk/transcript?id=GBOR%2FGLA%2FRAMSHORN%2FBUR%2F000490), burial of Mary Glasgow on 22 January 1779, daughter of Alexr. Glasgow, glasgow regt., age 6m. Ref: 644/1/59.</ref>

Alexander and Mary had the following children:
* [[Glasgow-1348|John Glasgow]].{{Citation Needed}}
* [[Glasgow-1304|John Glasgow]], christened 3 December 1765 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire.<ref name="John1765">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X17D-67M), John Glasgow, 1765; citing Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland, reference - 2:17L1JNP.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3300|Barbara (Glasgow) Carswell]].{{Citation Needed}}
* [[Glasgow-3121|Mary Glasgow]], who died of smallpox at 6 months old and was buried on 22 January 1779 in the Ramshorn parish of Glasgow.

The date and place of his death are unknown.

== Research Notes ==

'''Marriage Registrations in Two Parishes'''

Two marriage records exist for this couple with dates just a few days apart: one in Edinburgh and one in the Barony parish of Glasgow. This is not evidence of two different couples. It was standard practice in 18th-century Scotland for a couple's marriage banns to be proclaimed and recorded in both the bride's and the groom's home parishes if they lived separately before the wedding.

Given that Alexander was from Kirknewton (near Edinburgh) and the family subsequently lived and raised their children in Glasgow, it is almost certain that these two records refer to the same couple. One record represents his parish (Edinburgh) and the other represents hers (Barony, Glasgow).

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was reportedly born in '''1737'''. A Larne or Kilwaughter congregational record is said to contain an entry for a James, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], at '''New Town, Larne''', in that year.

The original congregational entry, or a reliable full transcription, has not yet been cited on this profile. The exact birth date, place and identification of Hugh as James’s father should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively established.

James was a '''ropemaker''' at Larne, County Antrim. A lease dated 10 September 1760, registered on 24 November 1763, describes him as a ropemaker of Belfast and leases him a marked-out ropewalk at Gardenmore in Larne for thirty-one years from 1 November 1760. He agreed to build a house at the south end of the ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1760">Registry of Deeds transcript, lease dated 10 September 1760 and registered 24 November 1763, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 FamilySearch image].</ref>

On 28 March 1768 James, described as a ropemaker of the Old Town of Larne, assigned the plot, workhouse and remainder of the same lease to John Hill for £50. The matching commencement date and rent identify it as the 1760 ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1768">Registry of Deeds transcript, assignment dated 28 March 1768, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-DDXW FamilySearch image].</ref>


A memorial at '''St Cedma’s Church, Larne''', is reported to record James Glasgow with the dates '''1737–1802''' and to name his wife as '''Janet Shutter'''. A photograph or complete reliable transcription of the monument should be cited before the exact dates and marriage are treated as fully verified.

James is reported to have died in '''1802'''.

An Irish probate-index transcription records a '''James Glasgow of Larne''' in the Diocese of Belfast in '''1803'''.<ref>Irish probate index transcription supplied July 2026, entry for James Glasgow, Diocese of Belfast, residence Larne, 1803.</ref>

The agreement in name and residence, together with probate in the year after the reported death, makes this a strong match to the man commemorated at St Cedma’s.

The 1803 entry should be understood as a probate or estate event. It does not replace the reported 1802 death year. Probate occurring in the year following death would be ordinary.

The probate entry establishes Larne as James’s recorded residence during the estate proceedings. It does not by itself prove that Larne was his place of death.

=== Wife and family ===

James’s wife is reported on the St Cedma’s memorial as '''Janet Shutter'''.

The complete inscription should be obtained and cited because the memorial may also contain:

* Janet’s dates;
* the date or duration of the marriage;
* children buried in the same plot;
* other Glasgow relatives; or
* wording clarifying whether the monument was erected by descendants.

No inspected baptismal, marriage, will or probate record currently cited on this profile names James’s children.

The 1803 probate record may be important. An original will, administration bond or surviving abstract could identify:

* Janet as his widow;
* sons or daughters;
* married daughters or sons-in-law;
* executors or administrators;
* business partners;
* property at Larne or Blackcave; or
* other relatives.

== Research Notes ==
=== Identification and evidence ===

The following records probably concern the same man:

* the James, son of Hugh Glasgow, reportedly recorded at New Town or Larne in 1737;
* James Glasgow, ropemaker, documented in the 1760 ropewalk lease and 1768 assignment;
* James Glasgow commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802 and wife Janet Shutter; and
* James Glasgow of Larne whose estate entered Belfast probate in 1803.

The chronology and repeated Larne association make this identification plausible and probably correct.

The strongest direct contemporary evidence presently cited is the 1760 ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment. The baptism and memorial evidence still require complete source citations, and the probate index does not name James’s father or wife.

The profile should therefore distinguish between:

* directly documented facts, including James’s ropemaking and Larne residence in the 1760–1773 records;
* strong identity matches, including the 1803 probate entry; and
* reported but not yet fully exposed evidence, including the 1737 congregational entry and St Cedma’s memorial.

=== Ropemaker evidence and identity distinction ===

A Registry of Deeds memorial dated 14 May 1766 also names James Glasgow, ropemaker of Larne, as a witness.<ref>[https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/mem.php?memorial=204122 Registry of Deeds Index Project, memorial 204122], deed dated 14 May 1766.</ref> In 1773 Mr James Glasgow of Larne, gentleman, swore that he was aged upwards of thirty, placing his birth before 27 October 1743.<ref name="Larne1773">Registry of Deeds memorial and affidavit, sworn 27 October 1773, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-M72W-M FamilySearch image].</ref> Alexander Holmes's 1799 will later identifies a Larne occupant as James Glasgow, roper. The repeated occupation and place form a coherent sequence.

The 1768 assignment was witnessed by a '''different''' James Glasgow who was expressly described as a tanner. A 1778 mortgage and the 1786 Blackcave lease continue that tanner sequence and fit [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow (about 1747–1812)]]. The two tradesmen should not be conflated.

The reported 1737 congregational occurrence and the present uncertain placement under [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remain competing parentage hypotheses until the original entry or another relationship record is inspected.

=== Research priorities ===

Further research should obtain:

* the original or fullest available congregational entry for the 1737 James, son of Hugh Glasgow;
* the name of the congregation and exact wording of that entry;
* a photograph or complete transcription of the St Cedma’s memorial;
* evidence supporting Janet Shutter’s identity and marriage to James;
* the exact nature of the 1803 Belfast probate entry;
* the original will, administration record or bond, if it survives;
* a Betham or other pre-destruction abstract of the estate;
* names of beneficiaries, executors, witnesses or sureties; and
* records identifying any children of James and Janet.

=== Research conclusion ===

James Glasgow was directly recorded as a ropemaker in the 1760 Larne ropewalk lease, the 1766 memorial and the 1768 assignment.

The 1803 Belfast probate entry for James Glasgow of Larne is a strong match to the man reportedly commemorated at St Cedma’s with dates 1737–1802. It supports Larne as his probate residence while remaining consistent with death in 1802.

The reported identification of his wife as Janet Shutter and his father as Hugh Glasgow is plausible, but the complete memorial and congregational record should be cited before those relationships and the exact dates are treated as certain.

=== Current Larne reconstruction ===

James is securely the Belfast/Larne ropemaker in the 1760 Gardenmore ropewalk lease and its 1768 assignment, and the 1773 affidavit places that adult James at Larne and over thirty. The 1768 document separately calls its witness James Glasgow a tanner; that is a different occupational record group, probably [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]], and does not change this James's occupation. The original 1784 lease registered in 1790 has now been inspected: its witness is explicitly a tanner and belongs to the separate occupational sequence probably represented by [[Glasgow-3991|James Glasgow]]. James is a plausible earlier-generation candidate in the Larne reconstruction, including as a possible father of [[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and possible kin of [[Glasgow-3904|older Alexander Glasgow]], but no record yet makes either relationship. His 1762 marriage to Janet Shutter postdates Adam's estimated 1758 birth, so Janet cannot be called Adam's mother. A William Glasgow, merchant, witnessed the 1760 lease, but is not yet definitely [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]].<ref name="LarneCurrent">Registry of Deeds memorials for the 1760 lease, 1768 assignment and 1773 affidavit, cited above.</ref>

=== Additional source context ===

These contextual and comparison sources supplement the individual record assessments above; they do not supply a missing parental statement.
* Related profile: [[Glasgow-1509]].
<ref name="Retained2">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF Registry of Deeds, 1784 transaction registered in 1790: James Glasgow, tanner; sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790].</ref>


A lease dated 14 January 1784 was witnessed by James Glasgow of Larne, '''tanner''', with Samuel Drummond, merchant, and James Farries, writing clerk. James’s affidavit was sworn 17 August 1790; the memorial was registered on 23 August. The original reads “Tanner”, resolving an earlier automated “Turner” reading. This strengthens the occupational sequence, without independently naming his family.<ref name="Tanner1784">Registry of Deeds, memorial 278037, lease 14 January 1784, sworn 17 August and registered 23 August 1790, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ4-4SJF FamilySearch image 437], original inspected 21 September 2026. The online collection label 1734–1736 does not describe this image’s date.</ref>

=== Newtown title succession: identities unresolved ===

An 1874 deed recites a lease to James Glasgow dated 2 October 1779 and its renewal to Anne Glasgow and Jane Glasgow on 25 February 1832. The north-side Newtown property, formerly John English’s, adjoined a tenement formerly Hugh Glasgow’s. This documents succession to a lease, but does not call the women James’s daughters or identify which James held it. Glasgow-1698.public_addition_wikitext:
=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. [https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Minister compilation], John Glasgow, New Row; derivative entry, not an original register.</ref>


=== Earlier review history ===
A possible identification concerns Samuel Glasgow, farmer examined at Moneymore. An 1845 tenant-right discussion quotes Samuel Glasgow, described as an intelligent farmer examined at Moneymore, advocating secure tenure and protection against rent charged on improvements. He described seeing reclamation on Sir Thomas Staples’s land in his neighbourhood.<ref>Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 March 1845, p. 1, Ulster tenant-right discussion; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050103241/ record]; Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 19 March 1845, p. 1, alternate archive image of tenant-right passage; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1380777866/ record].</ref> Moneymore is where he was examined, not an explicit home townland. The date of his examination, age and relatives are unstated. Cookstown farmers [[Glasgow-2054]] and [[Glasgow-1698]] are compatible; [[Glasgow-2908|Lisnagaver Glasgow]] is a weaker regional comparison, without a locality or occupation bridge. No connection to Lisnagaver is established. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Working father review, 20 October 2026 ===

Prefer the William named in PRONI T1959/3 as Samuel Glasgow-1698’s probable working father, at 66% confidence. The positive case combines the expressly named Samuel in the letter, the exact Killycurragh family-farm setting, and the later Samuel’s documented farmer/probate household there in 1857. It replaces an unnecessary blanket hold with a testable family placement. The identity is less secure than James’s: there is no traced lease succession or age for the letter’s Samuel, and the current birth estimate may represent a later generation.

The percentages assess each entire father-to-profile proposition, including identification of the named son with the later profile; they are subjective comparative judgments, not measured frequencies. The original letter and holding succession remain unverified. Samuel’s circa-1800 birth is an estimate, and a materially older Samuel or a later same-name descendant is possible. His wife Anne’s approximate 1801 birth and their children in the 1820s–1830s do not date Samuel himself. A nephew or later tenant could share the name and townland. Do not transfer a recorded relationship to a later adult merely from the letter’s parent clause. William’s birth and death remain unknown. The letter names an older William as his father; the specific Kirknewton profile is a 36% possibility. His mother remains unidentified. Miss Cunningham is retained as William’s reported wife, without selecting her as either profile’s mother. No existing person is merged or redated, and no live WikiTree edit has been made.

Inspect PRONI T1959/3 and associated family papers; test William’s identity against existing candidates and trace the Killycurragh holding through leases, rentals and valuation revisions. Establish Samuel’s age independently. The 1836 index date is probate information, not James’s exact death date.<ref>PRONI T1959/3; [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published family-letter transcription], earlier reviewed account reused; original not newly inspected. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/record-william-glasgow-killycurragh-t1959.html Sourced William Glasgow draft and identity comparisons].</ref>
Glasgow-1698.remote_wikitext:
[[Category:Killycurragh Townland, Derryloran Parish, County Tyrone]]

== Biography == 

Samuel Glasgow passed away on 29 July 1857 in Killycurragh, County Tyrone. His will, containing one codicil, was proven at Armagh. The will’s executors were Andrew Thomas Ferguson of Cookstown and John Creighton of Tamlaght, both in County Tyrone. Samuel was a farmer in Killycurragh, and his estate was valued at under £200.<ref>PRONI Will Calendars: "The Will with one Codicil of Samuel Glasgon late of Killycuragh in the County of Tyrone Farmer deceased who died 29 July 1857 at Killycuragh aforesaid was proved at Armagh by the oaths of Andrew Thomas Ferguson of Cookstown and John Creighton of Tamlaght (Cookstown) in the said County of Tyrone the Executors."</ref><ref>http://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/reels/cwa/005014882/005014882_00057.pdf</ref>

== Research Notes ==

From Samuel Glasgow’s will, we know the following about his family:

* '''Son:''' [[Glasgow-1697|Silas Glasgow]].
* '''Married Daughter:''' Sarah Mahood.
* '''Wife:''' Nancy Glasgow.
* '''Unmarried daughters:''' [[Glasgow-1835|Mary Jane (Glasgow) Parke (1836-1898)]] and [[Glasgow-1717|Adelaide Glasgow]].

In his will, Samuel refers to his residence as "the family mansion."

== Additional Family Connections == 

An interesting [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/3d923d3323349 marriage record] from 1863 at Owenreagh indicates a James Glasgow (widower), son of Samuel Glasgow. This family had another connection to Sixtowns through [[Loughlin-342|Isabella (Loughlin) Glasgow (abt.1823-1894)]], who was the wife of Silas Glasgow.

According to the '''Londonderry Standard''' marriage notice, Silas was Samuel’s eldest son.

=== Newspaper Mentions ===

In a [https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0001144/18571113/028/0003 newspaper article] from 13 November 1857, after Samuel’s death, he is listed as "Mr. Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh, Cookstown," one of the highest cesspayers in the barony.

=== Other Research Notes ===

Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh should not be confused with [[Glasgow-2054|Samuel Glasgow (abt.1792-1865)]] from Gortin, Derryloran, who died on a different date.

There is a possibility that [[Glasgow-2526|Samuel Glasgow (abt.1831-1902)]] was also a son, though he was not mentioned in the will.

Further DNA research suggests that [[Glasgow-1386|Samuel Glasgow (abt.1791-)]] may be another possible match, as there is a 10.9cM DNA match with [[Glasgow-933|M Glasgow]] (4th cousin relationship on the parent's side).

An extensive interview with '''Mr. Samuel Glasgow of Killycurragh''' was published in April 1844.<ref>https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/EPPI-1246182</ref>

== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' lived at Irvine, Ayrshire, where the parish register names him as the father of three children baptised between 1741 and 1747. Their mother was [[Nasmith-38|Helen Nasmith]], named in the same entries:

* [[Glasgow-4116|John Glasgow]], baptised 6 August 1741
* [[Glasgow-4110|Allan Glasgow]], baptised 22 May 1743
* [[Glasgow-4128|Susanna Glasgow]], baptised 29 March 1747

No birth or baptism record for James himself has been found, so his birth is placed before 1722, the year by which he must have been born to father John in 1741. Irvine is inferred from his children's baptisms and is not independently recorded.<ref name="IrvineOPR">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine, Ayrshire, Old Parish Register OPR 595/1; the individual baptism entries are cited on each child's profile, for example [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3575071&tab=this John Glasgow, 1741].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

James and Helen are linked only by the recurring father and mother names in the Irvine register. No record of James's own parents, birth or death has been found.
