== Biography ==

James Glasgow is named as a father in two Irvine, Ayrshire, baptism entries. [[Glasgow-4129|James Glasgow]] was baptised on 11 April 1721 with parents James Glasgow and [[Rae-3513|Margaret Rae]]. [[Glasgow-4120|William Glasgow]] was baptised on 3 February 1723 with parents James Glasgow and [[Rae-3515|Marion Rae]].<ref name="James1721">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine Old Parish Register, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573667&tab=this James Glasgow baptism, 11 April 1721]. The individual child profile gives the full indexed entry.</ref><ref name="William1723">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine Old Parish Register, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573825&tab=this William Glasgow baptism, 3 February 1723]. The individual child profile gives the full indexed entry.</ref>

No birth, baptism or death record has been identified for this adult James. His birth before about 1702 is an adult-age estimate from the 1721 child; Irvine is his recorded household locality, not a proved birthplace.

== Research Notes ==

The former father profile Glasgow-4164, based on the 1723 William entry, was merged into this profile on 27 September 2026. The same uncommon father name and Rae surname in the same Irvine parish within two years, with no separate identified James, support one adult identity. The maternal given names differ: Margaret and Marion may refer to distinct women or to a transcription/register variation. Both named mothers and both baptism entries are preserved; no marriage, death or remarriage between 1721 and 1723 is asserted without a record.

The birth estimates on the two former profiles were derived only from the children's dates. Compare the original 1721 and 1723 register pages and search Irvine marriage or burial entries for the two Rae names.

== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}
James Glasgow was born circa 1585, likely in Scotland. This estimate is based on the birth year of his first known child in 1605. He appears in baptismal records as a father residing in Midlothian, Scotland, between 1605 and 1618, with records showing activity in two distinct parishes: Mid Calder (OPR parish #694) and Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref>A patron submission to the LDS Church suggested a birth location of Inveresk, but this requires stronger sourcing. See Research Notes.</ref>

The mother of his children is not named in these specific records. James is recorded as the father of the following six children, with the location alternating between the two parishes:

* [[Glasgow-1082|George Glasgow]], christened 17 February 1605 in Mid Calder.<ref name="George1605">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BK-1B4), James Glasgow in entry for Gerge Glasgow, 1605.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-994|Eduard Glasgow]], born 27 February 1609 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="Eduard1609">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRF-FQX), James Glasgow in entry for Eduard Glasgow, 1609.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1083|Beatrix Glasgow]], christened 15 April 1610 in Mid Calder.<ref name="Beatrix1610">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-L51), James Glasgow in entry for Beatrix Glasgow, 1610.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow]], born 10 July 1614 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="William1614">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRN-WMS), James Glasgow in entry for William Glasgow, 1614.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]], christened 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder.<ref name="John1616">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-JXY), James Glasgow in entry for John Glasgow, 1616.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-993|Agnes Glasgow]], born 22 February 1618 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="Agnes1618">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRJ-SZX), James Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, 1618.</ref>

The pattern of baptisms/births alternating between Mid Calder and Inveresk with Musselburgh (parishes roughly 15-18 miles apart) suggests James and his family had significant ties, possibly residency or work, in both locations within Midlothian during this period.

The date and location of James Glasgow's death are currently unknown.

=== Research Notes ===

* '''Dual Locations:''' The records confirm activity in Mid Calder (Parish 694) and Inveresk with Musselburgh, Midlothian. Further research into land, kirk session, or court records might clarify the family's presence in both parishes.
* '''Single Identity Assumption:''' This profile currently assumes these records pertain to one James Glasgow, based on the consistent name and plausible timeframe/geography. However, the possibility of two contemporaries named James Glasgow cannot be entirely ruled out without further evidence (e.g., marriage, death, or conflicting records).
* '''Inveresk Birth Claim:''' A citation noted "Place of birth is listed as Inveresk<ref name="PatronSub">Patron submission record, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints ''(Note: Source details are vague in original text; treat with caution unless specific record identified).''</ref>". This is generally considered weak evidence unless corroborated by primary sources.
* '''Possible Earlier Record (Speculative):''' A record from Perth dated 19 January 1575 mentions the baptism of a James '''Glas''', son of '''Alexander Glas''' (Perth OPR 387/10/172).<ref name="Perth1575">OPR entry: “GLAS JAMES / ALEXR. GLAS/ M 19/01/1575 387 10 / 172 Perth”. Also cited via FamilySearch profile LZGY-NSY (https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LZGY-NSY) accessed [Insert Date].</ref> Any connection between this Perth record and the James Glasgow of Midlothian (born c. 1585) is unconfirmed and requires significant further research. It may relate to a different individual or family line.
* '''Mother Unknown:''' The mother of the children listed above is not identified in these baptism/birth records.
* '''Excluded Information:''' Information regarding a wife named Christina Bie, later generations potentially linked via Geneanet, or specific GEDmatch references previously in comments have been excluded from this biography pending reliable sources confirming their connection to *this* James Glasgow.



=== Connection to Father ===
Placement under Andrew Glasgow (bef.1540–1598) fits the alternating parish pattern between Mid Calder and Inveresk/Musselburgh from 1605 to 1618. Andrew’s branch anchors the Caldercleir/Mid-Lothian corridor and expands toward the east-coast parishes. Andrew’s testament names sons James and John; this James matches that statement and geography. No record on this page states his father.

* '''Next Step:''' Compare sponsors and witnesses across the 1605–1618 baptisms with Andrew’s testament and nearby sasines for overlapping names.

=== Possible older daughter ===
[[Glasgow-3183|Jonet Glasgow, wife of Martin Ramsy]], is James's leading possible older daughter. James is the only identified same-generation Glasgow repeatedly recorded as a father at Mid Calder, where children attributed to him were baptised in 1605, 1610 and 1616; Jonet married there in 1624.<ref>FamilySearch indexes: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BK-1BW George Glasgow, 1605], [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-L51 Beatrix Glasgow, 1610], [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-JXY John Glasgow, 1616], and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9X-4PR Jonet Glasgow and Martin Ramsy, 1624].</ref>

The placement also resolves a conflict in Jonet's current genealogy: Andrew of Corstoun's 1598 testament names exactly four operative children and excludes her.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32; printed index in ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514-1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref> James is now attached as Jonet's uncertain working father. The relationship remains a moderate-to-strong placement rather than direct proof, and Jonet's mother is unidentified.

== Biography ==

James Glasgow was christened on 21 May 1738 in Covington and Thankerton, Lanarkshire, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1070|George Glasgow]] and [[Williamson-12853|Agnes Williamson]].<ref name="Baptism1738">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLX-GQN record XTLX-GQN], accessed 11 February 2020), James Glasgow, christened 21 May 1738, Covington and Thankerton, Lanarkshire; son of George Glasgow and Agnes Williamson.</ref>

No record has yet been found that proves what happened to James after his christening.

=== Possible Adult Records ===

A James Glasgow was recorded as the father of Robert Glasgow, christened on 17 February 1760 in Wandell and Lamington. Robert's mother was Marion Saidler.<ref name="Robert1760">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTFT-KJ9 record XTFT-KJ9], accessed 16 September 2021), Robert Glasgow, christened 17 February 1760, Wandell and Lamington, Lanarkshire; son of James Glasgow and Marion Saidler.</ref>

A James Glasgow married [[Scott-41785|Mary Scott]] on 20 June 1766 in Wandell and Lamington.<ref name="Marriage1766">"Scotland Marriages, 1561-1910," database, FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XT1J-9QW record XT1J-9QW], accessed 11 February 2020), marriage of James Glasgow and Mary Scott, 20 June 1766, Wandell and Lamington, Lanarkshire.</ref>

James and Mary had a son:

* George Glasgow, christened on 7 May 1769 in Wandell and Lamington.<ref name="George1769">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTFT-2J1 record XTFT-2J1], accessed 16 September 2021), George Glasgow, christened 7 May 1769, Wandell and Lamington, Lanarkshire; son of James Glasgow and Mary Scot.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The 1766 marriage and the 1769 christening appear to concern the same James Glasgow. Both records are from Wandell and Lamington, and both name his wife as Mary Scott or Mary Scot.

The 1760 record may also concern the same man. This would suggest that Marion Saidler died, or that the earlier relationship ended, before James married Mary Scott in 1766. No supporting burial or marriage record has yet been found.

The James christened in 1738 is a reasonable candidate for the man recorded at Wandell and Lamington because:

* Covington and Thankerton is close to Wandell and Lamington.
* He would have been about 22 in 1760 and 28 in 1766.
* His father was named George, and James and Mary named their son George.

Other possible men named James Glasgow were reviewed, but currently appear less likely: 

* [[Glasgow-1469|James Glasgow (1736-)]], christened in 1736, was associated with Kilwinning, Ayrshire, and is said to have moved to Cookstown, County Tyrone, Ireland, around 1750. This conflicts with the later records in Wandell and Lamington. 
* [[Glasgow-3486|James Glasgow (1730-)]], born around 1730 in Kirknewton and East Calder, was associated with Katharine Rule and their daughter Marion, born in 1751. No record currently connects him to Wandell and Lamington, Marion Saidler or Mary Scott.

None of these points proves that the records concern the same man. The parish records do not give James's age, parents, occupation or exact residence.

The original register images should be checked for further details, particularly James's residence, occupation, marital status and witnesses.

Grant, ed., ''Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547-1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196]. This profile retains the Montfoid husband as an '''uncertain earlier same-person hypothesis''' for the John Glasgow of Quodquen whose estate was confirmed in 1650; no reviewed record bridges the two places or proves they were the same man. '''Transcription and identification note:''' This profile is based principally on the 1650 testament dative of John Glasgow in Quodquen. The document is written in seventeenth-century Scots Secretary Hand. The relationship between John and Bessie Glasgow is secure. The testament first describes Bessie as John’s “laufull sister” and later describes John as “hir brother”. A separate 1610 testament index identifies Bessie Robertson as the spouse of a John Glasgow in Montfoid. It has not been established that the John Glasgow in Montfoid was the same man as John Glasgow in Quodquen. {{Image|file=Glasgow-3296.png |align=c |size=l |caption=Testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, 1650. Lanark Commissary Court, National Records of Scotland reference CC14/5/5, images 65–66. }} == Biography == '''John Glasgow''' lived at Quodquen in Lanarkshire. He died in April 1650, and his estate was confirmed at Lanark on 27 May 1650.National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, CC14/5/5, images 65–66, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen; confirmed 27 May 1650.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy]. His testament was dative because he died intestate. It twice identifies Bessie Glasgow as his lawful sister: first when appointing her executrix dative and again when describing John as her brother. It names no parent, wife, son or daughter. Thomas Glasgow, deceased, and a William Glasgow appear in the financial account, but their relationships to John are not stated. === Residence and death === '''John Glasgow''' lived at '''Quodquen''', in Lanarkshire, Scotland.National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, Wills and Testaments, reference CC14/5/5, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, images 65–66. He died during '''April 1650'''. His estate was confirmed at Lanark on '''27 May 1650'''.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy]. The record gives Quodquen as John’s residence. It does not state his birthplace or exact place of death. === Testament and executrix === John’s estate was recorded as a '''testament dative'''. He had died intestate, and the commissary court appointed an executor to administer the estate. [[Glasgow-XXXX|Bessie Glasgow]] was appointed executrix dative. The testament expressly describes her as John’s:
“laufull sister”
The confirmation later describes John as:
“hir brother”
The relationship is therefore directly stated twice in the original record. On 27 May 1650 Bessie appeared before Master John Carmichael, commissary of Lanark, presented the inventory and was confirmed as executrix after providing the required caution. === Estate === John’s physical possessions included: * three kine, valued together at £8 Scots; * his clothing or bodily apparel, valued at £20 Scots. The physical inventory totalled '''£28 Scots'''. The testament also listed debts and sums owing to John’s estate. The clerk recorded:
“Na debtis awin be ye deid”
No debts owed by John himself were entered. The clerk also recorded:
“Na divisioun”
No formal division of the estate was entered. === Family === ==== Sister ==== * [[Glasgow-XXXX|Bessie Glasgow]] — John’s lawful sister and executrix dative. No parent, wife, son or daughter is identified in John’s 1650 testament. The absence of a wife or child from the record does not prove that John had never married or had no children. It means only that none is named in this testament. ==== Possible wife: Bessie Robertson ==== The published index to the Glasgow Commissariot Register contains the entry:
“Robertson, Bessie, spouse to John Glasgow, in Montfoid — 17 Aug. 1610”
The corresponding entry under Glasgow reads:
“Glasgow, John, in Montfoid. See Robertson, Bessie.”
This establishes that '''Bessie Robertson''' was the wife of a John Glasgow in Montfoid. The date is the testament date, not a marriage date.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'', Scottish Record Society, vol. 7 (Edinburgh, 1901), p. 426, entry for Robertson, Bessie, dated 17 August 1610, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/426/mode/2up digital copy]. It is possible that the Montfoid man was the same John who later lived at Quodquen, but this has not been proved. The two records concern different residences and commissary jurisdictions, and neither provides a distinctive identifier linking the men. Bessie Robertson should therefore remain a research possibility, not a confirmed wife. She must not be confused with John’s sister Bessie Glasgow. === Other people named in the testament === The following people appear in connection with money or debts owing to John’s estate: * Thomas Glasgow, deceased, in Quodquen; * John Miller, described as an executor; * W[illia]m Glasgow, apparently owing £8 Scots; * Isobell Fisher in Glasfurde; * James Gibson in Quodquen; * a probable William Wilsone; * Master John Carmichael, commissary of Lanark; * an unidentified cautioner for Bessie Glasgow. Thomas Glasgow and W[illia]m Glasgow may have belonged to the wider Glasgow family at Quodquen, but the testament does not state their relationship to John. == Research Notes == === Current evidence assessment === ==== Distinct records combined on this profile ==== The former profile [[Glasgow-3296]] now redirects here. That merge brought in a separate Mid Calder reconstruction. Derivative baptism indexes name a Jhone Glasgow as father of Jhone in 1608 and William in 1609.“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch ([https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-X8B record X1BL-X8B]), Jhone Glasgow, 1608, father Jhone Glasgow.“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1B2-3LV record X1B2-3LV]), William Glasgow, baptised 24 December 1609 at Mid Calder, son of Jhone Glasgow. Those records prove a father-child pair in Mid Calder but provide no bridge to the man whose estate was confirmed at Quodquen forty-one years later. [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]] must therefore remain uncertain children of this profile. A 1610 testament index also identifies Bessie Robertson as the wife of a John Glasgow in Montfoid.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196]. Bessie Robertson was the wife of the Montfoid man; she was not the Bessie Glasgow identified as the Quodquen man's sister. The Montfoid, Mid Calder and Quodquen records are chronologically compatible with one life, but no residence, occupation, property, spouse or kinship evidence joins all three. Both earlier identities and the wife relationship remain uncertain. The attached [[Glasgow-1029|Stephen Glasgow]] and Margaret Graham are not identified as this John's parents by any of these records. Their links must remain uncertain pending positive relationship evidence. The testament gives Quodquen as John's residence, not his birthplace or place of death. The present Mid Calder death location came from the merged earlier reconstruction and is unsupported by a death record; it must be treated as uncertain unless a sourced replacement location is established. [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] of nearby Linlithgow is a duplicate candidate only. Similar name, date and region do not justify another merge without an identity bridge. === Data corrections === The cited testament shows that John: * died in April 1650, not 1649; * lived at Quodquen; * was confirmed on 27 May 1650. The record does not state that he died at Carluke. Carluke should therefore be removed as the death location unless supported by another source. === Working child relationship === No child is identified in John’s testament. The existing relationship to [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow]] (formerly Glasgow-3019) is retained as an '''uncertain working son''', not as a proved relationship. The 1650 testament neither identifies nor disproves him. The 1650 testament does not prove John as the father of: * Isobell Glasgow; * John Glasgow of Burnesyde; * any other presently identified child. === Parentage === John’s father and mother are not named in the 1650 testament. Any parent relationship should remain unsupported unless established by another record. === Further research === Useful records include: * the original 1610 testament of Bessie Robertson; * Quodquen parish and kirk-session records; * land, sasine and rental records naming John, Bessie, Thomas or William Glasgow; * records identifying John Miller and the estate for which he acted; * any record connecting John Glasgow of Montfoid with Quodquen; * evidence establishing whether Thomas Glasgow or William Glasgow was related to John and Bessie. {{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

== Biography ==

'''Robert Glasgow''' was buried in the parish of Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland, on '''17 January 1647'''.<ref name="RobertBurial">Church of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Duddingston deaths and burials, burial of Robert Glasgow, 17 January 1647, parish number 684, reference 60/47, ''ScotlandsPeople''.</ref>

His date and place of birth have not been identified.

The burial entry does not state Robert's age, occupation, residence, spouse, parentage or children. It should not be assumed that every contemporary man named Robert Glasgow in Midlothian was the same person.

== Research Notes ==

=== Profile identity ===

This profile represents the '''Robert Glasgow buried at Duddingston on 17 January 1647'''.

The burial is the only record presently identified that can be assigned to this profile with reasonable certainty. Other records involving men of the same name are discussed below as possible or rejected identifications.

Because the record is a burial entry rather than an identified death entry, Robert died on or before 17 January 1647. His precise date of death is unknown.

=== Birth ===

The structured birth year of about 1582 and the Glasgow birthplace are retained as uncertain working estimates.

No inspected record states Robert's age or birthplace or supports either estimate. They should not be treated as proved facts.

Although Robert was buried in Scotland, the burial record does not establish that he was born there.

=== Possible identification at Wester Duddingston ===

On 16 June 1641 '''[[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]]''', son of a Robert Glasgow who was servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston, was apprenticed to William Sclaitter, weaver.<ref name="JamesApprentice">Francis J. Grant, ed., [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666''] (Scottish Record Society, 1906), printed p. 71: “Glasgow, James, son to Robert G., servitor to William Crichtoun, in Wester Duddingston, with William Sclaitter, weaver 16 June 1641.”</ref>

The record directly proves that:

* James's father was named Robert Glasgow;
* the elder Robert was associated with Wester Duddingston in 1641;
* Robert was then a servant to William Crichtoun; and
* James was apprenticed to William Sclaitter.

The matching surname, Duddingston locality and compatible dates make the father named in 1641 a plausible candidate for the man buried there in 1647.

The identification is not proved. Neither record supplies Robert's age, wife, occupation beyond the 1641 description, or another distinguishing relationship that securely joins the two entries.

If James remains attached as a son of this Robert, the relationship should be marked uncertain.

=== James Glasgow the Edinburgh weaver ===

The apprentice named in 1641 was later admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh on 20 June 1649. The burgess entry identifies him as a weaver, names his deceased master William Sklaitter and repeats the exact apprenticeship date of 16 June 1641.<ref name="JamesBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208: “Glasgow, James, B., weiver, as p. to umq. Wm. Sklaitter, weiver, B. (16 June 1641) 20 June 1649.”</ref>

The matching master and exact apprenticeship date establish that the 1641 apprentice and the later Edinburgh burgess were the same James Glasgow.

This evidence strengthens the identification of James but does not provide additional information identifying his father with the man buried in 1647.

=== Distinct from the Inveresk James ===

The Edinburgh apprentice was not '''[[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]]''', who was baptised at Inveresk and Musselburgh on 19 March 1626 as a son of Alexander Glasgow and Jannet Clerk.<ref name="InvereskJames">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW James Glasgow, baptised 19 March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh], son of Alexander Glasgow.</ref>

The 1641 apprenticeship explicitly names Robert Glasgow, not Alexander Glasgow, as the father of the Edinburgh weaver.

The two men should remain on separate profiles.

=== Possible father ===

'''[[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]]''' is attached as Robert's uncertain father.

Archibald and his wife Isobell Neulands are documented acquiring a tenement in Glasgow on 21 May 1551.<ref name="Archibald1551">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, ''First Protocol Book of William Hegait, 1547–55'' (Glasgow: Carson & Nicol, 1894), protocol 84, 21 May 1551, printed p. 31: Elizabeth Beitht sold a tenement to “Archinbald Glasgw and Isobell Neulands, spouses.” Robert Glasgw was among the witnesses.</ref>

The record does not name any children of Archibald and Isobell. It also does not state that Robert Glasgw, one of the witnesses, was Archibald's brother, son or other relative.

The proposed father-and-son relationship is chronologically possible. Archibald was married by 1551, and Robert's birth date is unknown. A son born later in the sixteenth century could have been the Robert associated with Wester Duddingston in 1641 and buried there in 1647.

There is presently no direct evidence establishing the relationship. No baptism, testament, sasine, deed or other inspected contemporary record identifies Robert as Archibald's son.

There is likewise no known record identifying a different father for Robert, and no better-supported profile has been identified as a child of Archibald.

Archibald may therefore remain attached as Robert's father with the relationship marked '''uncertain'''. The relationship should not be described as proved, probable or likely without further evidence.


=== Validator chronology note ===
WikiTree's warning that [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]] died before Robert was born is not a valid reading of the structured data. Archibald's death is recorded as '''after 1560''', an open lower boundary rather than a death in 1560. Robert's 1582 birth is an uncertain estimate, and their father-son relationship is itself marked uncertain. No source currently proves when Archibald died or that Robert was his son.

=== Deborah Ivey ===

'''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' has previously been attached as Robert's wife.

No Scottish marriage, baptism, testament, sasine, court record or other contemporary source has been found identifying Deborah as Robert's wife or as the mother of James Glasgow.

The attachment appears to derive from later compiled pedigrees involving Glasgow, Glasco, Glascocke or Glasscock families rather than from records concerning the Duddingston man.

Deborah should be detached from this profile.

=== Distinct from the Edinburgh cordiner ===

'''[[Glasgow-3938|Robert Glasgow]]''' married Jonet or Janet Thomsone at Edinburgh on 1 July 1652. The marriage register identifies that Robert as a cordiner.<ref name="CordinerMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Robert, cordiner; Janet Thomsone 1 July 1652.”</ref>

The Duddingston Robert was buried in January 1647 and therefore could not have been the bridegroom in July 1652.

The two men are conclusively distinct and should remain on separate profiles.

No evidence presently identifies the Edinburgh cordiner as a son of the Duddingston Robert.

=== Daniel Glasco ===

Daniel Glasco, husband of Mary Gamon, is documented in Lower Norfolk County, Virginia, through the will of his father-in-law John Gamon, dated 4 October 1693 and proved 15 March 1694.

No inspected record identifies Daniel as a son of the Robert buried at Duddingston.

The supposed relationship depends on unsourced submitted pedigrees and should be removed.

There is likewise no evidence that the Duddingston Robert:

* travelled to Virginia;
* had children in colonial America;
* belonged to the Glasco, Glascocke or Glasscock families;
* married Ann Johnson or Johnston; or
* participated in any Scottish-to-Virginia migration.

=== Occupation and social status ===

If the 1641 Wester Duddingston record concerns this Robert, he was described as a servant to William Crichtoun.

The term does not establish that Robert was a merchant, burgess, property owner or participant in civic government. No evidence presently supports those descriptions.

There is also no evidence that Robert migrated from the burgh of Glasgow to Edinburgh or Duddingston. His surname alone does not identify his place of origin.

=== Wife and other children ===

No inspected record identifies the wife of the Robert buried in 1647.

James Glasgow is the only proposed child supported by a contemporary record naming a father called Robert Glasgow in Wester Duddingston. Even that identification remains uncertain because the apprenticeship record does not directly connect the father to the 1647 burial.

No other children should be attached without independent evidence.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining research includes:

* inspection and transcription of the original 1647 Duddingston burial entry;
* Duddingston baptism, marriage and burial registers;
* neighbouring parish registers, including Canongate, Liberton and Inveresk;
* Edinburgh Commissary Court testaments;
* Midlothian sasines, rentals and property records;
* records concerning William Crichtoun of Wester Duddingston;
* household, estate or employment records naming William Crichtoun's servants;
* the original apprenticeship papers for James Glasgow;
* records of the Edinburgh Incorporation of Weavers;
* evidence identifying James Glasgow's mother;
* records naming the wife or other children of the Wester Duddingston Robert;
* a testament or estate inventory for the man buried in 1647; and
* evidence directly linking or separating the 1641 and 1647 records.

'''Ninian Glasgow''' was a fisher and burgess of Glasgow. On 23 October 1596
he was admitted burgess and freeman as the second son of [[Glasgow-1096|Robert
Glasgow]], fisher and burgess.<ref name="Burgess1596">James R. Anderson, ed.,
''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (1925),
[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p.
24], 23 October 1596.</ref> A 1605 roll also places him among Glasgow's
mariners and fishers.<ref>George Crawfurd, ''A Sketch of the Rise and Progress
of the Trades' House of Glasgow'' (1858), pp. 49, 56–57.</ref>

Ninian's earlier wife was [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]]. Her 1607 testament names
Ninian as her spouse and [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]] as her son.<ref name="Meik1607">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court,
CC9/7/5, images 82–83, testament of Jonet Meik.</ref> Ninian's own testament
again calls Robert his son, proving Robert's parentage by the two records.

By 10 January 1613 Ninian's spouse was [[Hutcheson-1774|Jonet Hutchesoun]]. He
appointed Jonet and Robert executors. The testament also names John Glasgow as
his brother and leaves ten merks to [[Glasgow-3062|Marioun Glasgow]], expressly
calling her his sister.<ref name="Ninian1613">National Records of Scotland,
Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, testament testamentar and
inventory of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613.
Working transcription of the original images supplied 6 September 2026.</ref>

Ninian died in January 1613. His testament was confirmed on 8 May; that later
date is not his death date.<ref name="Ninian1613" />

===  Identity, trade and civic status  ===

'''Niniane Glasgw''' was a '''fyscher''' and '''burges of Glasgw''' — a fisher and burgess of Glasgow.<ref name="Ninian1613" />

The occupation was formerly misread as '''flescher''', meaning butcher. That reading should be withdrawn. The manuscript word is '''fyscher'''. An independent burgess list also places '''Niniane Glasgow''' under the heading '''Marinellis and Fischeris''', meaning mariners and fishers.<ref name="Burgess1605">George Crawfurd, ''A Sketch of the Rise and Progress of the Trades' House of Glasgow: Its Constitution, Funds, and Bye-laws'' (Glasgow: Bell & Bain, 1858), pp. 49 and 56–57, reproducing the burgess roll associated with the reorganisation of 14 February 1605; Niniane Glasgow appears under “Marinellis and Fischeris”.</ref>

The 1605 list shows that he was already a burgess and associated with the fishing or maritime trade by that date. It does not necessarily give the date on which he was first admitted as a burgess.

James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], 23 October 1596 | The roll admits "Glasgow, Ninian, B. and F., as second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess." | Direct father-son evidence; also establishes Ninian's birth order, civic status and his father's occupation/status.

===  Chronology  ===

* '''1605''' — Niniane Glasgow appears in the burgess roll under mariners and fishers.<ref name="Burgess1605" />
* '''By 1607''' — he was the husband of Jonet Meik and the father of Robert Glasgow. Jonet's testament was indexed or recorded on 27 August 1607.<ref name="Jonet1607">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/5, Images 82–83, testament testamentar and inventory of Jonet Meik, spouse to Niniane Glasgw.</ref><ref name="SRSIndex">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'', Scottish Record Society, old series vol. 7 (Edinburgh, 1901), entries under Glasgow, Ninian, and Meik, Jonet.</ref>
* '''10 January 1613''' — Niniane made his own testament at Glasgow.<ref name="Ninian1613" />
* '''January 1613''' — he died during that month; the exact day is not stated.<ref name="Ninian1613" />
* '''8 May 1613''' — his testament was indexed or recorded under that date.<ref name="SRSIndex" />

The 8 May date is not his date of death.

===  Earlier known wife: Jonet Meik  ===

The earlier wife was '''Jonet Meik'''. Her surname is written '''Meik''' in the manuscript and in the printed testament index. The database form '''Melk''' is a later transcription or OCR error and should not be used as her surname.<ref name="Jonet1607" /><ref name="SRSIndex" />

Jonet's testament describes her as:

:'''Jonet meik spous to Niniane glasgw burges of glasgw'''

The executor or giving-up clause names:

:'''Niniane glasgw hir spous and Robert glasgw hir sone'''

A later legacy or residue clause again calls Robert:

:'''Robert glasgw hir sone'''

Robert is therefore directly identified as Jonet's son in two places. Niniane's 1613 testament independently calls Robert his son. This establishes Robert as the son of both Niniane Glasgow and Jonet Meik, rather than merely a probable relative.

Jonet also left a legacy to:

:'''Johne meik hir brother'''

A '''Marion Glasgow''' is named as a legatee in Jonet's testament, apparently receiving an article of clothing, but the clerk does not call Marion her daughter. Other Glasgow recipients may occur in the legacy list, but their forenames or relationships are not sufficiently clear to establish additional children.

Jonet was dead before her testament was recorded on 27 August 1607. Her death clause appears to refer to February, but the precise year numeral is not treated as settled here.

===  Later wife: Jonet Hutchesoun  ===

Niniane had remarried by 10 January 1613. His later wife was another woman named '''Jonet'''. Her surname appears twice in his testament: once in the nomination of executors and again in the confirmation clause.

The best palaeographic reading is '''Hutchesoun''', possibly '''Huchesoun'''. The middle of the word contains a crossed '''t''' followed by a '''ch'''-type group. The earlier working reading '''Herbessoun''' was closer than '''Smythesoun''', but does not fit the repeated letter pattern as well. '''Smythesoun''' should be withdrawn.

In a cautious semi-diplomatic transcription the name should be shown as:

:'''Jonet ⟦Hutchesoun?⟧'''

Jonet Hutchesoun and Robert Glasgow were appointed executors and intromitters with Niniane's movable estate.<ref name="Ninian1613" />

No surviving clause states that Jonet Hutchesoun was the mother of Robert or William. Robert's mother is independently proved to have been Jonet Meik. William's mother is not established by either testament.

The 1605 fisher list also contains a man printed as '''Niniane Hutchisonne''' immediately beside Niniane Glasgow.<ref name="Burgess1605" /> This makes Hutchesoun a locally and occupationally plausible surname, but it does not prove that the listed man was related to Niniane's later wife.



His assumed brother, [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow (abt.1540-1576)]] married a [[Hutcheson-1656|Margaret (Hutcheson) Glasgow (1550-)]], and his presumed Uncle [[Glasgow-3522|William Glasgow (abt.1525-bef.1586)]], married [[Herbison-439|Margaret (Herbison) Glasgow (abt.1540-)]]. Margaret’s father, Sir William Herbesoun, was a Roman priest with close ties to the Hutcheson family through his sister [[Herbertson-132|Helen Herbertson]], who married [[Hutcheson-1647|Thomas Hutcheson of Lambhill]]. This connection made Margaret Herbison likely a cousin of [[Hutcheson-1648|George Hutcheson]] and [[Hutcheson-1649|Thomas Hutcheson Jr.]].

===  Evidence that the records concern the same Niniane Glasgow  ===

The 1607 and 1613 testamentary records should be treated as referring to the same man.

The identification rests on a combined evidence set:

# Both records name '''Niniane Glasgow''' in Glasgow.
# The 1607 record calls him a '''burgess of Glasgow'''.
# The 1605 roll lists a Niniane Glasgow among Glasgow's mariners and fishers.
# The 1613 record calls him a '''fisher and burgess of Glasgow'''.
# The 1607 testament calls '''Robert Glasgow''' the son of Jonet Meik.
# The 1613 testament calls '''Robert Glasgow''' the son of Niniane Glasgow.
# The records fall only six years apart and form a coherent sequence: Jonet Meik died, Niniane remarried, and Niniane later made his own testament.

The shared son Robert is the strongest point. The identification does not depend only on the rarity of the surname, although the rarity of the name combination provides further support. A second contemporary Ninian Glasgow, burgess or fisher of Glasgow, with a son Robert would be required to displace this identification.

===  Children and other stated family  ===

The records establish the following relationships:

* '''Robert Glasgw''' — son of Niniane Glasgow and Jonet Meik.
** Jonet's 1607 testament calls him '''hir sone'''.
** Niniane's 1613 testament calls him '''his sone'''.
** He appears in the administration of both estates.
* '''William Glasgw''' — son of Niniane Glasgow.
** He received a separate provision in Niniane's 1613 testament.
** His mother is not identified in the surviving wording.
* '''Johne Glasgw''' — brother of Niniane Glasgow.
** Niniane left him '''ane new gowne'''.
* '''Johne Meik''' — brother of Jonet Meik.
** Jonet left him a legacy in her testament.
* '''Marion Glasgow''' — named as a legatee by Jonet Meik.
** No relationship is stated, so she should not presently be attached as a daughter solely from this entry.

Neither testament names Niniane's father or mother. No birthplace is stated.

===  Inventory and estate  ===

Niniane's inventory concerns his household goods, furnishings, vessels, money and debts.

Substantially readable items include:

* '''twa kistis and ane pres''' — two chests and a press or cupboard;
* '''ane mekill and littill buird''' — a large and a small board or table;
* '''all vther tymmer wark''' — the remaining wooden furniture;
* pewter vessels, described by weight;
* brewing vessels and other household vessels;
* '''the abuilzement of his bodie''' — his clothing or personal apparel.

The clerk lists debts owed to Niniane, debts payable from his estate, the free gear remaining after deduction, and division of the net movable estate. The exact totals and several debtor or creditor names remain too compressed or faded to quote safely from the present images.

The presence of brewing vessels is ordinary household evidence and does not make Niniane a brewer. His stated occupation remains fisher.

===  Testamentary provisions  ===

Niniane's personal testament begins at Glasgow on 10 January 1613. He was described as sick in body but of sound or perfect memory. He committed his soul to God and directed that his body be buried, although the precise burial wording is indistinct.

He appointed:

* his later wife, '''Jonet Hutchesoun'''; and
* his son, '''Robert Glasgw'''

as his executors and intromitters.

Among the readable legacies:

* '''Johne Glasgw his brother''' was to receive '''ane new gowne''';
* '''William Glasgw his sone''' received a separate provision, the exact object or amount being partly indistinct;
* further directions concern debts, expenses, legacies and the administration of the remaining estate.

===  Confirmation and archival extent  ===

Niniane's testament begins partway down Image 142, continues through Images 143 and 144, and concludes in the upper portion of Image 145. The large new testament heading in the lower portion of Image 145 belongs to another deceased person.

The lower part of Image 144 and upper part of Image 145 contain the formal Commissary Court confirmation. Jonet Hutchesoun and Robert Glasgow are again named in the executor wording. A cautioner or surety was provided, though the name and parts of the formula remain difficult to read.

===  Key semi-diplomatic extracts  ===

'''Jonet Meik's testament, 1607'''

:Jonet meik spous to Niniane glasgw burges of glasgw
:...
:be Niniane glasgw hir spous and Robert glasgw hir sone
:...
:to Johne meik hir brother
:...
:Robert glasgw hir sone

'''Niniane Glasgow's testament, 1613'''

:The testament testamentar and Inventar
:of the guidis geir debitis and sowmes of money q[uhi]lkis
:pertening to vmq[uhi]le Niniane glasgw fyscher burges
:of glasgw ...

:At glasgw the tent day of Januar 1613 zeiris
:...
:constitutis Jonet ⟦Hutchesoun?⟧ his spous & Robert
:glasgw his sone his executouris & intromettouris
:...
:Item to Johne glasgw his brother ane new gowne
:...
:Item to William glasgw his sone ⟦legacy partly indistinct⟧

===  Modern English rendering  ===

Ninian Glasgow was a fisher and burgess of Glasgow. A burgess roll from 1605 places him among the city's mariners and fishers.

His earlier known wife was Janet Meik. Her testament identifies Ninian as her husband and Robert Glasgow as her son. It again describes Robert as her son in the legacy or residue section. Ninian's own testament later describes Robert as his son, directly establishing Robert as the child of both spouses.

Janet Meik died before her testament was recorded in August 1607. Ninian subsequently remarried. By January 1613 his wife was another Janet, whose surname is best read as Hutchesoun. She and Robert were appointed to administer Ninian's estate.

Ninian made his will at Glasgow on 10 January 1613 and died during that month. He left a new gown to his brother John Glasgow and made a separate provision for his son William. His testament was recorded or confirmed on 8 May 1613.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

The manuscript calls Ninian a ''fyscher'', not a flesher or butcher. The word
''sister'' does not establish whether Marion was his full or half-sister, so
their common father should not be treated as certain solely from this clause.

A William Glasgow occurs in debt material and near the damaged foot of the
will's opening, but the previously asserted words ''his sone'' cannot be read
securely. [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith]], remains only a
possible son and possible identity match. The debtor and damaged will
occurrence may not be the same man. William's son Archibald was apprenticed at Edinburgh in 1639,<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666'' (1906), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up p. 71], 23 October 1639.</ref> which supplies a geographic and occupational lead but no father-to-son bridge back to Ninian.

The exact clothing description in the legacy to brother John is also unclear;
do not quote it as ''a new gown'' without a better image. [[Glasgow-1030]] is the
leading existing-profile candidate for John but is not yet identified by an
occupation, property, spouse or child bridge.

Jonet Hutchesoun was Ninian's spouse but was not Robert's mother. Robert's
maternity is separately proved by Jonet Meik's testament.

Several women recorded at South Leith or Edinburgh in 1611–19 form a possible collateral group, including [[Glasgow-3182|Barbara]], [[Glasgow-3598|Margaret]], [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara]] and [[Glasgow-3336|Isobel]]. Their locality and marriages to craftsmen make them reasonable network leads,<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 printed p. 267].</ref> but none is named as Ninian's daughter and no such relationship should be attached.

Elizabeth Hutchesoun received £5, but no relationship is stated. George
Glasgow, Ninian Hill, David Stevin and notary Mr Jeronimus Hutchesoun also
occur, with George and Ninian Hill recurring in the caution arrangements.
James Stewart, James Wilson, Alexander Fischer, John Morrison younger and
Malcolm Muir are further associates. These names are research leads only;
The testament does not state their kinship, including among the Hutchesouns.<ref name="Ninian1613" />

The printed testament index remains useful as a finding aid.<ref>Francis J.
Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments,
1547–1800'' (Edinburgh, 1901), entries for Ninian Glasgow and Jonet Meik.</ref>

* '''Meik''', not Melk, is the correct surname in the 1607 testament.
* The 1607 Jonet Meik was the earlier known wife of the same Ninian Glasgow who died in 1613.
* '''Robert Glasgow''' is directly proved as the son of both Ninian Glasgow and Jonet Meik.
* '''William Glasgow''' is directly proved as Ninian's son, but his mother remains unproved.
* '''Marion Glasgow''' is a named legatee in Jonet's testament, not a proved daughter.
* Ninian's occupation was '''fyscher''' or fisher, not '''flescher''' or butcher.
* The printed testament index's description of him as a fisher is correct on this point.
* The later wife's surname is best read '''Hutchesoun'''; '''Huchesoun''' remains a possible spelling. Smythesoun is withdrawn, and Herbessoun is less consistent with the repeated manuscript forms.
* The nearby '''Niniane Hutchisonne''' in the 1605 fisher list is a research lead only. No relationship to Jonet Hutchesoun is established.
* An estimated birth around 1550 is not stated in the records and should be labelled as an estimate, not a documented date.
* No parentage or birthplace for Ninian is supplied by either testament.
* No exact inventory or free-gear total is quoted here because the numeral groups have not yet been read securely.

=== Possible daughters and collateral women ===
Several disconnected women fit Ninian's household or immediate collateral circle, but none is directly named as his daughter. [[Glasgow-3262|Jonat Glasgow]], who had a child baptised at Mid Calder in 1609, repeats the name of Ninian's wife Jonet Meik. [[Glasgow-3182|Barbara]], [[Glasgow-3598|Margaret]], [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara]] and [[Glasgow-3336|Isobel]] appear in South Leith or Edinburgh records in 1611-19; the last three married two cordiners and a tailor.<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595-1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 printed p. 267].</ref>

*This is a family-specific trade and locality lead: Ninian's proved son Robert was a cordiner, his probable son [[Glasgow-3075|William]] lived at Leith, and William's son was apprenticed to a cordiner.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583-1666'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up p. 71], 23 October 1639.</ref> Jonet is the strongest individual daughter candidate; the four Edinburgh-Leith women are possible daughters or nieces. Ninian's and Jonet Meik's testaments do not identify them as daughters, so no exact parentage is asserted.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' was baptised at Torryburn, Fife, on 15 Oct 1689. The parish register names his father as [[Glasgow-4176|James Glasgow]] and his mother as [[Mitchell-58830|Jean Mitchell]].<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, his birth is placed before that date, and Torryburn is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

== Research Notes ==

'''James Glasgow''' was probably born about 1680. This is an uncertain estimate from his 1696 apprenticeship; his age and birthplace were not recorded. Edinburgh is usable only as an uncertain location inferred from the apprenticeship and his father's burgess status.

On 22 April 1696 James, son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess, was entered as apprentice to William Adam, apothecary and burgess of Edinburgh.<ref name="Apprentice1696">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1666–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 37, entry dated 22 April 1696; see also Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FEDINBURGH%2FAPPRENTICES%2F0005161%2F1&tab=this transcript SCOT/EDINBURGH/APPRENTICES/0005161/1], captured 3 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The Findmypast transcript renders the master as William Adamson. The published register reads “Wm. Adam”; that reading is used here.

[[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]], the documented Edinburgh weaver and burgess, is probably the father. He was admitted burgess in 1649 and was still acting as a weaver, burgess and apprenticeship master in 1693. The published register also places a Robert, son of James Glasgow, weaver, in an apprenticeship in 1672 and a Thomas, youngest son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess, in one in 1699. This is a coherent later-child group around the same burgh craftsman, but neither the 1696 nor 1699 entry names a mother. The father attachment should remain uncertain pending a baptism, testament or incorporation record with a second identifier.

This James is not the 1690 apprentice, whose father was explicitly deceased. [[Glasgow-1376|James Glasgow]] is excluded because his former 1657 birth was a record-role error based on Marion Glasgow's baptism and his remaining identity has no apothecary-apprenticeship evidence.

== Biography ==
{{Notables Sticker}}
James Glasgow was born before 1657, the son of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] and [[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]].<ref name=Birth>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YD-PRL : 11 February 2020), James Glesgow in entry for Marione Glesgow, 1657.</ref> He is noted in records during the tumultuous era of the Covenanter movement in Scotland.

In 1670, James appeared in legal proceedings for refusing to give his oath—a requirement aimed at suppressing illegal religious gatherings, known as field conventicles. These conventicles were organized by Presbyterians protesting government-imposed religious uniformity. James is specifically mentioned as being from a place called '''Whitecastle''', a site associated with Covenanting activities, although its exact location remains uncertain.<ref>Wodrow, Robert. ''The History of the Sufferings of the Church of Scotland from the Restoration to the Revolution.'' 1721. [https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_the-history-of-the-suffe_wodrow-robert_1721_1/page/n795/mode/2up?q=%22James+Glasgow%22 Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Whitecastle and Covenanting Context ===
It is not clear which Whitecastle James was associated with, as many areas in 17th-century Scotland hosted field conventicles, especially in Lanarkshire and Dumfriesshire. Lanarkshire, in particular, was a stronghold of Presbyterian dissent during this period. The fragmentary nature of the source makes it difficult to identify Whitecastle precisely without further geographical or archival clues.

=== Mr. Duncan and 1671 Proceedings ===
References to a certain '''Mr. Duncan''' in July 1671 connect him to the King’s Advocate and to legal action related to nonconformist religious practices. The records do not clarify whether he was a landowner, minister, or another figure who supported or harbored Covenanters. Many individuals, including local gentry and ministers, were penalized for enabling or attending these conventicles.

== Research Notes ==
* '''James Glasgow''' (b. ~late 1600s – d. unknown) may have held a position at Edinburgh Castle in 1738, as mentioned in ''The Principal Acts of the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland.''<ref>[https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_the-principal-acts-of-th_church-of-scotland-gene_1738/page/n19/mode/2up?q=%22James+Glasgow%22 ''The Principal Acts of the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland''], 1738 (Internet Archive)</ref>
* '''James Glasgow''' was a notable figure mentioned in legal proceedings during the turbulent times of the Covenanter movement in Scotland. In July 1670, he was fined for refusing to give his oath, alongside several others, as part of a crackdown on illegal religious gatherings known as field conventicles. These gatherings were a form of protest against the government's attempt to impose religious uniformity, particularly on those who adhered to Presbyterianism. James Glasgow is specifically noted as being from Whitecastle, a location associated with Covenanting activities during this period.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_the-history-of-the-state_crookshank-william_1751_1/page/284/mode/2up?q=%22James+Glasgow%22 ''The History of the Sufferings of the Church of Scotland from the Restoration to the Revolution''], by Robert Wodrow, 1721</ref>
**From the information provided in the images and context, '''Whitecastle''' is likely a location associated with the '''Covenanter''' activities, but the specific reference does not immediately clarify which Whitecastle it is. Given the widespread nature of the Covenanter movement in '''Scotland''', '''Whitecastle''' could plausibly be located in '''Lanarkshire''', '''Dumfriesshire''', or nearby areas known for strong Covenanter sympathies during the 17th century. The '''Lanarkshire''' region, specifically, was a hotspot for religious dissent during the Covenanting times, making it a strong candidate. However, without further geographic markers or historical maps, it's challenging to conclusively identify Whitecastle's exact location just from this.
**As for '''Mr. Duncan''', the mention of his name in the July 1671 proceedings involving the '''King's Advocate''' seems to tie him to some legal action related to the suppression of religious activities or nonconformity in religious practices. Without more context from the previous or following sections of the document, it's difficult to determine exactly who '''Mr. Duncan''' was. He could have been a local landowner, minister, or someone involved in harboring or protecting Covenanters, as many individuals were targeted during this period for their association with field conventicles.
**Further research into legal records or historical sources about '''Mr. Duncan''' in 1671 and '''Whitecastle''' in Covenanting Scotland would be required to offer a more precise identification.  Note, could be any of the other James Glasgow's in this timespan. No good match for location (Whitecastle) 
* On October 11, 1680, a James Glasgow is listed as a weaver in the Back of Lindsaylands, Parish of Biggar (Lanark Commissary Court, CC14/5/10). It is unclear if he is the same individual.

=== Current research ===

The asserted 29 January 1657 birth and placement as a son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan are unsupported and result from a record-role error. The profile's cited FamilySearch entry is for '''Marione Glesgow'''; "James Glesgow" appears in it as her father. It is not a baptism or birth record for a son James.

Glasgow-1376 was previously attached to the household. That relationship has been removed and should not be restored unless an independent record for a son James is found. The profile does not merge this profile into the father merely from the misread citation, because its later Whitecastle/Covenanter claims have not been shown to describe the Edinburgh weaver.

The proposed merge with [[Glasgow-2682|Glasgow-2682]] is also rejected. Glasgow-2682 is a documented father with Isobell Duffe from 1677 to 1691. The false 1657 birth on this profile supplies no matching identity fact, and no record connects the Whitecastle occurrence to the Duffe household.

This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YD-PRL FamilySearch index X1YD-PRL].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YD-PR2 FamilySearch index X1YD-PR2].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101 PDF p. 101].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource4">[https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_the-history-of-the-suffe_wodrow-robert_1721_1/page/n795/mode/2up?q=%22James+Glasgow%22 archive.org].</ref><ref name="ProjectSource5">[https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_the-principal-acts-of-th_church-of-scotland-gene_1738/page/n19/mode/2up?q=%22James+Glasgow%22 archive.org].</ref>

== Biography ==
The parentage and birth date for James Glasgow are not yet known. Based on the birth of his first known child in 1677, he was likely born by about 1657.

He was married to [[Duffe-18|Isobell Duffe]]. Her name is recorded as "Issobell Duff" or "Issobell Duffe" in the christening records of most of their children.

James and Issobell had the following children, all christened in Edinburgh Parish, Midlothian, Scotland:
* [[Glasgow-3088|Jean Glasgow]], christened 13 April 1677.<ref name="Jean1677">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPF-7YB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Jean Glasgow, 1677.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3103|James Glasgow]], christened 16 March 1679.<ref name="James1679">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-Q9J : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for James Glasgow, 1679.</ref> (See Research Notes regarding mother's name on this record).
* [[Glasgow-3368|James Glasgow]], christened 18 April 1680.<ref name="James1680">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-8S4 : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for James Glasgow, 1680.</ref> The christening of a second son with the same name strongly suggests the first James died in infancy.
* [[Glasgow-3284|Mary Glasgow]], christened 23 April 1682.<ref name="Mary1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQCM-LLH : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Mary Glasgow, 1682.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3285|Thomas Glasgow]], christened 13 November 1684.<ref name="Thomas1684">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-N9X : 11 February 2020), James Glascow in entry for Thomas Glascow, 1684.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-2681|Margaret Glasgow]], christened 20 March 1691.<ref name="Margaret1691">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FM3W-XBN : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for Margarett Glasgow, 1691.</ref>

The date and place of James's death are unknown, but he was alive as of March 1691.
== Research Notes ==
'''Identifying the parents of James Glasgow is a top research priority.''' Several contemporary men named James Glasgow who were also having children in Edinburgh at the same time have been investigated and ruled out as being the same person, though they are likely relatives (e.g., brothers or cousins). These include:
*   '''[[Glasgow-3098|James Glasgow (b. 1631)]]''', who was married to Bessie Whyte.
*   '''[[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow (b. bef. 1640)]]''', who was married to Helen Clerk.
*   '''[[Glasgow-3337|James Glasgow (b. ca. 1640)]]''', who was married to Annapill Glessie.

Since our James was consistently recorded with his wife, [[Duffe-18|Isobell Duffe]], it is highly unlikely he is the same person as any of the men listed above.

*   '''Parentage is Unknown:''' The parents of James are not yet confirmed. The original profile suggested he might descend from the Midlothian line of [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow (abt.1540-1580)]], perhaps as a son of [[Glasgow-1151|Johne Glasgow (1632-)]] or [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow (bef.1616-)]]. This is speculative and requires further research to find a primary source linking him to a father.
*   '''Conflicting Mother's Name:''' The 1679 christening record for his son [[Glasgow-3103|James]] lists the mother's name as "Elizabeth Duffe" instead of "Issobell". As all other children's records name her as Issobell, and given the commonality of clerical errors, it is most likely that "Elizabeth" was a mistake by the parish clerk.
*   '''Future Research:''' The highest priority is to find a marriage record for James Glasgow and Issobell Duffe in the Edinburgh parish registers, likely dated before April 1677. A search for burial records for both James and Issobell after March 1691 should also be conducted.

== Biography ==

Hugh Glasgow was probably born about 1705. This estimate is reportedly based on an inscription on a Glasgow family gravestone in St Cedma's churchyard, Larne.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

=== Residence and property in Larne ===

On 10 March 1736, Hugh Glasgow and [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], both of Larne, County Antrim, received a lease from Alexander, Earl of Antrim. Memorial 63221 was registered on 10 April 1738 at eleven in the morning.<ref name="lease">Registry of Deeds, Dublin, memorial 63221, lease dated 10 March 1736; registered 10 April 1738. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image 542], image group 008088380, volumes 87–88; original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The lease covered two tenements already in their possession on the north side of the street in Newtown, Larne. One had a frontage of 23 feet, bounded east by Mr Agnew's tenement and west by Robert Robinson's. The other had a frontage of 32 feet, bounded east by John Boyd's tenement and west by John White's. Both extended backwards 150 feet.<ref name="lease" />

The annual rent was £1 16 shillings sterling, with receiver's fees of two pence per pound. The term began on the preceding 1 November and was measured by the lives of George II, Frederick Prince of Wales and Prince William Augustus Duke of Cumberland, with provision for replacement lives. The named lives were royal family members, not Glasgow children.<ref name="lease" />

The lease witnesses were James Stenhouse of Larne and William Harrison, clerk to Alexander Stewart of Ballylough. Stenhouse and Robert Wilson of Larne, merchant, witnessed the memorial. Stenhouse proved execution at Carrickfergus on 28 March 1738, stating that Alexander Stewart had executed the lease in the Earl's name and that William and Hugh had executed the lease and memorial.<ref name="lease" />

The memorial names no parent, spouse or child of either lessee and states no relationship between them. The later renewal endorsements remain separate research targets.

=== Joint lessors named in a 1757 assignment ===

A deed poll dated 4 June 1757, Matthew Stewart of Carncastle, farmer, to Robert Rainey of Larne, weaver, concerned a conditional assignment for £20 of Stewart's interest in a lease granted by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne. The original memorial does not date their head lease or describe the holding sufficiently to identify it with the 1736 Newtown tenements.<ref name="JointLessors1757">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159181, manuscript pp. 473–474, deed dated 4 June 1757, registered 26 May 1761; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4 FamilySearch image 257, opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJP6 image 258, continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The joint names and Larne locality strongly support association with these lessees, but the record names no Glasgow relative or relationship between William and Hugh. Neither Glasgow executed this assignment; its registration in 1761 does not prove that either was then living. The separate 1751 and 1767 endorsements to the 1736 lease remain unexamined and may identify replacement lives.<ref>PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A, 1736 William and Hugh Glasgow lease with 1751 and 1767 endorsements; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI eCatalogue], catalogue description only.</ref>

=== Church ===

A family chronology states that Hugh Glasgow became an elder of the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation in 1741.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

A nineteenth-century account quoting the Larne Session Book includes Hugh Glasgow among the members of the Session and records that he died on 8 July 1767.<ref name="death">[https://archive.org/stream/christianunitari0003unse/christianunitari0003unse_djvu.txt “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,”] ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), p. 197. The account quotes the Larne Session Book entry: “Hugh Glasgow … dead July 8, 1767.”</ref>

Hugh therefore died on 8 July 1767, provided that the elder named in the Session Book was the same Hugh Glasgow who held the 1736 Larne lease.<ref name="death" />

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible son John of Larne ===

[[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]], who married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] at Larne in 1769, is a possible son, with low confidence. His estimated birth about 1747 fits Hugh's age and Larne household, but the marriage chronology does not name John's father.<ref>Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Kilwaughter and Larne Glasgow chronology], entry for John Glasgow and Rose Allan's 1769 marriage. The birth estimate of 1745–48 is the compiler's estimate.</ref> The relationship is a working hypothesis and is marked uncertain. [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remains an alternative father. No evidence establishes that Hugh's wife Ann was John's mother.

The Larne memorial gives Hugh's death as 8 July 1767 aged 62 and commemorates members of his family, but does not name John. It has not been established as a complete enumeration of surviving children, so the omission neither proves nor excludes the proposed relationship.<ref>''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'', ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Glasgow stone at Larne], pp. 47–48.</ref> Further tests include the original registers (PRONI MIC/1B/6) and the renewal endorsements to the 1736 lease (PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A).


=== Possible duplicate ===

This profile may represent the same person as [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1706-abt.1760)]]. A merger should not be completed until the conflicting death information and the other relationships attached to the two profiles have been examined. The Larne Session Book supports a death date of 8 July 1767 rather than about 1760.<ref name="death" />

=== Possible Dublin baptism ===

A Hugh Glascoe was baptised in Dublin in 1704, the son of William Glascoe and Jone.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FR3H-8L7 FamilySearch record for Hugh Glascoe].</ref>

No evidence currently establishes that the child baptised in Dublin was the later Hugh Glasgow of Larne. The similar name and approximate date are not enough by themselves to identify them as the same person.

=== 1740 Protestant householder ===

A Hugh Glasgow appears in the 1740 list of Protestant householders for Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish.<ref>[https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PRONI-T808-15258 Virtual Treasury of Ireland, PRONI T808/15258, Names of Protestant Householders, 1740].</ref>

The identification is uncertain. The 1736 lease places Hugh Glasgow in Larne, and the church evidence also associates a man of that name with Larne. The Tamlaght O'Crilly entry should therefore remain a possible identification, not a confirmed event in his life.

=== Duneane surname ambiguity ===
The 1740 Duneane return includes Henry Glads. The reading may represent another surname and is not securely Glasgow. It is retained only as east-Antrim surname context and is not evidence that Henry was this Hugh or a relative.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Underlying record source: henry glads duneane 1740].</ref>

=== Mortgage with Hugh Shutter, 1749 ===

A mortgage dated 6 November 1749 records William Eakine of Larne conveying Old Town premises as security to Hugh Shutter and Hugh Glasgow. Hugh Glasgow is described as a merchant of Larne and executed the memorial. The underlying lease was dated 11 August 1748.<ref name="HughMortgage1749">Registry of Deeds, memorial 97407, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG FamilySearch image 449], original manuscript inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

Place, date and occupation strongly favour this Hugh. The deed establishes a Glasgow–Shutter business association before the reported 1762 marriage of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] to Janet Shutter, but names no relationship and proves neither that marriage nor Hugh’s parentage of James or [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]].

== Biography ==

'''Hugh Glasgow''' was a weaver in County Antrim. His birth date is unknown; he was born before about 1802 based on the known ages of his children.

Three original civil marriage registers name children of a father called Hugh Glasgow, weaver:

* [[Glasgow-3957|Mary Glasgow]], who married [[Montgomery-14069|Thomas Montgomery]] on 13 September 1862, expressly named her father as Hugh Glasgow, weaver.<ref name="MaryMarriage1862">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/09623/5489617.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Thomas Montgomery and Mary Glasgow, 13 September 1862.</ref> This parent-child relationship is direct and confident.
* [[Glasgow-4048|Hugh Glasgow]], aged 23 and a weaver of Liminary, married Ann Wilson on 24 December 1852 and named his father as Hugh Glasgow, weaver.<ref name="HughMarriage1852">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-4047|Eliza Glasgow]], aged 21 and of Liminary, married William Montgomery on 21 August 1854 and named her father as Hugh Glasgow, labourer and weaver.<ref name="ElizaMarriage1854">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1854/09463/5428881.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], William Montgomery and Eliza Glasgow, 21 August 1854.</ref>

The matching father name and occupation prove each child's relationship to a Hugh Glasgow. Hugh junior and Eliza also shared the Liminary residence, strongly indicating that they were siblings. Mary may have been their older sister, but her register gives a different residence and the common name does not by itself prove that all three records identify one father.

== Research Notes ==

=== Relationship to Robert Glasgow ===

Hugh is currently attached as an uncertain son of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]. That relationship is not proved. Robert's 1851 Glenleslie household contained an unmarried niece Mary Glasgow, aged 34 and a linen weaver.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/23/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Glenleslie household 23.</ref> She is a strong candidate for the Mary who later named Hugh as her father. If they were the same woman, Hugh was more probably Robert's brother or another collateral relative than his son. No record inspected names Hugh's parents or explicitly calls Hugh and Robert brothers.

== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}}

'''Robert Glasgow''' was a farmer at '''Glenleslie, Dunaghy, County Antrim'''. His recorded age of seventy-two in the 1851 census places his birth about '''1779'''. The same return gives County Antrim as his birthplace.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, barony of Kilconway, parish of Dunaghy, Glenleslie, household 23. [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/23/ National Archives of Ireland, legacy household locator]. Detailed transcription: [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], printed p. 103, Glenleslie household 23. The transcription, including its absent-member and death entries, was examined; the full original return was not re-examined for this revision.</ref>

He married '''Catherine''', whose maiden name has not been established. Their census return gives '''1803''' as the marriage year. Catherine was sixty-eight in 1851, born in County Antrim, and worked at spinning flax.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== Household and family in 1851 ===

Robert and Catherine occupied household 23 at Glenleslie. The seven people recorded as present were:<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

|+ '''Glenleslie household 23: residents in 1851'''
|-
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Name
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Relationship to Robert
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Age
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Occupation or status
|-
| '''Robert Glasgow''' || Head || 72 || Farmer; could read; married in 1803
|-

|-

|-

|-
