|}

All seven were recorded as born in County Antrim. Two further family members were entered as '''absent in America''': '''John Glasgow''', Robert's son, aged forty and a labourer; and '''Samuel Glasgow''', his son, aged thirty and a linen weaver. They should not be counted among the residents physically present at Glenleslie.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

The death section records '''Catherine Hume''', Robert's granddaughter, who died of scarlatina in '''spring 1850''', aged '''three months'''. Her parents are not identified in the entry.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

The census therefore identifies '''Margaret, John and Samuel''' as Robert's children. His will independently identifies Margaret as his daughter and James and Mary Young as Margaret's children. It does not follow that these were his only children.<ref name="RobertWill">Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie, will dated 3 February 1851, proved 13 February 1854; National Archives of Ireland copy, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ8-MQQJ?view=fullText FamilySearch, image 229]. Will details are retained from the earlier research transcription supplied for this profile; the image was not independently re-examined during this revision.</ref>

=== Will and death ===

Robert made his will at '''Glenleslie on 3 February 1851'''. He left his farm, livestock, furniture and farming utensils to his daughter [[Glasgow-3955|Margaret Glasgow]] for life. After her death, the property was to be divided equally between her children '''James Young''' and [[Young-78755|Mary Young]]. The named executors were '''Andrew McCaughey''' and '''John Kirk'''.<ref name="RobertWill" />

The probate notation states that he died '''in or about 1852'''. The will was proved on '''13 February 1854'''. These details support an approximate death in 1852, not an exact death date or a separately verified place of death.<ref name="RobertWill" />

The earlier research also identified a PRONI index entry for Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie among the '''Connor Diocesan Wills, 1854'''. The date of the will, the approximate death year and the probate year are distinct events.<ref name="PRONI1854">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Name Search, ''Pre-1858 Wills and Admons'', Connor Diocesan Wills: Robert Glasgow, Glenleslie, 1854. [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search]. Entry details retained from the earlier profile's recorded search of 5 August 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Proposed son: Robert Glasgow of Donbought ===

The younger [[Glasgow-1049|Robert Glasgow]], a forty-year-old linen weaver living with his wife Margaret at Donbought in 1851, remains a '''plausible son or close relative'''. The attached father-son relationship should remain '''uncertain''': neither census household states a relationship between the two men.<ref name="Donbought1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy, Donbought, household 16. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf Detailed comma-delimited transcription], printed p. 100. Compare W. Scott and W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], printed pp. 77-78, references 7883-7890. These are transcriptions of the same census, not independent family records.</ref>

The proposed connection rests on compatible ages, the same parish, a possible earlier Doonbought holding and a reported same-name occurrence in the will. None presently identifies the younger Robert as this Robert's son.

'''The 1825 tithe entry.''' W. Macafee's transcription lists '''Robert Glasco''' at '''Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2]''', Dunaghy, in 1825. The compiler standardises the surname as Glasgow. The entry is on printed page 41, compiler's index '''5804'''; that number is not an original property-lot number.<ref name="Tithe1825">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering the Baronies of Cary, Dunluce and Kilconway in North Antrim plus the Barony of N. E. Liberties, Co. Londonderry''], surname order, dated 17 October 2016, printed p. 41, index 5804: Robert Glasco, Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2], Dunaghy, 1825. Transcription, not an inspected original tithe-book image.</ref> This Robert would have been about forty-six, whereas the younger man would have been about fourteen. The Glenleslie farmer is therefore a better chronological candidate for the 1825 entry. However, the entry supplies no age, wife, children or connection to Glenleslie. Identifying him with the tithe occupier does not, by itself, prove that the younger Robert was his son or succeeded to the same holding.

'''The reported will witness.''' The earlier will transcription lists '''Robert Glasgow, John Hamill, Robert Kirk and Thomas Matter''' as witnesses. It does not identify the same-name Robert as the Donbought man or describe him as a son. The original attestation and signature layout should be checked before treating this as an independently identified second Robert; in particular, a testator's signature must not be mistaken for a witness entry. No correction to the earlier transcription is asserted here.<ref name="RobertWill" />

'''The will is not a complete list of children.''' John and Samuel are named as sons in the census but are not among the beneficiaries in the supplied will summary. The absence of the younger Robert from that summary therefore does not disprove the proposed relationship. Equally, an incomplete beneficiary list cannot be used to prove an additional child.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" /><ref name="RobertWill" />

The father-son link could be strengthened by a documented land succession, a church entry, or an independently established relationship between the younger Robert and one of this man's proved children. A direct statement is not the only possible route to a conclusion, but the present indirect evidence does not yet distinguish a son from another relative or namesake.

=== Margaret and the Glenleslie holding ===

The Dunaghy index to Griffith's Valuation lists '''Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie''' and, separately, '''Robert Glasgow at Doonbought'''.<ref name="GriffithDunaghy">[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/dunaghy.php Fáilte Romhat, Griffith's Valuation index, Dunaghy parish, County Antrim], entries for Margaret Glasgow, Glenleslie, and Robert Glasgow, Doonbought. Name-and-townland index; original valuation pages, plot references and revision entries have not been inspected.</ref> The Margaret entry is consistent with the will's provision for his daughter, but her identity and the precise holding remain to be established. This is a possible continuation of the '''Glenleslie''' farm, not proof of father-son succession at '''Doonbought'''.

=== Marriage and age discrepancy ===

Margaret's census age of fifty suggests a birth about 1800 or 1801, slightly before Robert and Catherine's reported marriage in 1803. Either age or marriage year may be inaccurate, or there may be an explanation not recorded in the surviving evidence. The discrepancy remains unresolved; no earlier marriage or different mother has been established.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== Identification of the emigrant sons ===

The census establishes that Robert had sons John and Samuel in America in 1851; it does not establish their later residences, wives or children. The earlier attachment of [[Glasgow-3140|John Glasgow]] to the Elizabeth Fee and County Armagh family remains unproved. Robert's absent son John must also be distinguished from the forty-year-old nephew in [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]]'s nearby household 21: that nephew was present at Glenleslie, was a linen weaver and had married in 1839.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

[[Glasgow-1053|Margaret (Glasgow) Winters]], associated with a Canadian family, has not been identified with Robert's unmarried daughter at Glenleslie. Their profiles should not be merged on the strength of their common name.

=== Mary Glasgow, niece, and the Hugh Glasgow lead ===

The thirty-four-year-old niece may be [[Glasgow-3957|Mary (Glasgow) Montgomery]]. The earlier civil-register research records that Mary's marriage to Thomas Montgomery on '''13 September 1862''' named her father as '''Hugh Glasgow, weaver'''. Her death on '''22 March 1898''' gives an age consistent with birth about 1818, close to the census niece's estimated birth about 1816 or 1817.<ref name="MaryMarriage1862">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Thomas Montgomery and Mary Glasgow, 13 September 1862: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/09623/5489617.pdf register image]. Record details retained from the earlier profile's research.</ref><ref name="MaryDeath1898">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, Mary Montgomery, 22 March 1898: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1898/05842/4654852.pdf register image]. Record details retained from the earlier profile's research.</ref>

This remains an identification to test, not proof that Hugh was Robert's brother. The census niece relationship does not identify the connecting parent, and a relationship through Catherine must also be considered.

A Hugh Glasgow, weaver, was also named as father in the Liminary-associated marriages of '''Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852''', and '''Eliza Glasgow and William Montgomery, 21 August 1854'''. Mary may belong to that family, but the common paternal name and occupation do not establish the connection.<ref name="HughMarriage1852">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf register image]. Earlier research comparison.</ref><ref name="ElizaMarriage1854">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, William Montgomery and Eliza Glasgow, 21 August 1854: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1854/09463/5428881.pdf register image]. Earlier research comparison.</ref>

=== Robert's parents and earlier hypotheses ===

'''Robert's parents remain unidentified.''' The County Antrim birthplace comes from his census return; a previously reported County Tyrone birthplace has no supporting source in this profile.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

[[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and Rose of Inishrush were previously suggested as his parents, but the attachment is not retained. Adam's reported birth about 1758 makes the paternal chronology possible, while Rose's reported birth about 1767 would make her about twelve at Robert's birth. That is a serious chronological difficulty, not evidence of maternity. Their documented County Londonderry association also supplies no link to Robert's County Antrim family.

The proposal drew on the incomplete family named on Adam and Rose's gravestone and a notice describing Nancy Glasgow as Adam's '''sixth daughter'''. Those sources show that some of Adam's children are not named on the stone; neither identifies Robert as one of them.<ref name="AdamGrave">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ ''Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower Graveyard''], Glasgow gravestone transcription and photograph naming Rose, wife of Adam Glasgow; Adam; daughter Eliza; son James; and grandson William. Source retained from the earlier research.</ref><ref name="NancyMarriage">[https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/ ''Marriage Notices 1840-42''], notice published 29 January 1842: John Kyle of Tyanee married Nancy, sixth daughter of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush, on 14 January 1842. Source retained from the earlier research.</ref>

[[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] of Glenleslie was another proposed father. No record establishes that relationship. Robert's birth also precedes John and Rose Alexander's reported 1791 marriage, although that alone would not exclude an earlier marriage. Household proximity is not sufficient evidence of parentage.

=== Namesakes and other unproved connections ===

* '''Coltrim:''' [[Glasgow-3941|Robert Glasgow of Coltrim]] is separately associated with Coltrim, Lissan, between 1820 and 1831. No inspected record bridges him to Robert and Catherine at Glenleslie.
* '''Lisnagaver:''' the Robert Glasgow in the 1834 Rasharkin tithe material has not been identified with this man. The older John and Samuel of Lisnagaver must not be substituted for Robert's much younger sons of those names.
* '''Gortereghy:''' this man, whose death is placed about 1852, cannot simply be treated as the later occupier. [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]], whose 1866 marriage names his father as Alexander, is the stronger existing candidate for the later Lisnagaver-Gortereghy identity.<ref name="Robert938Marriage">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Robert Glasgow and Jane Graham, 1866: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1866/11531/8240963.pdf register image]. Identification comparison retained from earlier research.</ref>
* '''Possible duplicate:''' [[Glasgow-2963|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1780 and attached to [[Glasgow-1142|James Glasgow]] and [[Simpson-19200|Jean Simpson]], has not been connected to Catherine or the Glenleslie household. A merge is not supported at present.

Earlier possibilities involving [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]], born about 1725; [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1690; [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow]], born about 1706; and [[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1710, remain unconnected hypotheses. Previously reported FamilyTreeDNA relationship-distance figures, RDist 3 and GDist 6, do not establish a documentary chain to any particular couple.

The Blair extracts of the ''Belfast Newsletter'' list William, John, James and Robert Glasgow on 7 April 1772. These are earlier surname occurrences, not evidence of this Robert's parentage.<ref name="Belfast1772">[https://www.kinsleuth.com/belnews/1770-1779.htm ''Blair Extracts from the Belfast Newsletter, 1770-1779''], 7 April 1772, p. 3. Source retained from the earlier profile.</ref>

=== Relationship assessment ===

The recorded household and the supplied will transcription support Catherine as Robert's wife; Margaret, John and Samuel as his children; Mary and James Young as Margaret's children and his grandchildren; Mary Glasgow as his niece; and Catherine Hume as his granddaughter through an unidentified parent. Identification of James Young with [[Young-23682|James Young]] remains unproved. The proposed younger son [[Glasgow-1049|Robert Glasgow]], Robert's own parents and the wider family links remain uncertain.

=== Original census and working father, 23 October 2026 ===

The original 1851 Glenleslie household 21 return records John Glasgow as 100, Rose as 80, and 1791 for both. Its marriage heading asks “In what Year Married, or in what Years if more than once?” The detailed transcription’s first-marriage field is therefore an editorial description, not the literal question on this return. Only 1791 is entered: an earlier union is not documented, and the request for multiple years means its absence still weighs against a straightforward earlier-marriage explanation. The original also calls the forty-year-old John a nephew and gives his occupation as vagrant; the 1839 marriage belongs to him. The mortality table explicitly calls Andrew Glasgow, a thirty-year-old linen weaver who died of consumption in winter 1848, a son of the head. It does not name Andrew’s mother.

Select John Glasgow-1022 as the possible working father of the Glenleslie Robert represented by Glasgow-1367, at 38% subjective confidence. The original makes their reported age difference 28 years (100 versus 72), a comfortable father–son interval. They were Antrim-born Glasgow farmers in Glenleslie households 21 and 23, separated by the Hamill household. This is a specific nearby older family, and John is the best identified local father comparison already retained in the research. Reading the original marriage question removes the previous overstatement that it expressly records a first marriage in 1791. The combined generation and neighbouring-family argument is sufficient to select a weak working model rather than leave this preferred named comparison outside the tree; it is not a parent statement.

=== Prescott sibling family reviewed 18 October 2026 ===
John Glasgow, Prescott watchmaker with wife Jane in deed B13, is selected as Robert [[Glasgow-4150]]’s brother at 98% subjective confidence. Robert’s 1849 will gives brother John one sixth. John and Jane’s 1856 deed transfers an undivided one sixth of the same Dibble Street lots to Samuel, who is another will-named brother. The exact locality, buyer, parcels and fraction identify the grantor strongly; B13 does not itself expressly call John Robert’s brother. John’s birth, death and parents are not named, and his identity with an existing John profile is unresolved.

Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow, is Robert’s sister at 99% subjective confidence: C298 expressly states that relationship and traces her six children’s interests to Robert’s will, which names his sister Mary. Her children were John Black and Rose Ann Black of Drumoolish, Jane Miller and Agnes Black of Newburgh, Thomasina Montgomery of Legrand, Iowa, and Elizabeth Black, formerly of Newburgh. John’s wife Martha, Jane’s husband Robert Miller and Thomasina’s husband Mathew Montgomery also joined. Elizabeth, not Mary, is expressly deceased unmarried and intestate; her five siblings convey her share as heirs. Mary’s own birth, death, residence and husband’s forename remain unknown.

Extend the existing Alexander [[Glasgow-3904]] father hypothesis to John and Mary at 27%, uncertain, conditional on their documented membership in the Prescott sibling family. Thomas-987 and Daniel-3896 already carry this father, and Samuel-4010 and Robert-4150 already have the same selected uncertain hypothesis. Its basis remains the single late descendant tradition naming Alexander as Thomas’s father, with compatible generation and sibling inference. The original will and deeds name no parent. These two extensions supply no independent parent testimony and do not raise the existing estimate; no mother is selected.

These are two previously unstructured record accounts recovered from evidence already researched in September, not two newly discovered sources or two proven additional distinct people. John retains six unselected compatible or weak existing-profile comparisons; later residence, spouse or death elsewhere is not by itself an exclusion of a possible migrant. No Mary Black/Glasgow match is established in the bounded local historical catalogue check. Both accounts remain on identity hold before any new WikiTree profile creation. Record dates are not birth dates.

Resolve John against the retained profile candidates using Jane, his watchmaking trade and the exact Prescott household. Compare the six Black children’s Irish and North American records for an identification of Mary and her husband. A contemporary source naming a parent remains the decisive question for Alexander; the later accounts cannot be counted twice.<ref name="PrescottSiblingReview18Oct2026">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S Robert Glasgow’s will, B12, 9 October 1849, registered 13 November 1856; volume B, pp. 9–10, images 35–36]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 John and Jane Glasgow to Samuel, B13, 30 October 1856, registered 13 November 1856; volume B, pp. 10–11, image 36]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K Mary Black’s children to Mary Eno Glasgow, C298, 15 September 1869, registered 1 July 1870; volume C, pp. 477–482, images 277–280]. Glasgow-4150.remote_wikitext: {{Estimated Date}} [[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was an early shipbuilder at Prescott, Upper Canada, later Canada West. Prescott heritage material identifies him as the builder of the Centre Street house now known as Glasgow House.Town of Prescott, [https://www.prescott.ca/media/3dtiztjk/council-agenda-june-16-2025.pdf ''Council Agenda, 16 June 2025''], heritage-designation material for 388 Centre Street, “Glasgow House.” A later property history dates the building to about 1835.Theresa Taylor, [https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf “Auction all for others,”] ''Brockville Recorder & Times'', 22 February 2017. Robert made his will on 9 October 1849. The registered copy divides his estate into six shares: one each for his brothers Daniel, [[Glasgow-4010|Samuel]], John and Thomas Glasgow, one collectively for the children of his brother James, and one for his sister Mary Glasgow.FamilySearch, ''Land records of Grenville County, 1822–1955'', film 008200419, image 35, registered copy of the will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated October 1849 and registered in 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S image 3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S]; original image inspected 8 September 2026. The explicit sibling language makes Samuel Robert's brother, not his son. The later statement that Robert left the house to six “children” and that a son Samuel acquired the other shares appears to have misread the six-share title chain. Local history reports that Robert died at Prescott in 1856. The 1856 date is compatible with an 1849 will: 1849 is the date on which the will was made, while 1856 is the reported death and registration period. == Research Notes == === The 1842 census lead === A modern index reports a Robert Glasgow in Augusta in the 1842 Canada West census. The image formerly cited for that claim, frame 004569584_00050, was inspected at full resolution and contains no readable Robert Glasgow entry.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1842&op=img&id=004569584_00050 1842 Census of Canada West, image 004569584_00050], inspected 13 August 2026. It is not used here as evidence for Robert's identity. === Family interpretation === The will's named beneficiaries are Robert's siblings and the children of one brother. It does not name Robert's parents, spouse or children. The 30 July 1861 conveyance, B465, identifies the will’s Daniel as the Kilrea watchmaker and Thomas as the Lisnagaver farmer, with wives Margaret and Mary Anne. This establishes the Irish sibling identities when read with the will; it does not name their parents or identify Alexander of Lisnagaver as another brother.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D Prescott land register, volume B, memorial 465, pp.397–398, DGS 008200419, images 240–241]. The 1861 deed identifies the brothers as [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel of Kilrea]] and [[Glasgow-987|Thomas of Lisnagaver]]. The original 15 September 1869 deed, C298, identifies the sister as Mary Black, formerly Glasgow, and names six children, including John and Rose Ann Black of Drumoolish.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K Prescott land register, volume C, memorial 298, pp.476–482, DGS 008200420, images 277–280]. John of Prescott, watchmaker, remains an unassigned profile identity. James the Prescott carpenter is a property-based comparison for brother James, but their identity is not yet proved; the will does not say James was deceased. Robert's actual birthplace is unknown. His birth is estimated only far enough before about 1835 for him to have worked as a shipbuilder and built the house. His brother Samuel was recorded as Irish-born in the original 1851 Prescott census.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1851&op=img&id=e002351566 1851 Census of Canada West, Prescott, page 31, lines 11–18, image e002351566], Samuel Glasgow household. Ireland is therefore a usable uncertain creation-field location from Robert's documented immediate-family context; it is not a statement that Robert's birthplace has been found. Prescott should be entered as an uncertain death place from the local history, not as a birthplace. === Duplicate audit === The local One Tree export, current project index and live WikiTree name results were reviewed in August and September 2026. No compatible Prescott shipbuilder profile was found. [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]], [[Glasgow-1171|Robert Glasgow of New York]], [[Glasgow-1983|Robert Glasgow of South Carolina]], [[Glasgow-1189|Robert Glasgow of Ohio]] and [[Glasgow-2769|Robert Glasgow of Tennessee]] have incompatible documented lives. Create Robert unconnected; the sibling link to Samuel can be expressed in the biographies until their parents are identified. == Sources ==

== Biography ==
John Glasgow was christened in 1649 in the parish of Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-3610|John Glasgow]].<ref name="Birth1649">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-X6G : 16 September 2021), Johne Glasgow, 1649.</ref> His known siblings included [[Glasgow-3112|Margaret Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3118|Alexander Glasgow]].{{Citation needed }}

He married '''[[Currie-4998|Margaret Currie]]''' in 1673 in Kirknewton.<ref name="Marriage1673">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9W-J5Q : 11 February 2020), Johne Glasgow, 1673.</ref>

Sometime after their marriage, the family moved to the neighboring parish of Glencorse, Midlothian, where their known children were christened.

John and Margaret had the following children:
* [[Glasgow-3011|Robert Glasgow]], christened 29 December 1676 in Glencorse.<ref name="Robert1676">Old Parish Registers, Baptisms, Glencorse, Midlothian. Ref: 687/ FR11.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3013|William Glasgow]], christened 26 December 1680 in Glencorse.<ref name="William1680">Old Parish Registers, Baptisms, Glencorse, Midlothian. Ref: 687/ FR16.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3085|Margaret Glasgow]], christened 13 April 1684 in Glencorse.<ref name="Margaret1684">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-FXD : 16 September 2021), John Glaskow in entry for Margarat Glaskow, 1684.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-2917|Charles James Glasgow]], christened 3 October 1686 in Glencorse.<ref name="Charles1686">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4J-JJK : 16 September 2021), John Glesgowe in entry for Charles Glesgowe, 1686.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
Sources are needed to confirm these sibling relationships.

'''Spelling Variations'''
The parish records show variations in the spelling of the family's names. The father is recorded as John Glaskow and John Glesgowe, and the mother as Margaret Corrie. These phonetic spellings were common due to varying literacy and local dialects.

'''Marriage and Residency'''
The marriage record places the couple in Kirknewton in 1673, while the baptismal records for all known children place them in the neighboring parish of Glencorse from 1676 onward. This indicates a move shortly after their marriage.

=== Supplied parish index comparison ===

The supplied Scotland’s People index records '''JOHNE GLASGOW''' on '''22/04/1649''' at Kirknewton and East Calder, with parent text “JOHNE GLASGOW/ FR15 (FR15)”.<ref name="OPRBirth046">Scotland’s People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms], exact surname Glasgow through 1700, index text supplied 10 September 2026: JOHNE GLASGOW, 22/04/1649, JOHNE GLASGOW/ FR15 (FR15), indexed gender M, Kirknewton and East Calder, parish 690, reference 10 / 14. Original register image not inspected for this review.</ref>

The profile’s structured birth date is 1649-04-04, whereas this index date is 1649-04-22. The two dates remain unreconciled. The combined births and baptisms collection does not establish whether the indexed date is a birthday or a baptism date. A parent’s name alone does not uniquely identify an attached historical person, and the index does not establish an unnamed parent.

'''⚠️ Paleographic Warning:''' This profile is based on a testament written in 16th-century Secretary Hand. Due to the ornate and inconsistent handwriting style, all names, places, and relationships should be considered '''tentative''' and subject to '''revision''' pending further document comparison or corroboration. Interpretations are paleographically informed but speculative. == Biography == '''Archibald Glasgow''' was baptized on 20 March 1618 in South Leith, Edinburghshire, the son of [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow (bef.1600–)]] and [[Fraser-15286|Catherine (Fraser) Glasgow (1600–)]]."Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FQM4-LYL : 12 February 2020), Archbald Glascow, 1618. === Parentage === Four records identify Archibald as the son of [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow]], mealmaker in Leith. His 1618 baptism names William as his father. On 23 October 1639 the Edinburgh apprentice register called Archibald the son of William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith, when he was apprenticed to Thomas Park, cordiner.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583-1666'', Scottish Record Society 28 (1906), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up p. 71], 23 October 1639. William's testament dative, confirmed on 22 July 1646, says that William died in September 1644 and was given up by Archibald Glasgow, his lawful son and sole executor dative.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/62, images 461–462, testament dative and inventory of William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith, confirmed 22 July 1646; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search]. On 1 May 1647 Archibald was served heir to William; the retour abstract again described Archibald as a shoemaker in Leith and William as a mealmaker there, expressly calling William his father.Great Britain Record Commission, ''Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum... Abbreviatio'', vol. 2 (1811), Inquisitiones Generales, no. 3278, 1 May 1647, original retour xix.128, [https://archive.org/details/inquisitionumadc00grea_0 Internet Archive]. He is possibly the same '''Archibald Glasgow''' who appears in multiple mid-17th century records associated with Leith: * On 14 April 1646, Archibald Glasgow married '''Margaret Hilstones''' in South Leith.Scotland Marriages 1561–1910, OPR Marriages, South Leith, 692/2, 90/310. Entry: Archbald Glasgow and Margaret Hilstones, 14 April 1646. * A child named [[Glasgow-2714|George Glasgow (bef.1658–)]] was born in 1658 in South Leith to parents named '''Archibald Glasgow''' and '''Agnes Watson'''."Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FQMH-CXH : 12 February 2020), Georg Glasgowe, 1658. This may indicate a second marriage or a clerical discrepancy in the mother’s recorded name. * On 24 May 1662, an '''Archibald Glasgow, maltman and indweller in Leith''' is referenced in a testament recorded in the Edinburgh Commissary Court (CC8/8/70). This legal record, associated with the inventory of his estate, confirms his occupation and residency in Leith during this period. Given the overlap of dates, location, and naming patterns, it is plausible that all these records refer to the same individual—'''Archibald Glasgow, maltman of Leith'''—though further evidence is needed to confirm each connection definitively.
::Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/70 ::GLASGOWE ::ARCHBALD ::MARGARET HILSTONES/FR3086 (FR3086) ::14/04/1646 ::692 / 2 ::90 / 310 ::Leith South
The testament testamentar and inventar of the goods gear, sums of money and debts pertaining to umquhile Archibald Glasgow, maltman and indweller in Glasgow, who deceased in the month of February last bypast 1662, faithfully made and given up by himself upon the xxix day of May the year of God above written in so far as concerns the nomination of his executors testamentar, and a part of the debts owed to him, and given up by Agnes Watson his relict spouse, taking burden upon her in name and behalf of Archibald, George, and William Glasgows, minors being lawful to the said umquhile defunct, in so far as concerns the whole rest of his goods, gear, debts, etc., and to him and as to the profit of the debts owed to him called and belonging... == Biography ==

John Glasgow was born about 1794 (exact birthplace not yet proven). He worked as a farmer and was recorded in '''Drumgreenagh''' townland, Derrynoose parish, County Armagh, in 1839.<ref name="Freeholders1839">"Ireland, Ulster Freeholders," entry for '''John Glasgow''', farmer, Drumgreenagh, Armagh, 1839; reference T/808/14961, vol. 123, p. 1, line 151.</ref>

A holding at Drumgreenagh/Killyreavy associated with the Glasgow name appears again in the land valuation compiled 1 Dec 1864 (after John’s death), with landlord '''William Kirk'''.<ref name="Griffiths1864">''Ireland, Griffith’s Valuation, 1847–1864'', Derrynoose parish (Killyreavy/Drumgreenagh), entry dated 1 Dec 1864; occupier recorded as Glasgow; landlord William Kirk.</ref>

Known children—identified from Irish civil marriage records that name their father as '''John Glasgow'''—include:
* '''Mary Jane Glasgow''', married '''Samuel Boyd''' on 15 Jun 1854 at Derrynoose, County Armagh.<ref name="Mary1854">"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," marriage of '''Samuel Boyd''' & '''Mary Jane Glasgow''', 15 Jun 1854, Derrynoose, Armagh; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGV8-X359</ref><ref>"Ireland, Marriages, 1619–1898," index entry naming father '''John Glasgow'''; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGXJ-4YD</ref>
* '''Sarah Anne Glasgow''', married '''James Sloan''' on 5 Dec 1862 (record names her father as '''John Glasgow''').<ref name="Sarah1862">"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," marriage of '''James Sloan''' & '''Sarah Anne Glasgow''', 5 Dec 1862; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGV8-J5BV</ref>
* '''Elizabeth Glasgow''', married '''Thomas Lennon''' on 15 Jan 1868 (indexed also as '''Glasson''' and '''Leemon''').<ref name="Elizabeth1868">"Ireland, Marriages, 1619–1898," marriage of '''Thomas Lennon''' & '''Elizabeth Glasgow''', 15 Jan 1868; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGZ6-YGT</ref><ref>"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," variant index ('''Elizabeth Glasson''' to '''Thomas Leemon'''), 15 Jan 1868; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGY7-Z684</ref>

John is reported to have died on '''30 Apr 1849''' (citation still needed).
A marriage for Elizabeth Glasgow and Leemon was registered on 15 January 1868 in the Armagh district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 15 January 1868, Armagh district, M/1868/Q1/86/2/26.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
* '''Residence & Land''' — The 1839 freeholder entry for a farmer '''John Glasgow''' in Drumgreenagh aligns with later valuation evidence in Killyreavy/Drumgreenagh, Derrynoose parish, where the landlord was '''William Kirk'''. The 1864 valuation date is post-mortem for John and likely reflects continuity of the family holding rather than John himself.<ref name="Freeholders1839" /><ref name="Griffiths1864" />
* '''Children''' — Mary Jane (1854), Sarah Anne (1862), and Elizabeth (1868) are securely linked as his children via marriage records that explicitly name their father as '''John Glasgow'''. Additional Glasgow marriages in the area (e.g., a '''Samuel Glasgow''' indexed 23 Mar 1870) may indicate further children; evidence not yet evaluated.
* '''Name & Place Variants''' — Surname appears as '''Glasgow''' and occasionally '''Glasson''' in indexes; bridegroom Lennon is indexed as '''Lennon/Leemon'''. Townland appears as '''Drumgreenagh/Drumgreeney''' within the civil parish of '''Derrynoose''' (sometimes written '''Killyreavy''').
* '''To Do''' — Seek Church of Ireland or Presbyterian registers for Derrynoose/Keady area for baptisms and burial; consult PRONI Freeholders books, Tithe Applotment (1820s–1830s), and Valuation Revision Books for chain of occupancy; locate primary source for the stated death date (30 Apr 1849).

=== Earlier Drumgreenagh namesake ===
A deed made on 13 February 1786 identifies [[Glasgow-4031|an older John Glasgow]] as a farmer at Drumgreenagh and husband of Jane Murphy. He cannot be this profile, who was born about 1794. The shared residence makes an older-family relationship plausible, but the deed names no child and does not prove that the older John was this John's father.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial of deed of assignment, David Murphy to John Glasgow, deed dated 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD FamilySearch image].</ref>

An 1828 probate-index entry also names John Glasgow of Drumgreenagh, County Armagh. This profile was later documented in the same townland, but his 1849 death prevents treating an 1828 administration as his death without inspecting the record type. The entry may concern the older namesake, but that identity is not yet proved.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Names, Pre-1858 Wills and Admons search], John Glasgow, Drumgreenagh, 1828.</ref>

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was a farmer at '''Drumgreenagh, County Armagh'''. A deed of assignment dated 13 February 1786 identifies his wife as '''Jane Murphy''', daughter of the late '''Thomas Murphy'''. The deed recites that Thomas died intestate leaving a widow and five children, and that a one-fifth share of land at Lislea fell to Jane.<ref name="Deed1786">Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial of deed of assignment, David Murphy to John Glasgow, deed dated 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD FamilySearch image].</ref>

For £25, David Murphy assigned John two acres, one rood and thirty-five perches at Lislea, with the associated renewal rights. The memorial was registered on 22 December 1792. William Henry and [[Glasgow-4014|Nathaniel Glasgow of Drumgreenagh]], farmer, witnessed the transaction.<ref name="Deed1786" />

John's birth is shown only as before 1768, an estimated boundary consistent with his being married and transacting land in 1786. His death occurred after the deed date; no exact death record has been identified.

== Research Notes ==
This John cannot be [[Glasgow-3439|John Glasgow born about 1794]], who belonged to a later Drumgreenagh generation. The shared residence makes a family relationship plausible, but the 1786 memorial names no child of John and Jane.

The memorial also states no relationship between John and Nathaniel Glasgow.

The entry is indexed under 21 March 1836.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Names], ''Pre-1858 Wills and Admons'', search result for James Glasgow, Killycarragh, 21 March 1836, accessed 7 September 2026. The result's item-detail URL is session-bound and the original probate document does not survive. The index date should not be treated as an exact death date. The entry establishes a probate subject named James Glasgow and his recorded residence, but it supplies no age, occupation or relatives. A later family statement preserved as PRONI T1959/3 describes the writer's paternal grandfather, William Glasgow of Killycurragh, as the husband of an unidentified Miss Cunningham of Omagh and father of five sons and three daughters. The writer said that her father and a brother William were educated together; William became a physician in England. Three other sons—apparently Henry, James and Samuel—“lived and died on [the] farm in Killycurragh,” with Samuel remaining in their parents' house.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T1959/3, photocopy of an undated and unsigned Glasgow–Rutherford family letter preserved with papers of the 1890s; online transcription by Albert Rutherford reproduced by Gary Harding, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ “Rutherfords and Glasgows in Co. Tyrone, Ireland”], 9 January 2005. That relationship-defined James is the strongest and probable identity for the same-named Killycarragh probate subject. The letter's writer was born five months after her father, Rev. John Glasgow of Orritor, died in July 1801, placing the named James in the correct generation. A Presbyterian-ministers compilation independently identifies John Glasgow of Orritor as the minister ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and records his death on 13 July 1801.[https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html “Presbyterian Ministers in Co. Tyrone”], entry for John Glasgow of Orritor and New Row, Coleraine, citing his ordination on 8 March 1796 and death on 13 July 1801. == Research Notes == The index spells the residence ''Killycarragh''. It is probably the townland now rendered Killycurragh in the Oritor electoral division and Derryloran parish. The T1959/3 statement independently places the writer's uncle James on the family farm at Killycurragh and says that he died there. The combined name, place, generation and death evidence supports one probable identity, although the original probate document is lost and the family letter is known only through an online transcription. The St Luran register records a James Glasgow living at Orritor Craigs in 1829, when a child was baptised to him and Mary Anne of Drumcann.Representative Church Body Library, [https://www.churchofireland.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/AngRecord/DerryloranVol1.pdf ''Derryloran Parish Register, Volume 1''], baptism no. 466, 5 April 1829. He is a useful locality candidate for the 1836 estate, but the shared forename and neighbouring residence do not prove that the two records concern the same person. === Duplicate audit === The local One Tree export and live WikiTree data were searched again in September 2026. The strongest automated place-name result is demonstrably not the deceased man: * [[Glasgow-1701|James Glasgow junior]] lived at Killycurragh but died there on 27 July 1875. His exact-place match is valuable for local context, not identity with the 1836 probate subject. * [[Glasgow-1702|James Glasgow of Ballynasollus]] died in 1882 and cannot be this man. * [[Glasgow-3444|James Glasgow of Cookstown]] died in 1866 and cannot be this man. * [[Glasgow-1165|James Glasgow]] belongs to the separately documented family of John Glasgow and Mary Arthur. His family Bible records his death on 20 April 1823 and gives no Killycurragh connection. The earlier death alone would not exclude a delayed probate entry, but the incompatible relationship-defined family does. * [[Glasgow-2989|James Glasgow of Derryloran]] is an older local candidate whose death is unresolved, but no source on the profile places him at Killycarragh or identifies him through relatives or property. No current WikiTree profile is proved to represent this 1836 estate. The surviving index is too slight to show whether the subject was the 1829 Orritor Craigs householder, the older unresolved Derryloran man, or another member of the several contemporary Glasgow households. The new family discriminator resolves the creation question even though it does not prove an exact birth date. None of the searched profiles represents the son of William Glasgow of Killycurragh and Miss Cunningham who lived and died on the family farm. [[Glasgow-2989|James of Derryloran]] is an older, relationship-free reconstruction, while the exact-place [[Glasgow-1701|James]] lived until 1875. Creating this man unconnected, with the probable family placement in Research Notes, avoids both conflation and omission. [[Glasgow-1698|Samuel Glasgow]], born about 1800 and reported to have died at Killycurragh in 1857, is the strongest live candidate for the brother Samuel whom T1959/3 says remained in his parents' Killycurragh house. This is a useful probable sibling identity, not proof of a shared parent attachment. By contrast, [[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow of Killycurragh]] became a Presbyterian elder and emigrated to Ohio; that documented life does not fit the letter's physician William who practised in London and Hull. === Further research === Inspect the original T1959/3 photocopy, the rest of T1959/1-8, D1413/3a-b and T1762, then trace the Killycurragh holding through Derryloran rentals, deeds and valuation material. Those records may supply James's dates, heirs and his mother's forename. They are still required before making structured parent or sibling attachments, but not before creating the distinct record bearer. == Sources ==

== Biography ==

'''William Glasgow''' was married to [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]]. They were living in or associated with Kirknewton parish, Midlothian, Scotland, by 1682.

Their daughter [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded there on 21 April 1682, daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook.<ref name="Bessie1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, Bessie Glasgow, 1682; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch record].</ref>

William and Ann were also recorded as the parents of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]], baptised on 22 April 1705.<ref name="William1705">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, 1705; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FY9 FamilySearch record].</ref>

William's own birth, parentage and death have not yet been established from contemporary evidence.

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

This William was previously conflated with [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], who was baptised on 24 September 1671 as a son of Andro Glasgow.<ref name="William1671">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, baptised 24 September 1671, son of Andro Glasgow; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-F2B FamilySearch record].</ref>

The two men cannot reasonably be the same person. [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded as the daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook in April 1682,<ref name="Bessie1682" /> when the William baptised in September 1671 was only ten years old.

The 1671 baptism and the parentage by Andro Glasgow therefore belong to [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], not this profile.

No contemporary evidence has yet been found establishing this William's date or place of birth or identifying his parents. The former structured father [[Glasgow-1554|Walter Glasgow]] was disconnected on 26 September 2026. Walter was christened in 1649, only about eleven years before this William's estimated birth, and no cited record names Walter as his father.<ref name="Walter1649">FamilySearch, “Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Walter Glasgow, christened 23 September 1649 in the Kirknewton/East Calder index, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FWL record VQ4K-FWL].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

William was married to [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]].

No contemporary marriage entry for the couple has yet been identified. Their relationship is nevertheless supported by parish records naming them together as the parents of children in 1682 and 1705.<ref name="Bessie1682" /><ref name="William1705" />

Ann's currently estimated birth date should be checked separately against the 1682 record, since she was already Bessie's mother by that date.

=== Drummore and "Walter" ===

Later online genealogies describe this man as '''William Walter Glasgow''' and associate him with Drummore. No contemporary source has yet been identified establishing either the middle name "Walter" or a Drummore birthplace or residence.

These claims should remain research leads rather than established facts.

=== Ireland ===

Later pedigrees connect this family with County Tyrone, Ireland. The presently identified records do not establish when or whether William himself migrated to Ireland.

The 1759 probate-index entry for [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] places James at Drumearn, County Tyrone, but does not by itself establish James as William's son or prove a Scottish-to-Irish migration by this William.

=== Priority Research ===

* '''Priority 1 — inspect Bessie's original 1682 parish entry.'''
** Obtain the original Kirknewton Old Parish Register entry behind the FamilySearch index.
** Record the exact wording, residence, father's occupation and witnesses.
** Confirm the spelling of Ann's surname in the original record.

* '''Priority 1 — locate the marriage of William and Ann.'''
** Search Kirknewton and neighbouring Midlothian parishes before April 1682.
** Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow and Glassgow.
** Search McCook and contemporary spelling variants.
** A marriage entry could establish William's residence, parish of origin or other identifying information.

* '''Priority 1 — inspect the original 1705 baptism of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]].'''
** Confirm both parents' names in the original register.
** Compare residence and witnesses with Bessie's 1682 entry.

* '''Priority 2 — reconstruct the complete William and Ann household.'''
** Inspect every Glasgow baptism in Kirknewton and neighbouring parishes between about 1680 and 1710.
** Resolve the parentage of [[Glasgow-1546|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1544|John Glasgow]] from their original records rather than existing tree relationships.

* '''Priority 2 — investigate the County Tyrone connection.'''
** Work backwards from the earliest securely documented members of the Glasgow family in County Tyrone.
** Look specifically for records naming Scottish relatives, places of origin, executors, beneficiaries or other associates capable of linking the Irish family to William and Ann.

Glasgow-1929.remote_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Hugh Glasgow was born on 30 January 1710 and baptised on 5 February at Kilwinning, Ayrshire. The index names his parents as [[Glasgow-1927|John Glasgow]] and [[Gemill-4|Mary Gemmill]].<ref name="hughbirth">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625904&tab=this Hugh Glasgow, 30 January/5 February 1710], Kilwinning, OPR 599/1, p. 70; FamilySearch [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYST-MFP record XYST-MFP].</ref>

A Kilmarnock marriage index records Hugh Glasgow and [[McEachin-120|Margaret McEachin]] on 20 March 1732.<ref name="marriage">FamilySearch, ''Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910'', {{FamilySearch Record|XT24-XWR}}, Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McEachin, 20 March 1732. Original page not compared.</ref> Kilmarnock baptism indexes name Hugh and Margaret, whose surname appears as McGechan/McCachen in different transcripts, for Mary (1732), Jean (1735), Margaret (1738), Hugh (1742), Ann (1749) and Hugh (1752). A 1755 Glasgow baptism names Hugh and Margtt. McKechny as parents of John. Each child's own profile holds its event-specific citation; the index spellings and child identifications should be compared against the original pages.<ref name="mary1732">Findmypast, Kilmarnock baptism [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3599128&tab=this Mary Glasgow, 17 December 1732], parents Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McGechan.</ref><ref name="john1755">FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRS2-MNP John Glasgo, 19/23 April 1755], parents Hugh and Margtt. McKechny.</ref>

A separate Kilmarnock baptism dated 11 April 1744 names Hugh Glasgow and [[Giffen-664|Margaret Giffen]] as parents of another Mary. The source names a different mother and the same father name. This child event was retained from the former [[Glasgow-4166]] profile; its connection to the Kilwinning-born Hugh remains a qualified inference, not proof of a second marriage, widowhood or Margaret McEachin's death.<ref name="mary1744">Findmypast, Kilmarnock baptism [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3600620&tab=this Mary Glasgow, 11 April 1744], parents Hugh Glasgow and Margaret Giffen.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The former Kilmarnock father profile Glasgow-4166 was merged into this one on 27 September 2026. The Kilwinning child of 1710 is age-compatible with the 1732 adult groom and father, and the 1732 marriage to Margaret McEachin together with recurring McGechan/McCachen forms in the Kilmarnock children provides a family bridge. The original Kilwinning and Kilmarnock records do not expressly identify the same Hugh, so the child-to-adult step remains inferred. Earlier profiles placed the first Hugh child with Margaret McEachin in 1749; the 1732–1742 Kilmarnock entries expand that sequence.

Two Mary baptisms, in 1732 and 1744, are separate records. They might be successive same-name children or belong to distinct same-name fathers. The 1744 Giffen entry should be examined separately for residence, occupation and witness details; preserve both recorded mothers and all child citations pending that comparison. No death date is established for Hugh.

== Biography ==  
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

John Glasgow was born before 1661. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] and [[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]].<ref>Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950. FamilySearch database. https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPZ-B5P (accessed 2025).</ref> He was baptized on 30 August 1661 at Edinburgh Parish, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland.

Baptism locations for their children suggest that John Glasgow and his wife [[Spark-330|Agnes Spark]] moved from Kilwinning parish to Stevenston parish sometime between 1687 and 1701.

From Elaine Comes: "[[Glasgow-1055|William Glasgow (abt.1701-)]] had a brother named [[Glasgow-1056|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1692-)]] who married [[Kilpatrick-1635|Janet (Kilpatrick) Glasgow]]. They were sons of [[Glasgow-1080|John Glasgow]] and [[Spark-330|Agnes (Spark) Glasgow]]."

From baptism records, they also had a son [[Glasgow-1058|George Glasgow (bef.1687-)]], baptized in Kilwinning.<ref>Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950. FamilySearch database. https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTVB-MX8 (accessed 2025).</ref>

== Research Notes ==

* John Glasgow's testament dative and inventory was recorded on 6 November 1685 in the Boog of Steivinstoun at the Glasgow Commissary Court (CC9/7/47).
* He appears as the father in baptism records for George Glasgow in 1687 and William Glasgow in 1701, suggesting he lived well beyond 1685 despite the early testament listing.<ref>Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950. FamilySearch database. https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZK-3J8 (accessed 2025).</ref>

== Biography ==

{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

Thomas Glasgow, born in 1612, is the son of [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]] and [[Steuart-563|Margaret Steuart]]. Witnesses to his baptism were: William Howie, David Scherrar<ref>Thomas Glasgow

* Record Type: Births & Baptisms
* Data Set: Glasgow High Kirk Baptisms 1609-1777
* Baptism Date: 15 March 1612
* Location: Glasgow
* Surnames: Glasgow, Steuart
*  Reference: Vol: 1/754

Lawful son of George Glasgow and Margaret STEUART

Witnesses: William Howie, David Scherrar</ref> 

=== Family and Descendants ===
Notable events in his life include the births of his children, as detailed in the Old Parish Records:

* '''JANNET''': Born on November 29, 1640, in Linlithgow. (No mother listed)<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RX-G4T : 16 September 2021), Thomas Glasgow in entry for Jannet Glasgow, 1640.</ref> 
* '''JOHN''': Born on February 25, 1644, in Linlithgow. Mother: Hellin Bryse.<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RV-T82 : 16 September 2021), Thomas Glasgow in entry for John Glasgow, 1644.</ref> 

== Research Notes == 
* This profile should not be confused with that of [[Glasgow-1159|Thomas Glasgow (bef.1627-)]], who married Catherine Weir in Midlothian  or [[Glasgow-2459|Thomas Glasgow (abt.1610-)]] who had children with Agnes Thomsone in Inveresk.
* Another child, '''THOMAS''', born to Alexander Glasgow and Issobell Anderson on August 12, 1666, in St Cuthbert's, may be related.

[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Thomas-1 Thomas Research]

==Sources==
Thomas Glasgow was likely born by about 1615, an estimate based on the timing of his marriage and the birth of his children. His parents have not yet been confirmed by primary sources (see Research Notes).

He married [[Thomsone-70|Agnes Thomsone]]. While their specific marriage record has not been located, their relationship is confirmed by their joint parentage listed in the baptismal records of their children in the Inveresk parish.<ref name="MarriageInferred">Marriage is confirmed by parentage listed in the baptism records of their children in the Inveresk Old Parish Registers between 1634 and 1643.</ref>

Thomas and Agnes had the following children christened in the parish of Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian, Scotland. The christening records for these children can be found in the Old Parish Registers under frame number 259 (OPR 689/1).<ref name="OPR">Old Parish Registers, Inveresk and Musselburgh, Midlothian, Scotland (OPR 689/1), Frame 259. Records for children of Thomas Glasgow and Agnes Thomsone.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-2460|Agnes Glasgow]], christened 27 July 1634.
* [[Glasgow-2461|Thomas Glasgow]], christened 6 August 1637.
* [[Glasgow-2462|William Glasgow]], christened 21 August 1639.
* [[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow]]. While his christening within this family has not been located, he is attached based on strong circumstantial evidence. Following traditional Scottish naming patterns, James and his wife Helen Clerk named their first known daughter [[Glasgow-3092|Agnes]], christened in 1658, presumably in honor of James's mother, [[Thomsone-70|Agnes Thomsone]].<ref name="Agnes1658">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", , FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F318-T2H : 16 September 2021), James Glesgow in entry for Agnes Glesgow, 1658.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3049|Marione Glasgow]], christened 18 December 1642.
* [[Glasgow-3050|Margaret Glasgow]], christened 16 November 1643.

Further details regarding Thomas's specific birth date, occupation, or death remain unknown and are goals for future research.

== Research Notes ==
'''Disproven & Unproven Parentage:'''
*   The corresponding FamilySearch Family Tree profile proposes that his parents are James Glasgow and Christina Adamson. However, no primary sources have been found to substantiate this connection for the Thomas Glasgow of Inveresk. This parentage should be considered a speculative clue until a primary record (such as a christening record naming the parents) is located.
*   The person was also previously attached to [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow I]] and [[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]] of Colonial Maryland.

[[Category:Kilbirnie, Ayrshire]]
[[Category:Scotland, Surgeons]]
== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}
{{Notables Sticker}}
{{Scotland Sticker}}
Robert Glasgow was baptised on 17 October 1693 in Kilbirnie, Ayrshire, Scotland.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Robert Glasgow 17 Oct 1693, son of John Glasgow and Jeane Cunynghame; citing Ref No: 10 / 19, parish 596.</ref> He was the son of the [[Glasgow-1073|John Glasgow]] and [[Cunningham-20924|Jean Cunningham]].<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY24-PMR : 11 February 2020), Robert Glasgow, 1693.</ref> Robert became a Surgeon and by November 1722 was resident at Puddevenholm (Paddockholm) in Kilbirnie.<ref>National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseDetails.aspx?reference=RH15/120/178 RH15/120/178]: Letter from Robert Glasgow, Paddockholm, to James Glasgow, student of divinity at Glasgow, his brother. Sends butter and cheese for Mr. Gordon. 22 Nov 1722.</ref> He also served as the factor (estate manager) for the estates of Kilbirnie and Glengarnock and was styled '''Chamberlain to the  Viscount of Garnock, and surgeon at Kilbirnie'''.

On 15 December 1736 in Kilbirnie, Robert married [[Allan-4046|Margaret Allan]].<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Banns and Marriages," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), marriage of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 74, parish 596.</ref> They had nine children: 
#[[Glasgow-3004|Jean Glasgow]], baptised 28 December 1727,<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Jean Glasgow 28 Dec 1727, daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 78, parish 596.</ref> married James White of  Woodsyde, parish of Kilwinning, 1 October 1750.
#[[Glasgow-3006|John Glasgow]], baptised 29 March 1730.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), John Glasgow 29 Mar 1730, son of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 83, parish 596.</ref>
#[[Glasgow-3007|Margaret Glasgow]], baptised 21 January 1734,<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Margaret Glasgow 21 Jan 1734, daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 85, parish 596.</ref> died in childhood.
#[[Glasgow-3008|Janet Glasgow]], born 4 January 1736,<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Jannet Glasgow 11 Jan 1736, daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 88, parish 596.</ref> married William Cochran,  younger of Ladyland, 2 September 1756, and left issue. 
#[[Glasgow-3005|Anna Glasgow]], born c.1738, married Hugh Allan in Kilwinning, 23  December 1757. 
#[[Glasgow-1515|Charles Glasgow]], baptised 28 September 1740.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Charles Glasgow 28 Sep 1740, daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 97, parish 596.</ref>
#[[Glasgow-3878|Margaret Glasgow]], baptised 21 August 1743,<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), Margarat Glasgow 21 Aug 1743, daughter of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref No: 10 / 105, parish 596.</ref> married to Andrew Smith of Todholes, in the parish of Dalry, 20 March 1764. 
#[[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow]] of Mountgreenan, baptised 18 October 1747.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 30 Dec 2025), Robert Glasgow 18 Oct 1747, son of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref 10 / 116, parish 596: Robert laul son to Robert Glasgow of Puddevenholm & Margaret Allan Oct 18.</ref> He gained a fortune in St  Vincent's, married Rachel, daughter of John Dunlop of that Ilk, and died at Mountgreenan House, 19 April 1827, leaving no legitimate issue.
#[[Glasgow-1142|James Glasgow]], baptised 18 March 1750.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 30 Dec 2025), James Glasgow 18 Mar 1750, son of Robert Glasgow and Margarat Allan; citing Ref 10 / 123, parish 596.</ref> He went to St Vincent's and died about 1803 in the parish of Calder, near Edinburgh, unmarried. 

In 1747, Robert was styled "of Puddockholm." He passed away on 9 May 1766 in Crookedhouse, Kilbirnie.<ref>Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Deaths and Burials," database with images, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : image accessed 13 May 2026), death of Robert Glasgow, 9 May 1766; citing Ref No: 10 / 326, parish 596.</ref>
 
== Research Notes ==
 Puddockholm, which was sometimes called "the Waters", lies on the banks of the water of Garnock, which gave rise to its picturesque name. 
 
 Robert's responsibilities as factor included overseeing financial matters, and one notable instance is documented in the account-book he kept for these estates. In this record, Glasgow handled the remittance of funds to Ireland on behalf of Mr. James Crawfurd. The specific entry mentions a payment made to Mr. Hew Crawfurd, writer to the signet, amounting to £64:11:6 Scots on 24 October 1724.This legitimate entry, proven by Glasgow's account-book, was later used in a forgery where a fraudulent entry was created, indicating payment to "Mr. Arthur Dawson of Dublin" for the same amount on behalf of Mr. James Crawfurd. The genuine entry by Robert Glasgow stands as evidence of his accurate financial management, contrasting the forged document's attempt to misrepresent transactions involving the estates.
 
 Although Robert was later referred to as "Dr. Robert Glasgow" he was a surgeon, not a M.D.

{{Estimated Date}} {{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}} == Biography == '''John Glasgow''', recorded as '''Jo Glascho''', was a taxed householder at Kilwaughter Demesne in Kilwaughter parish, upper Glenarm barony, County Antrim, in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll, T/307/A; W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf transcription], records 5347–5348, PDF p. 36. He is probably the same man who appears repeatedly in the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregational records about 1699–1700/1 as '''John Glasgow, senior''', representing Kilwaughter. If this identification is correct, his documented career extended for more than thirty years. The designation ''senior'' is genealogically significant: it strongly suggests that another, younger John Glasgow was then known within the local community. That younger man's identity and relationship remain unknown. === Kilwaughter in 1669 === The 1669 Hearth Money Roll records: :'''Jo. Glascho''' :'''James Glascho''' as immediately consecutive householders at Kilwaughter Demesne. The abbreviation ''Jo.'' most probably represents John. The exact co-location and uncommon surname make a close relationship between John and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] probable, although the tax roll gives no ages, household members or relationship. === John Glasgow senior, c. 1699–1700 === Classon Porter later published substantial extracts from an early record of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation. Porter stated that he had been unable to locate the original in his day and was working from a transcript made or procured for Rev. D. Davison, portions of which had already been published in 1826. Porter arranged his quotations by subject rather than strict chronology.Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 2 (1863–1864), pp. 410–415; [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0002unse Internet Archive]. Porter describes the provenance of the transcript on p. 410. On 3 March 1699/1700 the congregational record appointed four men to approach the Presbytery concerning Rev. William Ogilvie. One was:
"John Glasgow, sen."
Porter immediately reproduced the Presbytery's minute for the same deputation. It names the same four men — Samuel Smealley, William Hare, John Glasgow and James Callwell — but calls him simply '''John Glasgow'''. This is useful identity evidence. ''Senior'' was a contextual qualifier; the same man could be recorded without it in another record of the same transaction. On 17 May, John again appears as:
"John Glasgow, sen., for Kilwochter"
He and Patrick Agnew bound for Kilwaughter's £8 share of the minister's stipend, together with obligations for firing, ploughing and harrowing. John was also among the heads of families entrusted with considering the rebuilding of the meeting house. These entries establish that he was a substantial member of the Kilwaughter congregation and a representative of its householders. They do not establish that he held the office of elder. The following year's material again records plain '''John Glasgow''' acting for Kilwaughter. On 27 February 1700 in the record's dating, John Glasgow and Robert White were chosen for Kilwaughter to inspect the minister's land. In the same meeting, Patrick Agnew and John Glasgow were selected for Kilwaughter to consider repairs to the minister's house.Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), pp. 15–18; [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive]. The date falls in the period conventionally written 1700/1 when double-dating pre-1752 records. The recurrence of: * the same uncommon name; * the same Kilwaughter locality; * John being explicitly styled ''senior''; * plain John being paired again with Patrick Agnew; * and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] also appearing in Kilwaughter affairs about 1700; makes it more probable that the congregational John was the '''same man''' as Jo Glascho, householder at Kilwaughter in 1669, rather than an undocumented son of that man. The identification remains inferential because no surviving entry explicitly says that the 1669 and c.1700 men were identical. === Family === [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] was recorded immediately beside John at Kilwaughter in 1669. About 1700 a James Glasgow was appointed overseer for Kilwaughter during work on the minister's house. The repeated John-and-James presence in the same small district strengthens the case that they belonged to one close family cluster. Their exact relationship remains unknown. John is currently placed as an uncertain son of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]], the Robert ''Glaskow'' associated with Larne during the period of the 1641 rebellion.Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 153r, examination of Con O'Sheale, 21 April 1653, identifier 838153r210; Robert is described as "one Robert Glaskow liuing in Larne"; [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42821.html 1641 Depositions Project transcription]. That parentage remains a reconstruction from chronology, locality and surname continuity. No record names Robert as John's father. John's wife is unknown. == Research Notes == === The younger John implied by "senior" === The repeated designation '''John Glasgow, sen.''' strongly suggests that another, younger John Glasgow was known to the congregation by about 1700. The same group of congregational extracts uses other age qualifiers, including ''Robert Mea, jun.'' and ''John Kerr, sen.'', showing that such distinctions were actively used in the source. No located published extract explicitly names a '''John Glasgow junior''', however, and ''senior'' does not itself prove a father-son relationship. The younger namesake could have been: * John's son; * a nephew; * a cousin; * another younger member of the same Glasgow cluster. '''A son is a plausible hypothesis, but not yet a relationship suitable for attachment without further evidence.''' The important distinction is therefore: :'''Probable:''' Jo Glascho of Kilwaughter in 1669 = John Glasgow senior of Kilwaughter c.1700. :'''Possible:''' the younger John implied by ''senior'' was his son. :'''Unknown:''' the younger John's identity and later history. No reliable WikiTree profile has yet been identified for this younger namesake. === Could the c.1700 senior have been a son of the 1669 John? === It is chronologically possible but presently less likely. A male householder in 1669 could readily still have been active about 1700. Even if John had been only about twenty-one in 1669, he would have been about fifty-two by 1700 — entirely compatible with being the established ''senior'' John, a head of family and congregational bondsman. Making the c.1700 senior a son instead requires an additional same-name generation for which no record has yet been found. It would also require some other younger John to explain why that second-generation John was himself called ''senior''. The simpler reconstruction fits all presently located evidence without adding an undocumented generation. '''Current assessment: same person probable; father-son replacement possible but unsupported.''' === Parentage and Scottish hypothesis === The current uncertain father hypothesis should distinguish two separate questions. [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]] is the Robert ''Glaskow'' associated with Larne in the 1653 examination. He is a plausible earlier member of the Larne–Kilwaughter Glasgow family and is currently attached as John's uncertain father. A separate [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] was recorded in Glasgow, Scotland, in 1618. That Scottish Robert has been proposed as identical with the Larne Robert, but no documentary migration or identity bridge has been found. The two hypotheses should not be collapsed: * Robert of Larne → John of Kilwaughter: '''possible; unproved'''. * Scottish Robert → Robert of Larne: '''possible identity; unproved'''. John's mother remains unknown. === Record survival === Porter's nineteenth-century publication is derivative: he stated that the original early congregational record could not then be found and that he was using a transcript. There is now a more concrete archival route. Modern scholarship identifies surviving Larne and Kilwaughter session material for 1699–1701 and 1720–1769 and cites '''PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B'''.Robert Whan, ''The Presbyterians of Ulster, 1680–1730'' (Boydell Press, 2013), introduction and bibliography, identifying Larne and Kilwaughter session records for 1699–1701 and 1720–1769 and citing PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B; [https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/C038A358FF15C0285190286F12E951A4/9781782041894bib_p202-230_CBO.pdf/bibliography.pdf Cambridge bibliography]. The early section should be inspected directly to determine its precise relationship to the transcript used by Porter and, more importantly, whether entries omitted from his topical extracts identify the younger John Glasgow. === Suggested structured data === * '''First name:''' John * '''Last name at birth:''' Glasgow * '''Recorded spelling:''' Glascho * '''Birth:''' before 1651, place unknown, uncertain * '''Death:''' after about 1700, place unknown, uncertain, if the 1669 and c.1700 records are accepted as the same man * '''Residence:''' Kilwaughter Demesne, County Antrim, 1669 * '''Later residence/association:''' Kilwaughter, c.1699–1700/1, probable same person * '''Father:''' [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]], uncertain * '''Mother:''' unknown * '''Relationship to [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]]:''' probable close relative; exact relationship unknown * '''Spouse:''' unknown * '''Children:''' none proved * '''Possible child:''' an unidentified younger John Glasgow implied by the designation ''John Glasgow, sen.'' === Priority Research === * '''PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B — Larne and Kilwaughter session book, 1699–1701 and 1720–1769.''' ** Inspect the complete early section rather than Porter's selected extracts. ** Search every occurrence of Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascho, John, ''sen.'', ''jun.'', younger and elder. ** Concentrate on the entries surrounding 3 March 1699/1700, 17 May and 27 February 1700/1. ** Determine whether the implied younger John is named, and whether any relationship to John senior is stated. * '''Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland — Antrim Presbytery minutes, 1697–1713.''' ** Inspect the original minute for the Larne deputation of 3 March 1699/1700 and subsequent Larne/Kilwaughter business. ** Porter quotes the Presbytery minute as naming plain "John Glasgow"; surrounding entries may contain a qualifier, residence or relationship omitted from the published extract. * '''PRONI D282 and NRS GD154/505–534 — Kilwaughter estate material, approximately 1665–1710.''' ** Search for John Glasgow, Jo Glascho and variants, explicitly watching for simultaneous senior and junior tenants. ** Trace any holding occupied by John from the 1669 hearth roll into the early eighteenth century. ** A lease, renewal or succession entry naming a son, heir, widow or former tenant could distinguish the same-man and father-son hypotheses. * '''PRONI T/808/14889 — 1666 County Antrim subsidy roll.''' ** Search John/Jo, James and Robert Glasgow under Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascho, Glaskow and Glascow. ** An earlier appearance of John in the same Kilwaughter tenancy cluster would further strengthen continuity into 1669 and c.1700. == Sources ==
