{{Estimated Date}}

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' represents an unidentified younger namesake implied by the
description of [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] as "John Glasgow, senior" in
published extracts of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregational records.<ref name="Porter">Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter,"
''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), extracts from the congregational records;
[https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

The word "senior" distinguishes an older John from a younger contemporary. It
does not state that the younger man was his son. [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]]
is therefore attached as an uncertain working father, not a proved parent.

John's birth about 1680 is an estimate. No record has been found giving his
age, birthplace, wife or death, or proving a child.

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible identities ===

A '''John Glasgow of Killroot''' appears in the 1733 Connor diocesan administration-bond index.<ref name="Killroot">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search], Pre-1858 Wills and Admons, sub-index Connor Diocesan Administration Bonds: John Glasgow, Kilroot, 1733; official detail inspected 21 September 2026. Occupation, notes and reference fields are blank. PRONI states that the original documents do not exist and no further information survives in this index. Individual result links are session-bound.</ref> He is the strongest record-defined
candidate for the younger namesake, but the index does not identify his father
or establish that he was the man represented by this profile.

[[Glasgow-3959|John Glasgow of Ballyboggy]] is currently attached as an uncertain son, not as a proved descendant or an identified same person. A 1740 return
records `Joh Glask` in the Ballyboggy locality, and a three-life lease from the
same year names John Glasgow and James Wier as joint lessees of one-third of
Ballyboggy.<ref>W. MacAfee,
[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf 1740 County Antrim Protestant Householders' Return], Dunaghy entries; PRONI
`D2223/15/56`, Ballyboggy title-deed bundle.</ref> No record connects that John
to the older Kilwaughter man or proves the attached father-son relationship. If the 1733 administration-bond entry belongs to this profile, its deceased-estate chronology conflicts with identifying him as the man personally co-leasing Ballyboggy in 1740. An earlier relative remains possible, but unproved.

[[Glasgow-551|John Glasgow]] is associated with a separate traditional County
Tyrone family reconstruction. Similar name and estimated age do not establish
that the profiles are duplicates.

=== Family and descendants ===

No wife or descendant has been proved. [[Glasgow-3959|John Glasgow of Ballyboggy]] is attached as an uncertain working son; the attachment is a hypothesis, not historical proof. The word "senior" supports
only the existence of a younger namesake. The relationship could have been
father and son, but could also have been uncle and nephew, cousins or unrelated
men distinguished by age.

The decisive records are the complete Larne and Kilwaughter session material
at PRONI `MIC1B/6A/1B`, independent Kilroot estate or church material identifying the John in
the 1733 administration-bond index, and the three named lives in the 1740 Ballyboggy lease.

Glasgow-3375.remote_wikitext:
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' was born before about 1661, probably in Scotland. His exact date and place of birth are unknown.

The estimated birth date is based on John being old enough to have a child baptised in July 1679. He may have been born considerably earlier.

John was living in, or otherwise associated with, the parish of Kilwinning, Ayrshire, Scotland, between 1679 and 1689.

He had at least two known children:

* '''Jon Glasgow''', baptised on 6 July 1679 in Kilwinning, recorded as the son of Jon Glasgow and Barbara Alason.<ref name="Jon1679">Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 44, baptism of Jon Glasgow, 6 July 1679, son of Jon Glasgow and Barbara Alason.</ref>
* '''Jannet Glasgow''', baptised on 1 February 1689 in Kilwinning, recorded as the daughter of John Glasgow and a woman recorded by the surname Allason.<ref name="Jannet1689">Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 75, baptism of Jannet Glasgow, 1 February 1689, daughter of John Glasgow and Allason.</ref>

The woman surnamed Allason in Jannet's baptism was probably the same Barbara Alason named in Jon's baptism. The surviving indexed entry does not give her forename.

Her surname may appear in records under several spellings, including Alason, Allason, Alison and Allison.

No marriage or proclamation record for John Glasgow and Barbara Alason has yet been identified. Barbara should therefore be described as John's probable wife or partner rather than as a proven legal spouse.

John was alive, or was at least named as the father, when Jannet was baptised in February 1689.

His date and place of death are unknown.

=== Children ===

John Glasgow and probably Barbara Alason had the following known children:

# '''Jon Glasgow''', baptised 6 July 1679 at Kilwinning, Ayrshire.<ref name="Jon1679" />

# '''Jannet Glasgow''', baptised 1 February 1689 at Kilwinning, Ayrshire.<ref name="Jannet1689" />

There may have been other children whose baptisms were not recorded, whose records have not survived, or whose entries have not yet been identified.

== Possible Parentage ==

John's parents have not been established.

Five Scottish baptism records have been identified for men named John or Johne Glasgow who were born within, or close to, a plausible period for the father of a child baptised in 1679.

None of these records currently provides a direct connection to Kilwinning, Barbara Alason, or the children Jon and Jannet Glasgow.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 27 April 1656 in South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone.<ref name="John1656">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 27 April 1656, South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 23 years old when Jon Glasgow was baptised in 1679 and about 32 when Jannet was baptised in 1689.

He is a strong chronological candidate among the currently identified records.

However, South Leith is in Midlothian, while John's known children were baptised in Kilwinning, Ayrshire. No evidence has yet been found showing that this Johne moved to Ayrshire or was associated with Barbara Alason.

Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Johne Glasgow ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 22 April 1649 in Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of another Johne Glasgow.<ref name="John1649">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 22 April 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Johne Glasgow. The indexed record does not name his mother.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 30 years old in 1679 and about 40 in 1689.

He is chronologically plausible, but no evidence currently links him or his father with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

The elder Johne Glasgow should not presently be attached as John's father.

=== John Glasgow, son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse ===

A John Glasgow was baptised on 25 February 1644 in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse.<ref name="John1644">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," John Glasgow, baptised 25 February 1644, Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire, Scotland, son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse.</ref>

This John would have been about 35 years old in 1679 and about 45 in 1689.

He is chronologically plausible, but no evidence has yet been found connecting him or his parents with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 4 April 1639 in Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman.<ref name="John1639">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 4 April 1639, Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 40 years old in 1679 and about 50 in 1689.

He is chronologically possible, but no record currently links him with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 30 August 1661 in Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.<ref name="John1661">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 30 August 1661, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>

This Johne would have been approximately 17 years and 10 months old when Jon Glasgow was baptised on 6 July 1679. He would probably have been about 17 when the child was conceived.

He cannot be excluded entirely, but he is a less likely candidate because of his young age. His baptism also falls slightly later than John's estimated birth date of before about 1661.

No evidence has been found connecting him with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Parentage Assessment ===

The candidates may be ranked by chronological plausibility as follows:

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1656 at South Leith — about 23 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1649 at Kirknewton and East Calder — about 30 years old in 1679.

# '''John Glasgow''', baptised in 1644 at Linlithgow — about 35 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1639 at Duddingston — about 40 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1661 at Edinburgh — about 17 years old in 1679.

This ranking concerns age only. It is not evidence that the higher-ranked candidates were more closely connected to the Kilwinning family.

All five men were baptised in Midlothian or Linlithgowshire. The John Glasgow represented by this profile is currently known only from the baptism records of his children in Kilwinning, Ayrshire.

No candidate has yet been shown to have:

* lived in Kilwinning or elsewhere in Ayrshire;
* married or formed a household with Barbara Alason;
* fathered Jon Glasgow or Jannet Glasgow;
* used an occupation or territorial designation matching the Kilwinning records;
* shared relatives, witnesses, neighbours or associates with the Kilwinning family.

The absence of a matching Ayrshire baptism does not prove that John was born elsewhere. Scottish Old Parish Registers are incomplete, and some baptisms were never recorded or have not survived.

John's parents should remain unknown until additional evidence links one of these baptism records to the Kilwinning family.

== Research Notes ==

=== Original Kilwinning Records ===

The original images of the Kilwinning baptism entries should be examined rather than relying only on abbreviated index entries.

The images may contain information omitted from the index, including:

* John's occupation;
* a farm, village or residence;
* the mother's full name;
* witnesses or sponsors;
* whether the child was described as lawful or natural;
* marginal notes.

=== Marriage Search ===

A marriage or proclamation record should be sought for John Glasgow and Barbara Alason before July 1679.

Relevant parishes include:

* Kilwinning;
* Irvine;
* Stevenston;
* Kilbirnie;
* Dalry;
* Beith;
* Ardrossan;
* other nearby Ayrshire parishes.

Searches should include variants such as:

* John Glasgow;
* Johne Glasgow;
* Jon Glasgow;
* John Glasgo;
* Barbara Alason;
* Barbara Allason;
* Barbara Alison;
* Barbara Allison.

=== Kirk Session Records ===

Kilwinning kirk-session records may contain references to John Glasgow or Barbara Alason.

These records may be useful if:

* the couple married irregularly;
* a child was born outside a formally recorded marriage;
* the family received parish assistance;
* either parent was disciplined by the kirk session;
* the family moved into or out of the parish.

=== Other Records to Search ===

Potentially useful sources include:

* testaments and inventories;
* sasines;
* land and tenancy records;
* tax rolls;
* hearth-tax records;
* poll-tax records;
* communion rolls;
* kirk-session minutes;
* burial registers;
* mortcloth accounts.

Records involving Archbald Glasgow, Agnes Watsone, Thomas Glasgow, Hellin Bryse, Margaret Sluman, James Glasgow, Agnes Duncan or the elder Johne Glasgow should be checked for later appearances in Ayrshire.

== Identity and duplicate assessment ==
This Kilwinning John is a serious same-person candidate for [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow M.A.]]: the name and estimated generation agree, Kilwinning and Kilbirnie are neighbouring Ayrshire parishes, and the last indexed Barbara-family event in February 1689 preceded the minister's January 1690 marriage to Jean Cunningham. The chronology permits the identification but does not prove it.

Neither ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'' nor Paterson's county history mentions Barbara Alason, and the available index extracts do not give this John a title, occupation or residence that would identify him as the minister.<ref>''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'', vol. 3, p. 103, [https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf PDF]; James Paterson, ''History of the County of Ayr'', pp. 252-253, [https://archive.org/details/historyofcountyo02pateuoft/page/252/mode/2up scan].</ref> Glasgow-3375 and Glasgow-1073 must therefore remain separate unless the full Kilwinning OPR pages or another identifying record supplies a bridge.

The attached father [[Glasgow-1604|John Glasgow]] and the links to [[Glasgow-1434|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1433|Jannet Glasgow]] are retained as uncertain. [[Glasgow-3288|William Glasgow]] should not be moved between adult family groups without direct evidence.

== Sources ==

<references />

=== Principal Records ===

* Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 44, baptism of Jon Glasgow, 6 July 1679.
* Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 75, baptism of Jannet Glasgow, 1 February 1689.
* FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 27 April 1656 at South Leith, son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone.
* FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 22 April 1649 at Kirknewton and East Calder, son of Johne Glasgow.
* FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," John Glasgow, baptised 25 February 1644 at Linlithgow, son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse.
* FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 4 April 1639 at Duddingston, son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman.
* FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 30 August 1661 at Edinburgh, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3959]] is assessed at 27% (uncertain). The Ballyboggy John active in 1740 is a real earlier Antrim adult and could father the Glenleslie John born about 1751. The existing local pedigree offers a coherent older generation, but no shared holding or named-relative source bridges these men.

Next useful test: Seek a Ballyboggy–Glenleslie succession or named-kin link.

Source basis already held: [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.

=== Glenleslie father comparison ===

[[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] of Glenleslie is an uncertain father candidate, assessed at 18%, for the Glenleslie [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]. Their reported ages of 99 and 72 in 1851 give a plausible father–son generation, and both were Antrim-born farmers in houses 21 and 23. The census transcription, however, gives John’s first marriage as 1791, about twelve years after Robert’s estimated birth. Earlier fatherhood would require nonmarital fatherhood or an error or omission in the return; no earlier wife or union is established. Collateral kinship and another father remain more likely overall. Neither census entry states their relationship.<ref>[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf 1851 Irish Census Returns, detailed comma-delimited transcription], field definitions PDF p. 1 (field 17, first-marriage year), Glenleslie households 21–23 PDF p. 103. John’s original return has not been newly inspected. The original of Robert’s household is National Archives of Ireland, [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#id=31234&census_year=1851 Glenleslie household 23].</ref>

This unselected hypothesis concerns the Glenleslie census man. It does not identify the Lisnagaver tithe occupier, supply a mother or establish the wider pedigree.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2769]] is assessed at 64% (probable). This is the leading specific available father reconstruction, but the census does not name the boy and the older Newberry origins remain uncertain.

Probable 64%; household and locality inference, with no literal parent clause and no DNA data used.

Next useful test: Read Robert’s later property or probate for James by name.

=== Isabell father replacement, reviewed 22 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-3370|Isabell Glasgow]] is assigned in the local working model to [[Glasgow-4138|William Glasgow]], probable76%, with [[Glasgow-1605|the Polwarth child]] retained as the unselected possible38% alternative. Prefer William Glasgow-4138, documented at Cavers and Ormistoun in 1679–84, as the William who fathered Isabell at Cavers in December 1694. The repeated full name, same parish association, earlier adult activity and feasible father generation give this record-defined local adult a stronger fit than identifying the father directly with the 1658 Polwarth child Glasgow-1605. This is an inferred identification across the held records, not an explicit father-daughter statement in the Covenanter material.

Probable 76% for the complete father-profile identification. The baptism names William but supplies no mother. No shared relative, precise abode, occupation or continuous identifying clause connects the Cavers baptism to the 1679–84 servant. The Polwarth child remains a possible 38% alternative and might itself be the Cavers adult; no identity merge is selected. Other local Williams remain possible. The two FreeREG transcriptions disagree between 2 and 8 December 1694; the parish index gives 2 December. No new source inspection, birth age, mother, migration or live WikiTree change is claimed.

Held source basis: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3370 FreeREG, Isabell Glasgow baptism transcription, Cavers, 2 December 1694.]; [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3370 FreeREG record 0427, Isabell Glasgow baptism transcription, Cavers, 8 December 1694.]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028558&tab=this Cavers William, examination June 1679, servant at Ormistoun: reviewed Findmypast transcript JC39/22]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028560&tab=this William Glasgow, Ormistoun servant list, October 1684; Findmypast Scottish Covenanters, record GBPR/COVENANT/028560].

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1093]] is assessed at 58% (possible). Glasgow protocols identify an elder John’s son John in 1563 and again a younger John in 1570–71. The generation fits the Hirmanscheillis testator of 1577, whose death excludes both the elder John (dead by June 1575) and Ninian’s brother John (alive in 1613). This makes the documented son a useful preferred candidate for the rural testator.

The father–son wording is explicit for the burgh Johns; identifying that son with the Hirmanscheillis husband of Margaret Hoghame remains a possible inference, without an estate or residence bridge.

Next useful test: Compare protocol property names with Hirmanscheillis testament associates and land transfers.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n52/mode/2up Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 3, protocol 748, 13 May 1563, scan (https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n52/mode/2up); vol. 6, protocol 1722, 8 January 1570/71, scan (https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog/page/n58/mode/2up).]; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills National Records of Scotland, John Glasgow testament dative, CC8/8/5 images 276-277: John Glasgow]. Glasgow-4138.public_addition_wikitext:
=== Isabell father replacement, reviewed 22 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-3370|Isabell Glasgow]] is assigned in the local working model to [[Glasgow-4138|William Glasgow]], probable76%, with [[Glasgow-1605|the Polwarth child]] retained as the unselected possible38% alternative. Prefer William Glasgow-4138, documented at Cavers and Ormistoun in 1679–84, as the William who fathered Isabell at Cavers in December 1694. The repeated full name, same parish association, earlier adult activity and feasible father generation give this record-defined local adult a stronger fit than identifying the father directly with the 1658 Polwarth child Glasgow-1605. This is an inferred identification across the held records, not an explicit father-daughter statement in the Covenanter material.

Probable 76% for the complete father-profile identification. The baptism names William but supplies no mother. No shared relative, precise abode, occupation or continuous identifying clause connects the Cavers baptism to the 1679–84 servant. The Polwarth child remains a possible 38% alternative and might itself be the Cavers adult; no identity merge is selected. Other local Williams remain possible. The two FreeREG transcriptions disagree between 2 and 8 December 1694; the parish index gives 2 December. No new source inspection, birth age, mother, migration or live WikiTree change is claimed.

Held source basis: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3370 FreeREG, Isabell Glasgow baptism transcription, Cavers, 2 December 1694.]; [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3370 FreeREG record 0427, Isabell Glasgow baptism transcription, Cavers, 8 December 1694.]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028558&tab=this Cavers William, examination June 1679, servant at Ormistoun: reviewed Findmypast transcript JC39/22]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028560&tab=this William Glasgow, Ormistoun servant list, October 1684; Findmypast Scottish Covenanters, record GBPR/COVENANT/028560].

Glasgow-2872.summary: Preferred replacement father James Glasgow-1025, 67% probable, for Samuel Glasgow-2872; John Glasgow-2870 retained as an unselected 25% uncertain alternative, previously 72% probable. No mother, vital date, person merge or live attachment is changed. Samuel-2872 is now identified with the 1824 West Fallowfield testator at 98% subjective confidence: his checked memorial names both wives Judith and Tabitha and the infant daughter Margaret Ellen, matching the original will. The newly inspected official deed index places Samuel in West Fallowfield and enters Judith Heslett in the spouse column in 1805 and 1812, with repeated Haslett dealings. These connect the already recorded Judith household to the later Tabitha estate. The will names the testator’s three brothers William, James and Robert Glasgow of Ireland; the anonymous Irish family recollection names those same three brothers with Samuel, who went to America, as children of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford. The distinctive sibling constellation and transatlantic division favour this particular Irish father over the current John reconstruction. The 98% testator identification does not prove his father. 67% is a combined subjective father-profile judgement, not a multiplication of independent probabilities. Repeated family names can occur in another generation. The memorial contributes a 1761 Pennsylvania birth and a John father attribution, but no underlying birth or Bible entry has been inspected. === Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2952]] is assessed at 8% (uncertain). The held March 1817 registration account lists James, age 1, with enslaved Mary under Amelia’s life ownership after John Glasgow’s death. The ownership list provides no biological fatherhood evidence; the selected tree attachment alone leaves only a very weak possibility; the c 1816 birth fits the 1817 age 1, but the handed-down tree is not independent support.

Whole selected father-profile proposition; maternity and upstream ancestry assessed separately.

Next useful test: Inspect the 1817 registration and John’s will for explicit parent or relationship language.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2952 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-2952]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-193]] is assessed at 91% (proved). Samuel Lyle is attached to James in the cited 1860 South Fork household and Faris p 84. His 1838 birth fits James's 1836 Lyle remarriage, giving a specific family sequence despite conflicting Virginia/Ohio birthplace statements.

Selected Glasgow-193 fatherhood of Glasgow-192; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare original 1860 household and Samuel's 1916 death parent fields.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-192 Birth - 1860 United States Federal Census for James Glasgow Iowa Wayne South Fork shows Virginia, but Source: Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p 84 shows Adams County, Ohio]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.

new_people.name: Thomas Glasgow of Quothquan, 1527/28
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
7 February 1527/28: Thomas Gleschow is listed with Quothquan tenants fined for nonappearance in a case concerning breach of the lord’s judicial prohibition (called his “fence” in the text). The heading says 1527; Dickinson’s Appendix B assigns the court to 1527/28.<ref>William Croft Dickinson (ed.), Court Book of the Barony of Carnwath 1523–1542 (1937), printed pp.64–65, index p.217; Appendix B p.cxx; PDF 193–194; https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/1271/7974/127179749.23.pdf#page=193. Printed edition inspected 15 October 2026; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

The remaining Thomas passages belong to five court meetings in all: 7 and 23 February 1527/28, 10 March 1527/28, 27 March 1528 and 20 May 1528. The February and 10 March meetings are entered twice. At the 27 March court Thomas is included in the tenant group adjudged to have broken two judicial prohibitions: cultivating Newmains while restricted and paying rents out despite an arrestment. Fines and imprisonment for a year at the lord’s will were decreed; actual imprisonment is not established. These proceedings name no Glasgow relative.<ref>Dickinson (1937), printed pp.64–70,79–88; Appendix B p.cxx; PDF193–199,208–217,125; https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/1271/7974/127179749.23.pdf#page=214. Printed edition inspected 15 October 2026; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The tenant list begins “in Quodquen” on p.64; Thomas Gleschow falls before the separate Carswell names on p.65. This supports Quothquan itself, not merely the broad barony. John and Thomas form a plausible local family group, with their degree of kinship unknown. [[Glasgow-1095|John Glasgow]] is the leading possible existing-profile comparison for the Quothquan John, not a proved identification or parent of Thomas.



The five meetings are treated as one tenant’s career. The rolls do not identify his exact individual holding or establish that he inherited from John. Leases and tenancy succession might identify kin. No compatible existing profile was found in the bounded duplicate audit; the Dublin 1725 and Calton 1886 Thomas accounts have incompatible chronologies.

Consolidate the five dated court meetings and repeated entries as one Quothquan tenant, not one person per page. A full sourced draft is supplied from the visually verified printed court book; John is a possible local relative with no chosen degree, and no descent to the seventeenth-century Quothquan weaver is asserted.

new_people.name: Sarah Glasgow, daughter of William of Currituck
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

Sarah Glasgow was a daughter of [[Glasgow-428|William Glasgow]] of Currituck, North Carolina. Her father named her in his will of 30 September 1746, proved 7 April 1747.<ref name="William1746">[https://www.ncgenweb.us/currituck/wills/glasgowwilliam1746.html William Glasgow will, 30 September 1746; proved 7 April 1747, North Carolina State Archives MARS 12.96.1.805; NCGenWeb published transcription checked 17 October 2026].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Her mother, exact dates and later identity remain unknown. The will names her paternal siblings Caleb, Abiah and Elizabeth; the identification of the adult Caleb profiles remains probable. The unnamed grandfather and the wife’s unborn child are not assigned modern identities. The contingent land interest and cattle in a mark given by an unnamed grandfather belong to Sarah’s bequest; the will does not name that grandfather. The account is based on the checked published transcription; the manuscript has not been newly inspected.

== Biography ==
Walter Glasgow was indexed as buried on 4 June 1647 in the Kirknewton/East Calder register, with residence Leithford and next of kin William Glasgow, relationship “Son to”. The original is not inspected; burial is not an exact death date.<ref>Findmypast/SGS, Walter Glasgow, burial 4 June 1647, Leithford; OPR 689/20; https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F1625437.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The burial precedes both proposed 23 September 1647/1649 baptism dates for Glasgow-1554. It cannot be assigned to that later-born/baptised child on the current chronology. Reuse of the name within one family is possible, but the adult father’s identity and relationship between the two Walters remain unproved.
Inspect OPR 689/20 for the burial and both baptism readings; verify any year heading or transcription error before treating the two Walters as proved siblings or creating a new person.

=== Preferred father and the two Walters — 17 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]] is the selected probable father, at 68% subjective confidence. The transcript’s explicit William father role is assessed at 98%; the same-father Leithford household comparison with the later [[Glasgow-1554|Walter]] is 84%. The 68% identification with the Mid Calder man is a separate, weaker inference; these figures are not independent probabilities. No mother is assigned.

The burial and later baptism name William and the exact Leithford residence, with the same register reference. The later baptism follows the burial under either disputed year, consistent with reuse of a dead child’s name. Another William of Leithford remains the principal alternative; William-3517 and William-1556 lack this local household chain, while the older Leith mealmaker William-3075 is weaker geographically, not excluded solely because he died before the burial.

The two Walters remain separate record accounts pending original-year verification. This source-verification HOLD remains in force; no live creation, merge, exact death date or infant age follows.<ref>Findmypast/SGS, Walter Glasgow burial, 4 June 1647, Leithford, OPR 689/20, https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F1625437; Walter Glasgow baptism indexed 23 September 1647, same residence/reference, https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473489. Maintained provider readings reused; originals not inspected in this review.</ref>

new_people.name: Alexander Elder
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html; . This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

The inspected original 1911 Gortereghy census return records Alexander Elder, aged 40, as head, Mary Elder, aged 44, as wife, Robert Elder, aged 34, as brother, and Margaret Elder, aged 25, as sister (Form A, official index house 37, nai001390156, rows 1–4). These stated relationships support comparison with the 1901 household, the 1908 marriage lead and the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial; identification with existing profiles remains qualified.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 Gortereghy return records Robert Elder, 65, widowed farmer, with Alex 27 and Robert 20 as sons and Eliza 22 and Margaretta 14 as daughters. The 1911 Alexander/Mary household explicitly records Robert as Alexander’s brother and Margaret as his sister. The combined names and locality strongly support continuity, with age differences retained. Robert [[Elder-7144]] remains a qualified father identity; Robert/Mary Glasgow’s Gortahar household is separate.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Robert Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298460.pdf; Form A; official index house 42; rows 1–5; 1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: The original 1901 Alex is explicitly Robert’s son; the 1911 return names brother Robert and sister Margaret. Together with the 1908 Alexander/Mary Anderson marriage extract, these support one sibling family. Retain the actual age differences. Use the same qualified Elder-7144 father hypothesis for Alexander and proved siblings; mother Jane on the memorial is separately evidenced, while Jane Calderwood remains a comparison. No matching Alexander profile was established in full same-name and father-filtered searches.

The same reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Neal Anderson, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, marrying Sarah Elder, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, on 28 September 1893. == Biography ==

The same 1911 Gortereghy browse lists two further Elder households not currently represented in the catalogue: Joseph Elder, aged 79, with Ellen Elder, aged 38, recorded as his niece, and William Elder, aged 40, with Elizabeth Elder, aged 50, recorded as his sister. This demonstrates that Gortereghy contained several distinct Elder households at the same time.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Joseph Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390154.pdf; Form A; official index/printed house 36; rows 1–2; 1911 Gortereghy, William Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390136.pdf; Form A; official index house 27; rows 1–2. Global near-age Elder-6578 belongs to a Utah family as a daughter of Claybourne and Mary Pratt, with a different family and locality.

new_people.name: Caroline McCaughern
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah [[Dysart-1893]], married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf; PDF page 1; entry 28. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: Caroline McCaughern/McCarnagh searches returned zero results. McCaughan returned only other given-name or later-generation variants, without a compatible Caroline born about 1864 and daughter of Sarah. No existing profile was identified within this explicit search scope. The original 1901/1911 returns establish the household’s continuity. Carry Dysart-1893 as the qualified mother identity and John McCaughern-23 as the corresponding uncertain father hypothesis for proved siblings. George’s particular mother remains unproved.

== Biography ==

A fresh audit of the surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription located a second parent-bearing McCaughern/Macaw household at the target townland. Hugh Macaw was born 3 February 1839 and baptised 3 March 1839 as the son of William and Mary Kilpatrick, resident at Lisnagaver (entry 125).<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 125 and 204; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; . The same register records Jane Matilda Macaw, born 26 July 1843 and baptised 14 January 1844, as the daughter of William and Mary Kilpatrick at Granagh (entry 204). Named transcription reread 30 September 2026; originalmanuscriptuninspected.</ref>

Rereading Rasharkin baptism transcription entry 125 gives Hugh Macaw’s birth as 3 February 1839, replacing the maintained 5 February wording. His baptism remains 3 March 1839; original manuscript inspection is required before treating the corrected transcription as a final date.<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; transcription entries 125 and 204; original MIC/1P/292 uninspected. Named transcription reread; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: No compatible infant profile was identified through Hugh Macaw/McCaw/McCaughan searches. McCaw-10 represents the father of John, born about 1833. McCaw-233 represents an adult born about 1812 and father of Eliza, born about 1832. These are older generations, not the 1839 infant. The freshly inspected published baptism transcription, row 125, gives birth on 3 February 1839 and baptism on 3 March, whereas the maintained handoff gave 5 February. The original image is still needed to settle the date. Consolidate Hugh and Jane Matilda with the same named parental couple. Rereading the transcription gives 3 February 1839, with the manuscript still uninspected. Parent profile identities remain uncertain; later spouses alone do not exclude an earlier family.

new_people.name: Nicholas Glasco / Glascoe
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Nicholas Glasco is named in a 20 June 1746 report in the ''Weekly Worcester Journal'' among officers in the rebel army committed to New Gaol, Southwark. The notice lists him between John Duncan and Alexander M'Laughlan. It gives no rank for Nicholas individually and does not state a conviction, birthplace, residence, relatives, occupation, or dates of birth or death.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214317653/ ''Weekly Worcester Journal'', 20 June 1746, p.4], original roster inspected 4 October 2026. Date follows provider metadata; masthead date has not been separately checked.</ref>


The 27 and 28 June reports describe Nicholas Glascoe as a self-styled major and allege a role in the attack on the Hazard sloop. These are allegations, not a finding of guilt.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394536822/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-06-27, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404059808/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-06-28, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

An August report lists Nicholas among persons indicted for high treason, while the 7 November paper announces the pending trial.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404060798/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-08-23, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394542827/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-11-07, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

The 8 and 17 November reports say he was acquitted, with defence evidence identifying him as a French native born at Saint-Germain-en-Laye and a lieutenant in Dillon’s Regiment. They report an order to detain him as a French prisoner. The Caledonian account also mentions a Not Guilty verdict and removal of his bolts; the saved excerpt stops before the full cartel articles. These reports require comparison with the underlying legal and military records.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404061824/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-11-08, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394462695/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

In May 1747 a notice names Mr Glascoe as major in Lord Ogilvy’s new regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate, but the missing forename and unproved continuity prevent a firm identification.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404076485/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1747-05-09, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

No parents, spouse, children, birth date, death date or Irish origin is established.

Further original issues preserve June rosters, indictment reprints and Dutch reports, along with acquittal reports containing translated cartel articles. These are related issue appearances; no independent family identity follows. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979338930/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury (The Sherborne Mercury, or Weekly Advertiser), 1746-06-30, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334222061/ S Gravenhaegse Courant, 1746-09-21, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979339079/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971385255/ The Gloucester Journal, 1746-11-18, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334158733/ Opregte Haarlemsche Courant, 1746-12-01, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

The Gloucester Journal of 28 April 1747 describes Major Glascoe as lately discharged at London and chief major in Lord Ogilvy’s projected regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate; no forename is given, and English pay is not interpreted as British military service.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971516263/ Gloucester Journal, 28 April 1747, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

The rare full name, Southwark proceedings and Hazard episode support a probable association across the 1746 reports. French birth and service are reported defence evidence. They do not establish an Irish origin, a Glasgow-family connection or relatives. The May 1747 appointment lacks a forename.

new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
George Glasgow appears among Royal Artillery colonels in June 1811.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050144942/ Freeman’s Journal, 10 June 1811, p. 4], original previously inspected on 4 October 2026.</ref> A War Office notice in September 1819 lists Major-General George Glasgow of the Royal Artillery among officers taking lieutenant-general rank by brevet.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050057308/ Freeman’s Journal, 6 September 1819, p. 4], original previously inspected on 4 October 2026.</ref>

John W. Spurr’s biography records his appointment as an artillery cadet on 2 April 1771, colonel in 1806, major-general in July 1811 and lieutenant-general in August 1819. It gives his death as 28 October 1820 in London and names his late wife Margaret Green.<ref>[https://www.biographi.ca/en/bio/glasgow_george_5E.html John W. Spurr, “GLASGOW, GEORGE,” Dictionary of Canadian Biography, vol. 5], full English entry read on 17 October 2026.</ref>

The likely burial entry for this officer records George Glasgow, aged 64, buried on 3 November 1820 at St Luke, Charlton by Greenwich, Kent. Two companion indexes supply the lieutenant-general title; Woolwich is recorded as residence. The age implies a birth about 1756, not an exact birthday. These are three index forms of one burial, and the original register has not been inspected.<ref>[https://findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FD%2F28050276&tab=this Findmypast GBPRS/D/28050276 — St Luke Charlton burial derivative transcript]; [https://findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=BMD%2FNBI%2F12413020 Findmypast BMD/NBI/12413020 — St Luke Charlton burial derivative transcript]; [https://findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FD%2F963049679%2F1&tab=this Findmypast GBPRS/D/963049679/1 — St Luke Charlton burial derivative transcript], derivative transcripts inspected 23 October 2026; probably the same officer by title, locality and chronology.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The full DCB entry, successfully read through urllib on 17 October, identifies a cadet appointed 2 April 1771, colonel from 24 July 1806, major-general from 4 July 1811, lieutenant-general in August 1819, died 28 October 1820. This joins the June 1811 colonel and September 1819 brevet notices. Actual candidate biographies exclude 1529 (baptised 1769, aged two at cadet appointment), 3611 (born 1777, died 1857) and 3345 (born 1792). Retain the documented 6 October fully paged George/variant duplicate audit; no compatible profile found. Earlier 1771 first-lieutenant evidence describes another officer and must not be conflated with this 1771 cadet.

The English DCB says London; its French search snippet says Charlton, Gloucestershire. Keep the exact death place qualified. The earlier 1771 first lieutenant is not this officer’s cadet appointment.

Burial on 3 November is distinct from death on 28 October. Charlton is the burial place; it does not resolve the retained London/Charlton death-place question.

new_people.name: Owen Glasco, Meath Repeal Association records, 1841–1843
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
On 10 March 1841, a Repeal Association entry reads “From Baddinstown, county Meath, per Mr. Owen Glasco, 1l.” and states that Mr. Glasco was admitted a member. On 25 February 1843, Owen Glasco appears among members “having each collected 20 Repealers”; the list ends with “Raddinstown County Meath.” The uncommon full name, association roles and Meath place context support probable continuity, but the 1843 list layout does not securely attach Raddinstown specifically to Owen. Retain the separate Baddinstown/Raddinstown readings; no modern place is identified. Neither notice proves birth, kinship or residence. “1l.” is £1; “20 Repealers” counts people collected, not money.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050131561/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1841-03-10, p.3]</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050126480/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1843-02-25, p.4]</ref>

== Research Notes ==

No compatible adult Meath Owen Glasco found in live Glasgow/Glasco searches. Actual Glass-5701 describes a Kentucky physician, Henderson censuses in 1840/1850 and Kentucky marriage in 1844, a strong conflicting life. Glass-5334 (born 1840) and Glasgow-1954 (born 1846) cannot be the 1841 adult. Retain one probable 1841/1843 documentary Owen; keep Baddinstown/Raddinstown readings separate and do not invent a residence or family.

new_people.name: Bessie Glasgow, Quothquan executrix
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''Bessie Glasgow''' lived at Quodquen, now Quothquan in Lanarkshire, in 1650. She was the lawful sister of [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow]], whose testament dative and inventory were confirmed at Lanark on 27 May 1650. The opening calls Bessie his lawful sister; the confirmation calls the deceased John her brother and identifies her as his executrix dative.<ref name="Quothquan1650">National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, confirmed 27 May 1650, CC14/5/5, register images 65–66; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search]. The sibling clauses and continuity of both images were visually checked in the maintained original-image review of 10 September 2026; the full opening and accounts are not yet completely transcribed.</ref><ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy, PDF p. 50]. The calendar confirms John's estate entry; the original supplies Bessie's relationship.</ref>

Bessie was alive at that confirmation and was born before 1650. No age, birthplace, death date, spouse or child has been established. Quothquan is her recorded residence, not an established birthplace or death place.<ref name="Quothquan1650" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Family and identity ===
The two sibling clauses support the record-defined John–Bessie relationship at '''99% subjective confidence'''; they belong to one testament, not two independent sources. Bessie's identity among existing profiles remains unresolved. Compatible candidates include [[Glasgow-3361|Bessie Glasgow of South Leith, indexed in 1616]], [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabeth Glasgow of Glasgow, baptised in 1616]], [[Glasgow-1092|Bessie Glasgow of Glasgow, indexed in 1623]] and [[Glasgow-1517|Elizabeth Glasgow of Glasgow, christened in 1625]]. No baptism or later household is assigned to this woman merely from the shared name.

[[Glasgow-1029|Stephen Glasgow]] is the selected uncertain father of Bessie's brother John, assessed at '''22% subjective probability'''. Extending that same paternal hypothesis to the documented sister gives Bessie a '''conditional 22%''' placement. Stephen's adult Glasgow life in 1575 and marriage to [[Graham-38221|Margaret Grahame]] in 1582 permit the proposed generation, but do not connect that household to the Quothquan siblings.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2189, printed p. 110, 17 June 1575, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n126/mode/2up digital copy]; vol. 8, protocol 2431, 25 June 1582, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto08glas/page/56/mode/2up digital copy]. These name Stephen's parents and spouse, respectively, not Bessie or the Quothquan John as his children.</ref> This placement is dependent on John's hypothesis and adds no independent evidence for Stephen's paternity. Bessie's mother remains unknown; Margaret Grahame is not thereby her mother. No candidate baptism profile's documented parentage is changed by this conditional model.

Bessie Glasgow must be distinguished from [[Robertson-33965|Bessie Robertson]], the deceased spouse of a John Glasgow in Montfoid whose testament was confirmed in 1610.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196].</ref> The Montfoid husband's identity with the Quothquan deceased is itself uncertain.

=== Existing-profile comparison ===

The checked candidates below are unselected. Sparse later lives are not exclusions.

{| class="wikitable"
! Candidate !! Evidence and disposition
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3361|Bessie Glasgow-3361]] || South Leith child indexed 25 February 1616, daughter of William Glasgow and Catherine Fraser; FamilySearch FQM4-VMQ. Age about 34 in 1650 is compatible. No later record in her biography excludes Quothquan. Retain as a compatible candidate; the different recorded father would displace the Stephen hypothesis if identity were established.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabeth Glasgow-1091]] || Glasgow baptism, 15 December 1616, Robert Glasgow/Jonet Conynghame; OPR 644/1, 10/208. Compatible age about 33; no later-life contradiction. Retain, without treating name or age as an identity bridge.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1092|Bessie Glasgow-1092]] || Glasgow index, 24 January 1623, Robert Glasgow/Jonet Cuninghame; OPR 644/1, 20/41. Compatible age about 27; no later-life contradiction. Retain.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1517|Elizabeth Glasgow-1517]] || Glasgow christening, 24 August 1625, Robert Glasgow/Jonet Cuninghame; OPR 644/1, 20/116. Compatible age about 24. Retain; the repeated names in this household do not by themselves prove earlier children died.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3144|Elizabeth Glasgow-3144]] || Approximate 1622 birth, later Virginia account and uncertain parents rest on a FamilySearch tree. No dated 1650 incompatible residence was established. Retain as a weaker candidate; do not exclude solely for the later Virginia place.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3961|Elizabeth Glasgow-3961]] || Adult household occurrence at Glenarm in 1669; PRONI T/307/A, transcription record 5730. The approximate 1650 birth is unsupported by an age statement and does not exclude adulthood in 1650. Retain as a weaker candidate; no Scotland–Antrim identity is asserted.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1155|Bessie Glasgow-1155]] || Inveresk index in March 1635; only about fifteen in May 1650. This strains the personal executor role and the proposed older sibling generation, but the combined birth/baptism index and absence of an inspected legal age clause do not justify a categorical exclusion. Retain as a substantially weaker candidate, without inventing an age cutoff.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1161|Elizabeth Glasgow-1161]] || Edinburgh child account dated 1 July 1647, Thomas Glasgow/Catharine Weir. An infant baptism would make her only about three when the executrix appeared, a concrete chronological conflict with personal estate administration. However, the combined index has no inspected age statement, so retain this as a very weak candidate pending the original rather than turn an assumed infant baptism into a categorical exclusion.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3915|Elizabeth Glasgow-3915]] || Already a widow occupying Easter Corswood in 1552, 98 years before the executrix's appearance. Exclude on the documented adult chronology, not her estimated 1525 birth.
|-

|-
 | [[Howie-1119|Bessie Howie-1119]], [[Whyte-2772|Bessie Whyte-2772]], [[Unknown-761582|Elizabeth Unknown-761582]] || Married-surname search results, respectively a sparse Howie account, the maternal account associated with the 1651 Heleene Glasgow baptism, and the Elizabeth associated with Archibald Glasgow's 1673 Donegal will. None supplies a Glasgow birth surname or the Quothquan brother. They are weak unselected surname/household leads, not established contradictions or selected identities.

new_people.name: John Glasgow/Glasco, Prescott watchmaker
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
Reviewed: 2026-10-18. The documents establish a John Glasgow/Glasco of Prescott, watchmaker, as the brother-beneficiary named in Robert Glasgow's will and the grantor in B13. His identification with any existing John Glasgow profile is unresolved. Retain all six checked comparisons; none is selected or excluded by migration alone.

== Profile fields and identity hold ==

* First name: John; last name at birth: Glasgow (record spelling varies Glasgow/Glasco); male.
* Birth and death: unknown. The first known dated appearance is the will of 9 October 1849; this is not a birth-year estimate. Alive and conveying land on 30 October 1856.
* Birthplace and death place: unknown. Recorded residence: Prescott, Canada West (now Ontario), in 1856. Occupation in B13: watchmaker.
* Wife: Jane, releasing dower in B13; surname and further identity unknown.
* Brother: [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], identified by the will and matched deed share.

=== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''', also recorded as John Glasco, was a brother of [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], Canada West. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives one sixth of his estate to his brother John. The same will names brothers Daniel, Samuel and Thomas, sister Mary, and the children of brother James as beneficiaries.<ref name="will">Robert Glasgow of Prescott, will dated 9 October 1849, registered 13 November 1856, Prescott land registry, volume B, instrument B12, printed pp. 9–10, images 35–36; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S FamilySearch image 35], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 image 36]. The original clauses and date line were visually inspected 18 October 2026.</ref>

On 30 October 1856, John Glasgow/Glasco of Prescott, described as a watchmaker, and his wife Jane conveyed their one-sixth interest to Samuel Glasgow, Prescott merchant, for £125. Jane released her dower interest. The conveyance covers Town Lot 12 on the south side of Dibble Street and part of Lot 11, a 3,400-square-foot strip. The deed was registered 13 November 1856.<ref name="b13">Indenture B13, dated 30 October 1856, registered 13 November 1856, Prescott land registry, volume B, printed pp. 10–11, image 36; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 FamilySearch image 36]. Original instrument visually inspected 18 October 2026.</ref>

The records establish his Prescott residence and watchmaking occupation by 1856. They do not establish his birth date or place, death, parents, or Jane's surname.

== Research Notes ==

The identification of the will's brother-beneficiary with B13's grantor is '''strongly supported (98% subjective confidence)''': the deed transfers exactly the one-sixth share allocated to John in the will, in the same Prescott property, seven years later. The will's registration request was witnessed by Alexander Glasgow; his role was witness, not beneficiary.<ref name="will" /><ref name="b13" />

[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow-3904]] is the same tentative father hypothesis used for the related Prescott brothers Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert. Extending that existing hypothesis to John is assessed at '''27%''', uncertain. It is not independent support for Alexander's paternity and must not raise the existing estimate. No mother is inferred. The will names no parents.

No existing John profile is selected. All six comparisons above remain open because an earlier or later residence elsewhere does not establish incompatible identity for a possible migrant. Further linking evidence could come from Canadian vital, religious, occupational or property records connecting a candidate's spouse/household to Jane and the Prescott share.

The 2007 online discussion supplies the derivative tradition naming Alexander and Rosanna as Thomas Glasgow’s parents, not a newly inspected record; it is retained as context only and does not establish this identity.<ref>“Glasgow Family,” Genes Reunited discussion board, 2007, https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 (prior review reused; not freshly inspected for this draft).</ref>

== Sources ==

<references />
new_people.assessment: John Glasgow, Prescott watchmaker with wife Jane in deed B13, is selected as Robert Glasgow-4150’s brother at 98% subjective confidence. Robert’s 1849 will gives brother John one sixth. John and Jane’s 1856 deed transfers an undivided one sixth of the same Dibble Street lots to Samuel, who is another will-named brother. The exact locality, buyer, parcels and fraction identify the grantor strongly; B13 does not itself expressly call John Robert’s brother. John’s birth, death and parents are not named, and his identity with an existing John profile is unresolved. Extend the existing Alexander Glasgow-3904 father hypothesis to John and Mary at 27%, uncertain, conditional on their documented membership in the Prescott sibling family. Thomas-987 and Daniel-3896 already carry this father, and Samuel-4010 and Robert-4150 already have the same selected uncertain hypothesis. Its basis remains the single late descendant tradition naming Alexander as Thomas’s father, with compatible generation and sibling inference. The original will and deeds name no parent. These two extensions supply no independent parent testimony and do not raise the existing estimate; no mother is selected. These are two previously unstructured record accounts recovered from evidence already researched in September, not two newly discovered sources or two proven additional distinct people. John retains six unselected compatible or weak existing-profile comparisons; later residence, spouse or death elsewhere is not by itself an exclusion of a possible migrant. No Mary Black/Glasgow match is established in the bounded local historical catalogue check. Both accounts remain on identity hold before any new WikiTree profile creation. Record dates are not birth dates. [Prescott family comparison](/branches/lisnagaver-rasharkin/#chapter-prescott-john-mary-siblings).

new_people.name: Mary Black, formerly Glasgow, sister of Robert of Prescott
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
Reviewed: 2026-10-18. Robert Glasgow's will names his sister Mary as a beneficiary; deed C298 identifies Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow, as Robert's sister and identifies her six children. The identity among existing profiles is unresolved. Do not invent a forename for her husband or treat “Mr Black” as a separate structured person.

== Profile fields and identity hold ==

* First name: Mary; last name at birth: Glasgow; married name Black; female.
* Birth and death: unknown. First dated record in this account: Robert's will, 9 October 1849. No death for Mary is established; she was represented through her children in C298, dated 15 September 1869.
* Birthplace and death place: unknown. Places associated with her children in C298 include Drumoolish, County Londonderry; Newburgh, Orange County, New York; and Legrand, Marshall County, Iowa. These are not Mary's own residence or birthplaces.
* Spouse: a Black, forename unknown. The record does not name him as a grantor or establish his identity.
* Brother: [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], expressly identified by the will and C298.

== Existing-profile comparison ==

No established Mary Black, formerly Glasgow, match was found in the local historical catalogue. The bounded review found only an unrelated false positive, Anna Mary (Stever) Glasgow, whose spouse was Samuel Black Glasgow. This was a local catalogue check, not an exhaustive worldwide search. No candidate is selected or definitively excluded.

== Biography ==

'''Mary Glasgow''' was the sister of [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], Canada West. In his will dated 9 October 1849, Robert gives one sixth of his estate to his sister Mary and a separate one sixth collectively to the children of his brother James.<ref name="will">Robert Glasgow of Prescott, will dated 9 October 1849, registered 13 November 1856, Prescott land registry, volume B, instrument B12, printed pp. 9–10, images 35–36; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S FamilySearch image 35], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 image 36]. Original clauses and date line visually inspected 18 October 2026.</ref>

A deed dated 15 September 1869 identifies her as “Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow,” sister of the late Robert Glasgow of Prescott. Registered on 1 July 1870, C298 conveys the shares of her six children to Mary Eno Glasgow, widow of Samuel Glasgow of Prescott, for $800. The deed expressly traces the children's interests to Robert's will: each had one sixth of Mary's one-sixth share. The property was Town Lot 12 and part of Lot 11 on the south side of Dibble Street in Prescott.<ref name="c298">Grant and quitclaim C298, dated 15 September 1869, registered 1 July 1870, Prescott land registry, volume C, pp. 477–482, images 277–280; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K FamilySearch image 277], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQT5-R image 278], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTP-M image 279], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQT2-C image 280]. The relationship clause on printed p. 477 was visually reread 18 October 2026; later execution details reuse the maintained original inspection of 13 September 2026.</ref>

The six children named in C298 are:

* John Black, yeoman of Drumoolish, County Londonderry, Ireland; his wife Martha Black also joined the conveyance to release dower.
* Rose Ann Black, spinster of Drumoolish.
* Jane Miller of Newburgh, Orange County, New York; her husband Robert Miller, yeoman, joined.
* Agnes Black, spinster of Newburgh.
* Thomasina Montgomery of Legrand, Marshall County, Iowa; her husband Mathew Montgomery, yeoman, joined.
* Elizabeth Black, formerly of Newburgh, spinster, deceased unmarried and intestate. The deed calls the five living children her lawful brother, sisters and heirs. They conveyed her inherited share along with their own.

The deed records execution in stages: John, Rose Ann and Martha at Coleraine on 27 November 1869; Jane Miller and Thomasina Montgomery at Newburgh on 29 April 1870; and Agnes's separate attestation at Coleraine, sworn 4 June 1870. These are execution places and dates, not Mary's residence. Rose Ann signed by mark in the registered copy.<ref name="c298" />

No source cited here establishes Mary's birth or death, her husband's forename, or the identity of her parents beyond the documented sibling relationship to Robert.

== Research Notes ==

Mary's relationship as sister of Robert is '''proved (99%)''' by the direct statement in C298; Robert's 1849 will independently names a sister Mary, and C298 also traces the children's six shares to that will. The documents establish one consistent record-defined relationship, not a proven match to any existing Mary Glasgow profile.<ref name="will" /><ref name="c298" />

[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow-3904]] is the tentative father hypothesis already applied to the related Prescott brothers Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert. Extending that same hypothesis to their documented sister Mary is assessed at '''27%''', uncertain. This adds no independent support for the father's identity and does not change the existing estimate. Her mother remains unknown; the records do not name either parent.

The local historical catalogue check did not identify an established Mary Black/Glasgow profile. It was not a comprehensive search of all WikiTree profiles or records. Further work could compare Irish and North American records for the named children, while keeping each child's stated residence distinct from Mary's unknown residence.

The 2007 online discussion supplies the derivative tradition naming Alexander and Rosanna as Thomas Glasgow’s parents, not a newly inspected original; it is retained only as context and does not establish Mary's identity.<ref>“Glasgow Family,” Genes Reunited discussion board, 2007, https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 (prior review reused; not freshly inspected for this draft).</ref>

== Sources ==

John’s wife Martha, Jane’s husband Robert Miller and Thomasina’s husband Mathew Montgomery also joined. == Biography ==
'''Janet Broun''' was resident in Dalziel, Lanarkshire, Scotland, when marriage banns named her with Samuel Glasgow, also resident in Dalziel, on 23 June 1716. The transcript gives marriage year 1716 but no separate ceremony date.<ref name="Dalziel1716">Church of Scotland, Dalziel, Old Parish Registers, OPR 639/1, item 2, p.71, range 1648–1819; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FMAR%2F1215123%2F1 Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Marriages & Banns 1561–1893], Samuel Glasgow and Janet Broun, banns 23 June 1716. Transcript inspected 18 October 2026; original register uninspected.</ref>

The groom is probably [[Glasgow-3166|Samuel Glasgow]], the father named in the baptism index for [[Glasgow-3523|James Glasgow]] at Dalziel on 15 March 1719. Their shared parish, full name and close dates support one household. This identification is assessed at 88% subjective confidence; the banns do not establish that a wedding took place.<ref name="Dalziel1716" /><ref>Dalziel Parish, Church of Scotland, Old Parish Registers Births and Baptisms, parish 639, Ref 10/28; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLJ-PML FamilySearch, Scotland Births and Baptisms], James Glasgow, 1719; maintained index citation, original not newly inspected.</ref>

Her birth, death and parents are unknown. Broun is her recorded surname; the transcript does not establish her last name at birth or whether she had previously married. Brown is a spelling to test, not an additional recorded form in this transcript.

== Research Notes ==
Janet is a possible maternal lead for James, but no mother is assigned from the banns alone. Samuel's own parentage is unresolved. The proposed later Cambusnethan connection remains at 41% and is not strengthened by a new parent clause here.

Identity remains on '''HOLD''' before profile creation. A bounded anonymous WikiTree search on 18 October 2026 used FirstName Janet, LastName Broun and BirthDate 1685, returning 93 fuzzy matches on one page; this was not an exhaustive worldwide search. The nine Open, non-living exact-Janet Brown/Burn results were inspected with their biographies and spouse context. A local historical catalogue check for Janet/Jonet/Jennet/Jean/Jane Brown/Broun found no established match. Missing fields are not exclusions.

* [[Brown-4507|Janet Brown]] — Unresolved low-information comparison: Janet Brown, undated wife of William Leishman; the empty biography gives no chronology or locality conflict. No positive Dalziel identification.
* [[Brown-4583|Janet Brown]] — Unresolved low-information comparison: Janet Brown, no dates or family in the retrieved biography. No positive Dalziel identification; missing fields do not exclude her.
* [[Brown-18629|Janet Brown]] — Unresolved low-information comparison: Janet Brown, undated spouse of Sinclair-1202. No positive Dalziel identification or concrete conflict established.
* [[Brown-206625|Janet Brown]] — Exceptionally weak comparison: Aberdeen marriage in 1770 and death in 1828 would require an extraordinary lifespan for an adult in 1716. Retained conditionally because no birth is supplied; not a selected identity.

[[Brown-98967]] represents a documented overlapping Prestonpans Manners household; [[Brown-52254]] has a recorded 1711 death. They are opposed by positive conflicting evidence, not rejected for absent fields. Other returned profiles belong to substantially later households. The original Dalziel entries and the undated candidate families should be compared before creating or merging a profile.
